memories.summary: Divi 5's styling uses a variable-first approach (Variables > Presets > Custom CSS).
memories.solution:
The Divi 5 styling system operates on three levels: Design Variables for reusable values, Option Group/Element Presets for reusable style collections, and Custom CSS for edge cases. Key principle: Use variables for consistency; use presets for component styles; use custom CSS only when the UI cannot handle it.

**Design Variable Types:** Divi 5 supports six variable types, each mapping to specific outputs:
*   **Color:** Affects `color`, `background-color`, `border-color`, `fill`, `box-shadow` color.
*   **Font:** Affects `font-family`.
*   **Number:** Affects `font-size`, `padding`, `margin`, `border-radius`, `width`, `height`, `gap`. (Includes unit and supports CSS functions like `clamp()`).
*   **Image:** Affects `background-image`, `content` url, `src` attribute.
*   **Link:** Affects `href` attribute values (not CSS).
*   **Text:** Affects text content, `aria-label`, `title` attributes (not CSS).

**Variable Resolution & Output:** When a variable is assigned to a field, Divi resolves the **actual value** at render time and writes it into the element's CSS output. The variable reference never appears in the rendered stylesheet.
*   Example: A variable set to `60px` results in `.et_pb_section_0 { padding-top: 60px; }`, not `padding-top: var(--section-padding);`.

**Variable Limitations:**
1.  You cannot target or override a design variable's value using CSS custom properties (`var()`) because the browser only sees the resolved static value.
2.  Custom CSS fields cannot reference design variables by name.
3.  DevTools shows the resolved value, not a variable reference, and `getComputedStyle()` cannot identify the source variable.

**Cascade:** The hierarchy is: Variables (raw values) $\rightarrow$ Presets (style collections using variables) $\rightarrow$ Elements (using presets). Changing a Variable updates all dependent Presets and Elements site-wide.

**CSS Output Patterns:**
*   **Color:** Applied to backgrounds, it generates properties like `background-color`, `color`, etc., depending on the field.
*   **Number:** The unit is included in the output (e.g., `padding-top: 60px;`). CSS functions are output as-is (e.g., `font-size: clamp(24px, 4vw, 48px);`).
*   **Font:** Generates `font-family` (e.g., `font-family: 'Montserrat', sans-serif;`).

memories.summary: HSL offsets allow generating harmonious and functional derived colors.
memories.solution:
Relative color relationships can be defined using HSL offsets:

**Color Harmonies (Hue Shifts):**
*   Complementary: Hue +180° (Opposite on the color wheel)
*   Analogous warm: Hue +30° (Adjacent warm color)
*   Analogous cool: Hue -30° (Adjacent cool color)
*   Triadic: Hue +120° or -120° (One third around the wheel)
*   Split complementary: Hue +150° or +210° (Near-complementary pair)

**Desaturation/Toning:**
*   Muted variant: Saturation -30% (For secondary use)
*   Greyscale hint: Saturation -60% (Nearly grey with a color hint)
*   Neutral from color: Saturation -80%, Lightness +20% (Warm/cool grey derived from brand)

**Opacity Washes:**
*   Image overlay: Opacity 70-80% (Reduce to 20-30%) (Color wash over hero images)
*   Subtle tint: Opacity 90-95% (Reduce to 5-10%) (Barely visible color layer)
*   Glass effect: Opacity 60-70% (Reduce to 30-40%) (Semi-transparent surface)

**Contrast & Accessibility:**
*   WCAG AA normal text requires a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
*   WCAG AA large text requires a 3:1 contrast ratio.
*   WCAG AAA normal text requires a 7:1 contrast ratio.
*   When deriving colors, verify that lightness offsets maintain sufficient contrast (e.g., for AA on white, a base lightness of 50% needs no offset; a base lightness of 30% needs Lightness +40% or more).

**Variable Efficiency:** Using relative color offsets allows generating multiple derived colors from a minimal set of variables (e.g., 5 variables can yield 10+ usable colors).

memories.summary: Determine if a color relationship requires relative or separate variables.
memories.solution:
**Use Relative Colors When:**
*   The derived color must automatically track changes in the base color (e.g., hover state of a button).
*   The color needs to shift when the brand's primary color changes (e.g., light background from brand color).
**Use Separate Variables When:**
*   The colors have fixed, independent meanings (e.g., warning/error/success status colors).
*   The two brand colors are chosen independently and have no mathematical relationship.
**Rule of Thumb:** If changing the base color should automatically change the derived color, use a relative color. Otherwise, use separate variables.

memories.summary: Technical details for implementing and testing relative color data.
memories.solution:
**Data Storage (Needs Testing):** Relative color data is likely stored as a compound object in the element's attributes: a reference to the base color (static value or variable ID) plus HSL and opacity offset values. The format may be `{base_color, hue_offset, saturation_offset, lightness_offset, opacity_offset}`.

**Programmatic Access (Needs Testing):**
*   Read derived color: Inspect Layout JSON for objects containing base + offset fields.
*   Read resolved value: Render the page and inspect CSS output.
*   Modify base color: Update the variable or static value; all derived colors recalculate on next render.
*   Modify offsets: Update the offset values in the element's attributes, preserving the base reference.

**Platform Notes:** The HSL-native color model and Color Filters drawer are features introduced in Divi 5. Divi 4 supported hex/RGB but lacked relative color offset functionality.

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure
memories.solution:
How Divi 5’s **Divi Library** and **Design System** import/export JSON files are structured. This is reverse‑engineered from the [Divi 5 Launch Design System](https://www.elegantthemes.com/blog/divi-resources/divi-5-launch-gift-design-system) ZIP and applies to imports via **Divi > Divi Library > Import & Export**, **Theme Builder**, and **Theme Customizer**.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What this documents:** The root `context`, top-level keys, and main data shapes for each import file type.
    **File types:** Global Variables | Presets | Theme Builder Templates | Theme Customizer | Layouts (pages, sections, premade).
    **Last verified:** 2026-03-17 (Design System ZIP); 2026-04-30 (library `terms` taxonomies — see [Document changelog](#document-changelog))

---

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > Overview
memories.solution:
Each import file is a **single JSON object** with a **`context`** field that tells Divi which importer to use:

| Context | File purpose | Import location |
|--------|--------------|-----------------|
| `et_builder` | Global Variables, Presets (and optionally embedded colors/variables) | Divi Library > Import & Export |
| `et_builder_layouts` | Pages, sections, premade layouts | Divi Library > Import & Export |
| `et_theme_builder` | Theme Builder templates + embedded layouts | Theme Builder > ↑↓ |
| `et_divi_mods` | Theme Customizer settings | Theme Customizer > ↑↓ |

The same root object often includes **shared trailing keys** (`global_colors`, `global_variables`, `canvases`, `images`, `thumbnails`) for portability; import may use only the key(s) relevant to that context.

---

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 1. Global Variables (`context: "et_builder"`)
memories.solution:
**File example:** `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Global-Variables.json`

**Root shape:**

```json
{
  "context": "et_builder",
  "data": [],
  "presets": [],
  "global_colors": [ ["id", { "color", "status", "label" } ], ... ],
  "global_variables": [ { "id", "label", "value", "order", "status", "lastUpdated", "variableType", "type" }, ... ],
  "canvases": [],
  "images": [],
  "thumbnails": []
}
```

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 1. Global Variables (`context: "et_builder"`) > `global_colors`
memories.solution:
Array of **tuples** `[ id, definition ]`:

- **id:** string, e.g. `gcid-primary-color`, `gcid-s0kqi6v11w`
- **definition:** object
  - `color` — hex, rgba, or `$variable(...)$` reference
  - `status` — `"active"` | `"inactive"`
  - `label` — display name

Colors can reference other global colors via the **variable syntax** (see [Variable reference format](#variable-reference-format) below).

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 1. Global Variables (`context: "et_builder"`) > `global_variables`
memories.solution:
Array of **variable objects**. Each has:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|--------|
| `id` | string | e.g. `gvid-3ycvkww27b`, `gcid-primary-color` |
| `label` | string | Display name |
| `value` | string | e.g. `"16px"`, `"clamp(24px, 6vw, 90px)"`, `"#2176ff"`, `"Inter"` |
| `order` | string | Sort order (can be `""`) |
| `status` | string | `"active"` \| `"archived"` |
| `lastUpdated` | string | ISO 8601 |
| `variableType` | string | Same as `type` |
| `type` | string | `"numbers"` \| `"strings"` \| `"colors"` \| `"fonts"` \| `"images"` \| `"links"` |
| `groupKey` | string | *(optional)* e.g. `"colors"`, `"fonts"` |

**Variable types in the design system:**

- **numbers** — spacing, font sizes, border radius, line height, max-widths (e.g. `"60px"`, `"clamp(...)"`)
- **strings** — CTAs, company name, address, phone, email, URLs
- **colors** — same IDs as `global_colors`; value can be hex/rgba or `$variable(...)$`
- **fonts** — e.g. `"--et_global_heading_font"`, `"Inter"`
- **images** — base64 data URLs or URLs
- **links** — URL strings

Import this file with **“Import Global Variables”** checked in the Library import dialog.

---

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 2. Presets (`context: "et_builder"`)
memories.solution:
**File example:** `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Presets.json`

**Root shape:**

```json
{
  "context": "et_builder",
  "data": [],
  "presets": {
    "module": { "divi/heading": { "default", "items" }, "divi/row": { ... }, ... },
    "group": { "divi/button": { ... }, "divi/font": { ... }, "divi/spacing": { ... }, ... }
  },
  "global_colors": [ ... ],
  "global_variables": [ ... ],
  "canvases": [],
  "images": [],
  "thumbnails": []
}
```

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 2. Presets (`context: "et_builder"`) > `presets.module`
memories.solution:
Keyed by **module slug** (e.g. `divi/heading`, `divi/row`, `divi/section`, `divi/column`, `divi/text`, `divi/button`, `divi/contact-form`, `divi/signup`). Each value:

- `default` — id of the default preset for that module
- `items` — object of preset id → **preset object**

**Module preset object** (per item):

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` | Unique preset id (e.g. `vruk2g8yjw`) |
| `name` | Display name (e.g. `"Heading Preset 1"`, `"Subheading"`) |
| `moduleName` | Module slug (e.g. `divi/heading`) |
| `version` | Builder version (e.g. `5.0.0-public-beta.3`) |
| `type` | `"module"` |
| `created` | Timestamp (ms) |
| `updated` | Timestamp (ms) |
| `attrs` | *(optional)* Partial module attributes (e.g. `title.decoration.font`, `css`) — can reference `$variable(...)$` |
| `renderAttrs` | *(optional)* Serialized render attributes |

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 2. Presets (`context: "et_builder"`) > `presets.group`
memories.solution:
**Option group presets** (shared across modules). Keys are group names, e.g.:

- `divi/button`, `divi/font`, `divi/font-header`, `divi/font-body`
- `divi/border`, `divi/box-shadow`, `divi/spacing`, `divi/background`
- `divi/layout`, `divi/text`, `divi/sizing`, `divi/filters`

Structure is analogous to `module`: `default` + `items` (id → preset object). Layouts reference these via `groupPreset` (e.g. `module.decoration.spacing` → `presetId` + `groupName`).

Import with **“Import Presets”** checked.

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`)
internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > Taxonomy reference (`terms`)
memories.solution:
Each library layout in `data` should include a **`terms`** array with **WordPress term-shaped objects**. Divi 5 uses (at least) **three custom taxonomies** on `et_pb_layout` posts. For a **full page layout** that must appear under **Visual Builder → Add Layout → Saved Layout**, all three must be present with compatible slugs.

Official import **context** naming for library exports is documented by Elegant Themes (e.g. [`et_builder_layouts`](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/2612617-how-to-fix-the-this-file-should-not-be-imported-in-this-context-error-when-importing-a-json-file-in-divi)).

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > `post_meta` layout flags
memories.solution:
| Key | Example | Meaning |
|-----|---------|--------|
| `_et_pb_predefined_layout` | `"off"` | User-created / imported layout (not a bundled premade) |
| `_et_pb_predefined_layout` | `"on"` | Bundled or predefined layout treatment (see also [Global Elements](../builder/global-elements.md)) |

Setting `_et_pb_predefined_layout` to `"off"` for custom imports matches typical exported user layouts and avoids treating the item like a premade package layout.

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > Layout post object
memories.solution:
Each value in `data` is a **WP post-like object**:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `ID` | Post ID (numeric) |
| `post_date`, `post_date_gmt` | |
| `post_content` | **Block markup** — `<!-- wp:divi/placeholder --><!-- wp:divi/section ... -->` … (see [Block Comment Format](block-format.md)) |
| `post_title` | |
| `post_excerpt` | |
| `post_status`, `comment_status`, `ping_status`, `post_password` | |
| `post_name` | Slug |
| `post_modified`, `post_modified_gmt` | |
| `post_content_filtered` | |
| `post_parent`, `menu_order` | |
| `post_type` | e.g. `et_pb_layout` |
| `post_mime_type`, `comment_count`, `filter` | |
| `post_meta` | Key/value meta (see [`_et_pb_predefined_layout`](#post_meta-layout-flags)) |
| `terms` | Taxonomy terms — **required** for correct Visual Builder library pickers; see [Taxonomy reference (`terms`)](#taxonomy-reference-terms) |

Layout content lives in **`post_content`**: Gutenberg-style block comments (`wp:divi/section`, `wp:divi/row`, `wp:divi/column`, `wp:divi/heading`, etc.) with JSON attributes. Attributes can include:

- `module` — module settings (meta, decoration, sizing, etc.)
- `builderVersion`
- `modulePreset` — array of preset ids (e.g. `["vk5yn8ek75"]`)
- `groupPreset` — e.g. `{ "module.decoration.spacing": { "presetId": ["sjv7gwfcxt"], "groupName": "divi/spacing" } }`

Import via **Divi Library > Import & Export**; choose the appropriate layout type (pages, sections, etc.).

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > Taxonomy reference (`terms`) > 1. `layout_type`
memories.solution:
Classifies what kind of library item this is (page layout vs section vs row vs module). The **slug must match how the Visual Builder filters the “Load from Library” / “Saved Layout” lists** for each entry point — not the English label you might expect (see [Common pitfalls](#common-pitfalls-library-json-imports)).

| Slug | Typical meaning | Verification |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| `layout` | Full page layout (appears in **Add Layout → Saved Layout**) | Verified on Divi 5 (community testing, Nov 2025; doc update Apr 2026) |
| `section` | Saved section | **Not verified in this doc revision** — export a saved section from **Divi → Divi Library** and inspect `terms` |
| `row` | Saved row | **Not verified in this doc revision** — export a saved row and inspect `terms` |
| `module` | Saved module | **Not verified in this doc revision** — export a saved module and inspect `terms` |

The **display name** (`name`) in JSON often mirrors the admin “Type” column (e.g. `"Layout"`, `"Section"`). The **`slug`** is what must be correct for the builder UI.

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > Taxonomy reference (`terms`) > 2. `scope`
memories.solution:
Whether the item behaves as an ordinary library item or a **global** (site-wide) one.

| Slug | Typical meaning | Verification |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| `not_global` | Regular library item | Verified for non-global full page layouts (community testing, Nov 2025) |
| `global` | Global library item | **Not verified in this doc revision** — export a known global element and inspect `terms` |

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > Taxonomy reference (`terms`) > 3. `module_width`
memories.solution:
For section-level items, distinguishes **regular** sections from **specialty** sections in Divi’s internal classification.

| Slug | Typical meaning | Verification |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| `regular` | Standard (non-specialty) | Verified for typical full page layouts (community testing, Nov 2025) |
| `specialty` | Specialty section layout | **Not verified in this doc revision** — export a specialty section if applicable |

Each term object generally includes: `name`, `slug`, `taxonomy`, `term_group`, `term_taxonomy_id`, `description`, `parent`, `count`, `filter` — mirroring what Divi writes when **exporting** a layout. Placeholder zeros in export files are normal; Divi assigns real IDs on import.

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > Visual Builder entry points filter by `layout_type`
memories.solution:
There is **no single “generic” library item** that appears in every “Add from Library” picker. The Visual Builder **filters saved library items by the user’s entry point**:

| User action | Picker | Expect `layout_type` slug |
|-------------|--------|---------------------------|
| **Add Layout** (page) | Saved Layout | `layout` |
| **Add Section** | Add From Library | `section` |
| **Add Row** | Add From Library | `row` |
| **Add Module** | Add From Library | `module` |

If you generate `et_builder_layouts` JSON programmatically, **`layout_type` must match the workflow** your users will use. Correct `post_content` alone is not enough if the taxonomies disagree.

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > Minimal `terms` example (full page layout)
memories.solution:
Verified combination for a **non-global, regular** full page layout that surfaces under **Add Layout → Saved Layout**:

```json
"terms": [
  {
    "name": "Layout",
    "slug": "layout",
    "term_group": 0,
    "term_taxonomy_id": 0,
    "taxonomy": "layout_type",
    "description": "",
    "parent": 0,
    "count": 1,
    "filter": "raw"
  },
  {
    "name": "Not Global",
    "slug": "not_global",
    "term_group": 0,
    "term_taxonomy_id": 0,
    "taxonomy": "scope",
    "description": "",
    "parent": 0,
    "count": 1,
    "filter": "raw"
  },
  {
    "name": "Regular",
    "slug": "regular",
    "term_group": 0,
    "term_taxonomy_id": 0,
    "taxonomy": "module_width",
    "description": "",
    "parent": 0,
    "count": 1,
    "filter": "raw"
  }
]
```

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > Verifying taxonomy slugs before you rely on them
memories.solution:
This page **does not** substitute for inspecting a real export on your Divi version:

1. In Divi 5, save a library item of the type you care about (section, row, module, global, specialty section, etc.).
2. **Export** it from **Divi → Divi Library** (or the same portability flow you use for production JSON).
3. Open the JSON and copy the `terms` array from the matching `data` entry.

If a slug in the tables above differs from your export, **trust your export** and consider opening a PR to update this doc.

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > 5. Layouts — Pages, Sections, Premade (`context: "et_builder_layouts"`) > Common pitfalls: library JSON imports
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Silent failure: import succeeds but the layout never appears in the Visual Builder"
    **Symptom:** JSON imports without error; the item appears in **WP Admin → Divi → Divi Library**, but it **does not** appear in the Visual Builder picker (e.g. **Add Layout → Saved Layout**).

    **Cause:** Wrong or incomplete **`terms`** — especially **`layout_type`** — so the admin list and the builder filters disagree.

    **`slug: "page"` on `layout_type`:** The word “page” feels semantically right for a full page layout, but it is **not** the slug the builder uses for the Saved Layout list. **`layout_type` must use `slug: "layout"`** for that entry point (verified Nov 2025). Replacing `page` with `layout` fixed the issue with no other JSON changes.

    **Remediation:** Use the [minimal `terms` example](#minimal-terms-example-full-page-layout) as a baseline for full page layouts; for other item types, **export a known-good item** and mirror its `terms`.

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > Root schema quick reference
memories.solution:
Compact view of required root keys per context. Optional or often-empty keys (`canvases`, `images`, `thumbnails`) omitted.

**`et_builder`** (Global Variables and/or Presets):

```text
context: "et_builder"
data: []
presets: [] | { module?: { [moduleSlug]: { default, items } }, group?: { [groupName]: { default, items } } }
global_colors: [ [id, { color, status, label } ], ... ]
global_variables: [ { id, label, value, order, status, lastUpdated, variableType, type, groupKey? }, ... ]
```

**`et_builder_layouts`** (pages, sections, premade):

```text
context: "et_builder_layouts"
data: { [postId]: { ID, post_content, post_title, post_type, post_meta, terms, ... } }
```

**`et_theme_builder`**:

```text
context: "et_theme_builder"
templates: [ { title, default, enabled, use_on, exclude_from, layouts: { header, body, footer }, description }, ... ]
layouts: { [layoutId]: { context, data, post_title, post_type, theme_builder, global_colors, post_meta, ... } }
presets?: {}
global_colors?: []
global_variables?: []
has_default_template?: boolean
has_global_layouts?: boolean
```

**`et_divi_mods`** (Theme Customizer):

```text
context: "et_divi_mods"
data: { body_font_size, heading_font, body_font, header_color, font_color, link_color, accent_color, ... }
```

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > Step-by-step: Importing the Design System
memories.solution:
Use this order on a **clean Divi 5 site** to avoid conflicts and missing variable references.

1. **Download and extract** the Design System ZIP (e.g. from the [Divi 5 Launch Gift](https://www.elegantthemes.com/blog/divi-resources/divi-5-launch-gift-design-system) post).
2. **Divi → Divi Library → Import & Export**
   - **Import Presets:** Choose `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Presets.json`, ensure **Import Presets** is checked, import.
   - **Import Global Variables:** Choose `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Global-Variables.json`, ensure **Import Global Variables** is checked, import.
   - **Import section layouts:** Choose `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_All-Sections_Layouts.json` (or `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_All-Individual-Sections.json` for individual sections). Import as layouts.
   - **Import page layouts:** Choose `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Pages.json` (and optionally `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Preset-Pages.json`, `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Premade-Layouts.json`). Import as layouts.
3. **Divi → Theme Builder → ↑↓** (Import/Export)
   - Import `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Theme-Builder-Templates.json` with **Presets** enabled. Allow override of existing template assignments if the site is new.
4. **Optional — Divi → Theme Customizer → ↑↓**
   - Import `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Theme-Customizer.json` to apply baseline typography and colors at the Customizer level.

After import, customize via **Design Variables** first (colors, fonts, spacing); presets and layouts that reference them will update automatically.

memories.summary: internals/style-guide-to-divi-variables-design.md: Design: Style Guide → Divi 5 Global Variables Import
memories.solution: Define a repeatable workflow (and companion Claude skill) that takes an arbitrary "style guide" input (prose and/or design tokens) and produces a **Divi 5–importable** JSON file for **Global Variables**.

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > After import: how to customize safely
memories.solution:
1. **Start with Design Variables** (colors, fonts, spacing, type scale).
2. Then adjust key **presets** (buttons, headings, sections, etc.).
3. Only then tweak specific **layouts**.

This preserves the “single source of truth” workflow where variables feed presets, and presets feed layouts.

memories.summary: internals/library-import-json.md: Library Import JSON Structure > Variable reference format
memories.solution:
Global colors and variables can reference other variables with a **wrapper syntax**:

```
$variable({"type":"<type>","value":{"name":"<variable-id>","settings":{<optional overrides>}}})$
```

**Examples:**

- Color with opacity: `"$variable({\"type\":\"color\",\"value\":{\"name\":\"gcid-y43rzvjcdl\",\"settings\":{\"opacity\":90}}})$"`
- Content (e.g. number): `"$variable({\"type\":\"content\",\"value\":{\"name\":\"gvid-6kxjcrjyig\",\"settings\":{}}})$"`

`type` can be `color`, `content`, etc.; `name` is the global variable/color id; `settings` can override (e.g. `opacity` for colors).

---

memories.summary: internals/style-guide-to-divi-variables-design.md: Design: Style Guide → Divi 5 Global Variables Import > Output artifact > Divi 5 Global Variables import JSON
memories.solution:
Single JSON object (root):

- `context`: `"et_builder"`
- `data`: `[]`
- `presets`: `[]`
- `global_colors`: array of tuples `[id, { color, status, label }]`
- `global_variables`: array of objects `{ id, label, value, order, status, lastUpdated, variableType, type, groupKey? }`
- `canvases`: `[]`
- `images`: `[]`
- `thumbnails`: `[]`

See [Library Import JSON](library-import-json.md) for the reverse-engineered schema.

memories.summary: internals/style-guide-to-divi-variables-design.md: Design: Style Guide → Divi 5 Global Variables Import > Extraction model > Precedence
memories.solution:
1. **Tokens payload** (if provided)
2. **Style guide prose extraction**

If both provide the same logical token, tokens payload wins.

memories.summary: internals/style-guide-to-divi-variables-design.md: Design: Style Guide → Divi 5 Global Variables Import > Extraction model > Confidence gating (prose)
memories.solution:
Only extract when there is an **explicit value** present, e.g.:

- Colors: `#RRGGBB`, `rgb(...)`, `rgba(...)`, `hsl(...)`, `hsla(...)`
- Sizes: `48px`, `1.2` (line-height), `-0.5px` (letter-spacing)
- Shadows: `0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)`
- URLs/emails/phones
- Font families: quoted or clearly named families (e.g. `Inter`, `Open Sans`)

If the text describes intent without a value (e.g. "use a deep navy"), it is reported as missing.

memories.summary: internals/style-guide-to-divi-variables-design.md: Design: Style Guide → Divi 5 Global Variables Import > Normalization rules
memories.solution:
- **Colors**: keep as hex if present; otherwise keep original functional color string (`rgb/rgba/hsl/hsla`).
- **Numbers**: store as string values with units when appropriate (`"16px"`, `"1200px"`, `"1.2"`).
- **Fonts**: store font family names as plain strings.
- **Strings/Links**: store as plain strings.

memories.summary: internals/style-guide-to-divi-variables-design.md: Design: Style Guide → Divi 5 Global Variables Import > Token taxonomy (canonical names)
memories.solution:
The generator should map found values into a canonical name hierarchy:

- `color.brand.*`, `color.neutral.*`, `color.semantic.*`
- `font.heading.family`, `font.body.family`
- `type.h1.size`, `type.h1.lineHeight`, `type.h1.letterSpacing`, `type.h1.weight`, `type.h1.color` (if present)
- `space.*` (scale), `radius.*`, `shadow.*`
- `layout.container.max`, `layout.text.max`, `layout.breakpoint.*` (if present)
- `link.*`, `string.*`

These names are used for labels/IDs and for a human-facing "token report".

memories.summary: internals/style-guide-to-divi-variables-design.md: Design: Style Guide → Divi 5 Global Variables Import > ID strategy (stable)
memories.solution:
Divi global identifiers are free-form strings. Use stable, deterministic IDs:

- **Global colors**: `gcid-<slug>`
- **Global variables**: `gvid-<slug>`

Where `<slug>` is derived from canonical name (or label), normalized to:

- lowercase
- alphanumerics and hyphens only
- collapse repeats, trim hyphens

Collision handling: append `-2`, `-3`, etc.

memories.summary: internals/style-guide-to-divi-variables-design.md: Design: Style Guide → Divi 5 Global Variables Import > Divi variable typing
memories.solution:
Map token categories to Divi's `type`:

- Colors → `colors` (+ mirrored entry in `global_colors`)
- Font families → `fonts`
- Measurements, type scale, spacing, radii, shadows → `numbers`
- Brand phrases, address, CTA copy → `strings`
- URLs → `links`
- Images (if present) → `images`

For each variable object:

- `status`: `"active"`
- `lastUpdated`: ISO 8601 (generation time)
- `variableType`: same as `type`
- `order`: `""` (or a numeric string, if we decide to enforce ordering later)
- `groupKey`: optional, may be used to group in UI (e.g. `"colors"`, `"fonts"`)

memories.summary: playbooks/design-system-setup.md: Playbook: Design System Setup
memories.solution:
**Configure global typography, colors, and design variables BEFORE building any pages.**

!!! abstract "Quick Rules"
    1. Always set global typography and colors in Theme Customizer BEFORE building any pages — this is the highest-leverage step in any Divi 5 build.
    2. Use `wp.customize` JavaScript API to set font, size, and color globals programmatically, then click Publish.
    3. Map hex colors and font families to named Divi 5 Design Variables in the Variable Manager — use site variables instead of hardcoded values.
    4. Verify globals by opening any page — text modules should display correct fonts, sizes, and colors without per-module overrides.

!!! danger "CRITICAL: Do This First"
    If you skip this step, every text module on every page will need manual font, size, and color overrides. Setting globals first means ~80% of text styling is automatic. This is the single highest-leverage step in any Divi 5 build.

memories.summary: playbooks/design-system-setup.md: Playbook: Design System Setup > Why This Matters
memories.solution:
Divi 5 modules inherit from Theme Customizer globals. If the globals match the target design, most modules will look correct by default. Without globals set first, you'll spend exponentially more time on per-module styling and fight Divi's defaults (14px body text, 30px headings) on every single element.

Color globals (accent, link, header) cascade into buttons, links, and heading modules site-wide. Get these right once and they propagate everywhere.

If you already have a style guide (brand guidelines, design tokens, or a doc), you can use the [Divi Variables From Style Guide](https://github.com/16wells/divi-styleguide-variables) Claude skill to generate a Divi 5 Global Variables import file (see [Import Design Systems](../recipes/import-design-systems.md)), then follow this playbook to get everything into your site quickly.

memories.summary: playbooks/design-system-setup.md: Playbook: Design System Setup > Step-by-Step Process > Step 4: Configure Divi 5 Design Variables
memories.solution:
After setting Theme Customizer globals, open the Visual Builder and configure **Design Variables** (Variable Manager):

- Map your hex colors to named variables (Primary, Secondary, Accent, etc.)
- Map font families and sizes to variables
- These variables can then be referenced in any module's settings

Audit the default Divi 5 variables against the client's style guide — the defaults may not match. Fix variables first, then verify that Element Presets (which inherit variable values) look correct.

memories.summary: playbooks/design-system-setup.md: Playbook: Design System Setup > Step-by-Step Process > Step 5: Use Site Variables in Module Settings
memories.solution:
When editing any field in the Design panel (spacing, sizing, typography, color, etc.), clicking into the field reveals a small **database icon** at the right edge. Clicking this icon lets you insert a **site variable** — a global design token from the Variable Manager.

**Use site variables instead of hardcoded values** whenever a value should be global: accent color, standard section padding, maximum content width. This means updating the global variable automatically propagates to every module using it — no hunting through dozens of modules to change a padding value.

memories.summary: playbooks/known-limitations.md: Playbook: Known Limitations > Soft Rules (Getting These Wrong Wastes Time) > 18. Design Panel Site Variables (Database Icon)
memories.solution: When editing any field in the Design panel (spacing, sizing, typography, etc.), clicking into the field reveals a small database icon at the right edge. memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5
memories.solution: How to import a Divi 5 “design system” (presets, design variables, layouts, Theme Builder templates, and optional Customizer settings) into a clean Divi 5 installation.

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > Overview
memories.solution:
Most Divi 5 design system downloads ship as a ZIP containing multiple JSON files. Each JSON file targets a different importer:

- **Presets**: module presets + option group presets
- **Design Variables**: global colors + variables (numbers, strings, fonts, images, links)
- **Layouts**: pages, section layouts, premade layouts
- **Theme Builder**: headers/footers/templates (often references layouts)
- **Theme Customizer (optional)**: baseline typography + colors as WP theme mods

The key to successful imports is **order**: presets + variables first, then layouts, then Theme Builder, then Customizer.

!!! note "Start on a clean site"
    Imports are safest on a fresh Divi 5 install. Importing into an existing site can overwrite presets, add lots of library items, and change Theme Builder assignments.

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > What’s in a typical ZIP
memories.solution:
Using the Divi 5 Launch Design System as an example, the ZIP contains files like:

- `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Presets.json`
- `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Global-Variables.json`
- `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_All-Sections_Layouts.json` (or `..._All-Individual-Sections.json`)
- `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Pages.json` (and sometimes additional layout packs)
- `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Theme-Builder-Templates.json`
- `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Theme-Customizer.json` (optional)

If you see `__MACOSX/` folders, you can ignore them.

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > Import order (recommended)
memories.solution:
1. **Import Presets**
2. **Import Global Variables**
3. **Import Section Layouts**
4. **Import Page / Premade Layouts**
5. **Import Theme Builder Templates**
6. **(Optional) Import Theme Customizer settings**

This order avoids missing references like a layout that points to a preset id or a variable that doesn’t exist yet.

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > How to tell which JSON file goes where (by `context`)
memories.solution:
If you’re importing a different design system and the filenames aren’t obvious, open the JSON file and check the first field: **`context`**. It determines which Divi importer will accept the file.

| `context` value | What it contains | Where to import |
|---|---|---|
| `et_builder` | Presets and/or Global Variables | **Divi → Divi Library → Import & Export** |
| `et_builder_layouts` | Layouts (pages, sections, premades) | **Divi → Divi Library → Import & Export** |
| `et_theme_builder` | Theme Builder templates + referenced layouts | **Divi → Theme Builder → ↑↓** |
| `et_divi_mods` | Theme Customizer settings (theme mods) | **Divi → Theme Customizer → ↑↓** |

For the deeper JSON structure and how presets/variables are referenced, see [Library Import JSON Structure](../internals/library-import-json.md).

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > Step-by-step import (Divi 5 Launch Design System) > 1) Import Presets (Divi Library)
memories.solution:
1. Go to **Divi → Divi Library → Import & Export**
2. Choose `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Presets.json`
3. Ensure **Import Presets** is enabled
4. Import

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > Step-by-step import (Divi 5 Launch Design System) > 2) Import Global Variables (Divi Library)
memories.solution:
1. In the same **Import & Export** dialog, choose `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Global-Variables.json`
2. Ensure **Import Global Variables** is enabled
3. Import

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > Step-by-step import (Divi 5 Launch Design System) > 3) Import Section Layouts (Divi Library)
memories.solution:
Choose one:

- **Grouped section layouts**: import `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_All-Sections_Layouts.json`
- **Individual sections**: import `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_All-Individual-Sections.json`

Import via **Divi → Divi Library → Import & Export**.

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > Step-by-step import (Divi 5 Launch Design System) > 4) Import Pages and Premade Layouts (Divi Library)
memories.solution:
Import any of the following (as desired):

- `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Pages.json`
- `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Premade-Layouts.json`
- `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Preset-Pages.json`

These create many Divi Library items and/or pages depending on how the pack is structured.

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > Step-by-step import (Divi 5 Launch Design System) > 5) Import Theme Builder templates (Theme Builder)
memories.solution:
1. Go to **Divi → Theme Builder**
2. Use the **↑↓ Import/Export** control
3. Import `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Theme-Builder-Templates.json`
4. If prompted, enable importing presets with the templates

!!! warning "Template assignments can override your site"
    Theme Builder imports can replace existing header/footer/template assignments. On a non-clean site, export your current Theme Builder state first.

memories.summary: recipes/import-design-systems.md: Import a Design System into Divi 5 > Step-by-step import (Divi 5 Launch Design System) > 6) Optional: Import Theme Customizer settings (Customizer)
memories.solution:
1. Go to **Divi → Theme Customizer**
2. Use the **↑↓ Import/Export** control
3. Import `Divi-5-Launch-Freebie_Theme-Customizer.json`

This typically affects global typography and baseline colors.

memories.summary: internals/ssr-rendering.md: SSR Rendering
memories.solution:
How Divi 5's server-side rendering processes block comments into HTML, and the critical boundaries that determine what renders.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What this documents:** Server-side rendering behavior in Divi 5, including the critical `post-content` boundary, the double comment bug, and background image rendering gaps.
    **Key data structures:** `<!-- /wp:post-content -->` boundary marker, `_et_pb_use_builder` post meta flag, section open/close tag validation.
    **Last verified:** 2026-03-12

memories.summary: internals/ssr-rendering.md: SSR Rendering > The `post-content` Boundary
memories.solution:
**This is the #1 gotcha for programmatic content management with Divi 5.**

Page content often ends with a `<!-- /wp:post-content -->` closing tag. This marks the boundary of the WordPress block parser's content area. Any Divi blocks inserted AFTER this tag will NOT be rendered by SSR.

Blocks after the boundary appear in `view-source:` as unprocessed block comments (invisible to users on the rendered page).

memories.summary: internals/ssr-rendering.md: SSR Rendering > The `post-content` Boundary > How to Detect
memories.solution: Content appears in raw HTML source but not in the rendered DOM. Block comments are passed through literally instead of being processed into `<div class="et_pb_section_X">` elements.

memories.summary: internals/ssr-rendering.md: SSR Rendering > The `post-content` Boundary > How to Prevent
internals/ssr-rendering.md: SSR Rendering > Background Image Rendering Gap
memories.solution:
Divi 5 SSR does not reliably render background images set via section JSON attributes. Sections render with a white/blank background.

**Workaround:** Set a solid `color` in section attributes, then use inline CSS in a text block for the actual background image. See the [HTML Workarounds](../playbooks/html-workarounds.md) playbook.

memories.summary: internals/ssr-rendering.md: SSR Rendering > Post Meta Requirements
memories.solution: For Divi SSR to process a page, the `_et_pb_use_builder` post meta must be set to `"on"`. This is automatic for pages created through the Visual Builder but must be explicitly set when creating pages via REST API.

memories.summary: internals/ssr-rendering.md: SSR Rendering > Section Validation Checklist
memories.solution:
Before every programmatic content save:

1. Section open and close tag counts must be equal
2. Zero `<!--<!--` double comment patterns
3. Content starts with `<!-- wp:divi/placeholder -->` (if using placeholder wrapper)
4. Content ends before `<!-- /wp:post-content -->` boundary
5. No raw HTML between section close tags and next section open tags
6. Total character count is reasonable (not accidentally truncated)

memories.summary: internals/testimonial-ssr.md: Testimonial Rendering Gaps > Author and JobTitle Fields Not Rendered
playbooks/known-limitations.md: Playbook: Known Limitations > Hard Rules (Violating These Breaks Things) > 3. Testimonial Blocks Don't Render Author/JobTitle
memories.solution:
The `wp:divi/testimonial` block supports `content.author` and `content.jobTitle` fields in JSON, but SSR renders ONLY the `innerContent` field. Author and job title are silently dropped.

Additionally, testimonial `innerContent` is **plain text, not HTML**. Unicode-encoded HTML tags (`\u003c`) render as literal escape sequences on the page.

**What to do instead:** Append attribution as plain text with an em dash:
```

— Author Name, Company Name
```

memories.summary: TinyMCE state sync in Divi 5: Reading works, but setting content fails on save.
memories.solution:
When a Text module is selected in the Visual Builder, the active TinyMCE editor instance can be accessed via `window.tinymce.get('_content-innerContent_vb_tiny_mce')`. Content reading is reliable using `editor.getContent()`. However, calling `tinymce.setContent()` only updates the visual display and fails to sync with Divi's internal React save state; content set this way will revert upon saving. The reliable method for programmatically setting text content is simulating keyboard input: click into the editor, use Cmd+A / Ctrl+A (or equivalent) to select all, and then type the replacement content. This triggers the necessary React event chain that Divi captures.

Keyboard shortcuts that reliably sync include:
- Bold: `Cmd+B` / `Ctrl+B`
- Italic: `Cmd+I` / `Ctrl+I`
- Insert link: `Cmd+K` / `Ctrl+K`
- Select all: `Cmd+A` / `Ctrl+A`
- Changing heading level (H1-H6) via the Paragraph dropdown.

For automation tools, use `type()` actions instead of direct JavaScript DOM manipulation.

memories.summary: Divi 5 VB uses dual-frame architecture, React state, and global objects for structure.
memories.solution:
The Visual Builder (VB) employs a dual-frame structure: 

1. **Parent window:** Contains the sidebar, settings panel (React app), toolbar, and Layers panel. This is where `window.tinymce` lives.
2. **Iframe (`#et-vb-app-frame`):** Contains the page canvas/preview, housing the page DOM, WordPress core (`wp.*`), and Divi runtime objects.

**Accessing the iframe:** 
```javascript
const appFrame = document.querySelector('#et-vb-app-frame');
const iframeWin = appFrame.contentWindow;
```

**Global Objects:**
* **Parent Window:** `window.tinymce` (TinyMCE instances when a text module is selected). The React root for the settings panel/sidebar UI is `#et-vb-app-frame-wrapper`. 
* **Iframe (`iframeWin`):** Contains builder-specific objects:
    * `DIVI`: Builder configuration (e.g., item counts, selectors).
    * `ET_Builder`: Builder API (includes `API`, `Frames`, `Misc`).
    * `ETCloudApp`: Cloud/Library functions.
    * `wp`: WordPress core (hooks, i18n, ajax). **Note:** `wp.data` is NOT available in the iframe. 

**State Management:** State management is internal; Divi 5 does not expose a Redux store or `wp.data` stores.

memories.summary: modules/accordion.md: Accordion
memories.solution:
The Accordion module displays collapsible content sections where only one item is open at a time.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What it does:** Organizes content into vertically stacked expandable/collapsible panels where only one panel is open at a time.
    **When to use it:** FAQ sections, product/service detail breakdowns, step-by-step instructions
    **Key settings:** Toggle Icon, Loop, Order, individual item Title and Content
    **Block identifier:** `divi/accordion`
    **ET Docs:** [Official documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/10063343-the-accordion-module-in-divi-5)

!!! tip "When to Use This Module"
    - You need collapsible content sections where only one item should be open at a time
    - FAQ pages where visitors scan questions and expand individual answers
    - Long-form content that needs to be broken into scannable, on-demand sections

!!! warning "When NOT to Use This Module"
    - You need multiple items open simultaneously → use [Toggle](toggle.md)
    - You want horizontal tab-based content organization → use [Tabs](tabs.md)
    - You need rich media galleries or sliders → use [Gallery](gallery.md) or [Slider](slider.md)

memories.summary: modules/accordion.md: Accordion > Overview
memories.solution:
The Accordion module organizes content into a vertically stacked group of expandable/collapsible panels. When a visitor clicks on a panel header, its content is revealed and any previously open panel collapses automatically. By default, the first panel is open when the page loads.

This behavior distinguishes it from the [Toggle](toggle.md) module, where multiple items can be open simultaneously. The accordion enforces a one-at-a-time pattern, which keeps the layout compact and focused.

For additional reference, see the [official Elegant Themes documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/10063343-the-accordion-module-in-divi-5).

[View A Live Demo Of This Module](https://www.16wells.dev/module-demos/accordion/)

![Accordion module](../assets/screenshots/modules/accordion/element.png){ loading=lazy }
*The Accordion module showing collapsible FAQ-style content panels.*

memories.summary: modules/accordion.md: Accordion > Use Cases
memories.solution:
1. **FAQ Sections** — Present frequently asked questions with answers that expand on click, keeping the page scannable without overwhelming visitors with a wall of text.
2. **Product or Service Details** — Break down features, specifications, or plan tiers into expandable sections so visitors can drill into what interests them.
3. **Step-by-Step Instructions** — Organize multi-step processes where each step expands to reveal detailed instructions, keeping the overall flow visible.

memories.summary: modules/accordion.md: Accordion > How to Add the Accordion Module
memories.solution:
1. Open the Visual Builder on the page you want to edit.
2. Click the gray **+** icon to add a new module to a row.
3. Search for "Accordion" in the module picker or find it in the Content Elements category, then click to insert it.

memories.summary: modules/accordion.md: Accordion > Settings & Options
memories.solution: The Accordion module settings are organized across three tabs: Content, Design, and Advanced.

memories.summary: modules/accordion.md: Accordion > Settings & Options > Content Tab
memories.solution:
The Content tab controls the accordion's items, icon, link behavior, background, and metadata.

| Setting | Type | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| Add, Edit, and Remove | item list | Manage individual accordion items. Each item has its own title and body content. Click **+** to add, the pencil icon to edit, the trash icon to delete, and drag to reorder. |
| Toggle Icon | icon picker | Choose the icon displayed next to each accordion item header that indicates expand/collapse state. |
| Link | url | Optionally link the entire accordion module to a URL. |
| Background | background controls | Set a background color, gradient, image, or video behind the entire accordion module. |
| Loop | toggle | When enabled, collapsing the last item automatically opens the first item, creating a circular navigation pattern. |
| Order | select | Control the display order of accordion items (e.g., default order or reversed). |
| Meta | admin label | Set an admin label for the module to help identify it in the Visual Builder's layer panel. |

![Accordion Content tab settings](../assets/screenshots/modules/accordion/settings-content.png){ loading=lazy }

memories.summary: modules/accordion.md: Accordion > Settings & Options > Content Tab > Individual Accordion Item Settings

Each accordion item within the module has its own settings:

| Content | rich text editor | The body content revealed when the item is expanded. Supports text, images, and other media. |

memories.summary: modules/accordion.md: Accordion > Managing Accordion Items
memories.solution:
Each accordion module starts with a set of default items. You can:

memories.summary: Troubleshooting issues with bar and circle counter modules.
memories.solution:
**Bar Counter Issues:**
* **Not Animating:** Ensure the module is below the fold to trigger scroll animations. Check for JavaScript errors or caching plugins serving static snapshots.
* **Percentage Labels Missing:** In the Content tab, open Elements and confirm percentage display is enabled. Verify that the Design tab Percentage Text color does not match the bar fill color. Ensure the bar height is sufficient for the configured font size.
* **Bars Same Color:** To assign unique colors to individual bars, set the Background Color in each bar item's settings.

**Circle Counter Issues:**
* **Not Animating:** Animation triggers on scroll into view. If visible at load, it may have already completed. Check for script-blocking plugins or content security policy conflicts. Temporarily disabling lazy-load optimizations can help diagnose issues.
* **Not Visible:** Verify that the circle color and background color are not identical (making the arc invisible). Ensure the **Number** field in the Content tab is set to a value greater than 0. Inspect with DevTools to confirm the canvas/SVG element exists and has proper dimensions.
* **Matching Sizes:** Circle counters scale to column width. For consistent sizing across columns, ensure all columns have equal widths or apply `max-width` via custom CSS on `.et_pb_circle_counter`.

**Number Counter Issues:**
* **Not Animating:** Clear site and CDN caches. Check for JavaScript errors in the browser console, as script conflicts can prevent animation initialization.
* **Zero Value:** The counter must have a numeric value entered in the Number field (Content tab's Text group). Non-numeric or empty fields result in zero. Also confirm the module is not hidden by Visibility settings.
* **Percent Sign Missing:** In the Content tab, expand Elements and ensure the Percent Sign toggle is explicitly enabled for percentage counters.

memories.summary: The Blog module displays dynamic WordPress posts in configurable grid or fullwidth layouts.
memories.solution:
The Blog module (`divi/blog`) pulls and renders WordPress posts on any page, supporting various layouts (fullwidth list, multi-column grid with masonry). It displays featured images, titles, excerpts/full content, author/date metadata, category labels, comment counts, and read-more links. Key settings include Post Count, Layout (Grid/Fullwidth), Show Pagination, Offset, and Include Categories.

**Use Cases:** Blog index pages, homepage 'latest posts' sections, category archives, and related post areas.

**Content Query Settings (Content Tab > Content):**
*   `Post Count`: Maximum number of posts per page (default 10).
*   `Include Categories`: Filters posts to selected WordPress categories. If none are selected, all published posts are included.
*   `Date Format`: PHP date format string for post dates (default `M j, Y`).
*   `Show Featured Image`: Toggle visibility of the featured image above the title.
*   `Show Content`: Selects between displaying a truncated excerpt or full post content.
*   `Excerpt Length`: Character count for excerpts (default 270). Only applies when `Show Content` is set to excerpt mode.
*   `Show Author`, `Show Date`, `Show Categories`, `Show Comments Count`: Toggles to display/hide specific metadata elements in the meta line.
*   `Show Pagination`: Enables or disables page navigation at the bottom of the post list. If disabled, only the first page is shown.
*   `Offset`: Skips a specified number of posts from the beginning of the query (useful for avoiding duplicates).

**Design Controls (Design Tab):**
*   `Layout`: Choose between Fullwidth (list) and Grid layout modes. In Grid mode, set columns (1-4) and toggle masonry positioning.
*   `Overlay`: Configures the hover overlay on featured images (color, icon, icon color).
*   `Read More Text`: Styles the 'read more' link.
*   **Shared Options Groups:** The module supports extensive styling via standard options groups for visual control:
    *   `Image`: Border radius, alignment, sizing for featured images.
    *   `Text`, `Title Text`, `Body Text`, `Meta Text`, `Pagination Text`: Control typography (font, size, color, line height, text shadow).
    *   `Sizing`, `Spacing`, `Border`, `Box Shadow`, `Filters`, `Transform`, `Animation`: Advanced visual styling controls.

memories.solution:
Most modules share an Advanced tab offering controls for custom attributes, conditional display, interactions, and scroll effects. These options include:

*   **CSS:** Add custom CSS code to fine-tune the module's appearance.

*   **Transitions:** Control animation timing (e.g., hover transition duration).

memories.summary: Blog Module usage for various content display scenarios.
memories.solution:
For a **Homepage Latest Posts** section, place the Blog module in a fullwidth section with Post Count set to 3, Layout set to Grid (3 columns), and pagination disabled. Add a button module below linking to the blog archive.

For a **Category Landing Page**, use the Include Categories filter. Set the layout to Fullwidth or Grid. Enable all meta elements (author, date, related categories).

For a **Related Posts Section** within a Theme Builder post template: Add the Blog module below main content. Filter it by the current post's category, set a low Post Count (3-4), use Grid layout, and apply an offset of 1 to skip the current post.

**Troubleshooting:**
*   If posts are empty, verify that published posts exist in selected categories, the Offset is not too high, and no custom code filters results. Ensure Post Count > 0.
*   For uneven Grid columns (Masonry), either crop featured images to a uniform aspect ratio or disable Masonry.
*   On static front pages, Blog module pagination may conflict with WordPress paging; add a query variable fix (`page` to `paged`) in the child theme's `functions.php`.

memories.summary: Post Carousel Module details and usage for dynamic content display.
memories.solution:
The Post Carousel module displays posts (featured image, title, date) in a browsable format via horizontal scrolling or static grid.

**Usage:**
*   **Homepage Featured Posts:** Place prominently to highlight recent/featured articles.
*   **Category Spotlight:** Filter by category on a landing page for focused content sections.
*   **Portfolio Grid:** Use the Grid layout mode with custom post types (e.g., portfolio projects) for an interactive card-based display.

**Settings & Options:**
*   **Content Tab:** Controls which posts appear, what elements are shown (Title, Date), and module linking/backgrounds. Settings include: `Post Type` (select), `Categories` (multi-select filter), `Show Post Title` (toggle), `Show Publish Date` (toggle), `Link` (url), `Background` (controls), `Order` (select), `Meta` (admin label).
*   **Design Tab:** Controls layout and styling. Settings include: `Layout` (select: Carousel/Grid), `Carousel Columns` (number, only for Grid), `Column Spacing` (range, only for Grid), `Overlay` (overlay styling), `Image` (image styling), `Title Text` (text styling), `Carousel Item Title Text` (text styling), `Meta Text` (text styling).
*   **Advanced Tab:** Provides developer controls: `Attributes` (CSS ID, classes, custom HTML attributes), `CSS` (custom CSS per element target), `HTML` (semantic tag choice), `Conditions` (display rules), `Interactions` (hover/click/scroll effects), `Visibility` (device toggles), `Transitions` (timing), `Position` (CSS position), `Scroll Effects` (animation).

**Module Identifier:** `divi/post-carousel`

memories.summary: Combines icon or image with text for feature grids, service cards, and content blocks.
memories.solution:
The Blurb module creates self-contained content units by pairing a visual element (Divi icon or uploaded image) with a title and body text. It is used for feature highlights, service descriptions, process steps, and benefit lists.

**Layouts & Placement:**
*   **Vertical Stack (Default):** Image/icon appears above the text, suitable for card-style grids.
*   **Horizontal Layout:** Visual element can be placed to the left of the text, ideal for inline feature lists or process flows. The `Image/Icon Placement` setting controls this.

**Technical Details & Settings:**
*   **Block Identifier:** `divi/blurb`
*   **Content Tab:** Controls title and body text (rich text supported), visual media choice (icon from built-in library or uploaded image with alt text), linking behavior (assigning a URL makes the entire module, including title and icon/image, clickable), background settings, loop builder support, display order (`Order`), and custom admin labeling (`Meta`).
*   **Design Tab:** Provides styling for the visual element and all text components. Specific controls include: `Image & Icon` (setting color, size, shape, padding for icons; max width, alignment, border radius for images), typography settings for Title Text and Body Text, spacing, borders, box shadows, CSS filters, transforms, and animations.
*   **Advanced Options:** The module supports dynamic content via the loop builder and layout control via `Order` (for Flexbox/CSS Grid). Styling is highly customizable using dedicated options groups like [Text], [Title Text], [Body Text], [Sizing], [Spacing], [Border], [Box Shadow], [Filters], [Transform], and [Animation].
*   **Image & Icon Options:** A shared setting controlling placement, alignment, border, shadow, and filters for combined image/icon elements. It is available on the Blurb module (primarily) and supports responsive settings.

**Use Cases:**
1.  **Feature/Service Grid:** Arranging multiple blurbs in equal-width columns with icons to present key product features or services.
2.  **Process Steps:** Using left placement with numbered icons for sequential workflows or 'how-it-works' sections.
3.  **Clickable Card Navigation:** Assigning URLs and applying design effects (background, border radius, box shadow) to create a visual navigation grid linking to sub-pages.

**Troubleshooting & Gotchas:**
*   **Icon Not Displaying:** If the icon appears as an empty square, ensure that performance optimization plugins are not dequeuing the `et-icons` stylesheet. Verify icon font file accessibility.
*   **Image Blurriness (Retina):** To achieve crisp display on high-density screens, upload images at twice the intended display size and use the Image Max Width setting to constrain them.

memories.summary: Button styling uses Visual Design, Responsive Editor, Presets, and Custom CSS.
memories.solution:
Divi 5 fundamentally changed button styling from Divi 4. Styling is managed through four approaches: 
1. **Visual Design Tab:** Built-in style properties with instant preview.
2. **Hover States:** Managed via the Responsive Editor for interactive effects.
3. **Button Presets:** Reusable, stackable style sets for design systems.
4. **Custom CSS:** For specialized effects not covered by the Design tab.

The core styling controls are located in the **Design → Button** panel. To enable advanced styling, toggle **Use Custom Styles for Button** to **ON**. All visual properties (e.g., `Button Background Color`, `Button Border Radius`) can be set here. The Responsive Editor manages device breakpoints and hover states simultaneously:

| Breakpoint | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| Desktop | Screens >992px wide (Default baseline). |
| Tablet | Screens 768px–992px wide (Inherits from Desktop if unset). |
| Mobile | Screens <768px wide (Inherits from Tablet if unset). |
| Hover | Interactive state for all devices. Always the bottom row in the Responsive Editor.

**Customization Methods:**
* **Attributes Panel:** Add custom HTML attributes and CSS classes (e.g., `class`, `data-tracking`). This is where CSS classes are added, not a dedicated toggle.
* **Free-Form CSS:** Use the `Advanced → CSS` area for module-specific raw CSS rules. Use the `selector` keyword to target the button without knowing its generated class name (e.g., `selector { color: red; }`).

memories.summary: Presets are reusable style sets that can be stacked and globally updated.
memories.solution:
Button Presets are named, reusable style sets applied via the **Preset dropdown** at the top of the settings panel. 

**Workflow:**
1. Set desired default styles in **Design → Button**. 
2. Click the **Preset dropdown** and select **"Create New Preset From Current Styles"** to save the current state.
3. Apply the preset by selecting it from the dropdown; all default and hover styles apply instantly.
4. **Global Editing:** To update a preset site-wide, open any button using the preset, click the **Preset dropdown**, hover over the name, and click the **gear icon**. Changes made here affect *all* instances of that preset.
5. **Stacking:** Multiple presets can be applied; later presets override earlier ones for the same property.
6. **Default Preset:** Mark a preset as default using the **star icon** in the dropdown so all new buttons automatically use it.

memories.summary: Button module is a standalone CTA element with customizable styling and functionality.
memories.solution:
The Button module creates a single styled link (CTA) that can point to an external URL, internal page, section anchor, or file download. It supports configurable text, icon, colors, borders, hover effects, and responsive settings across desktop, tablet, and phone breakpoints.

**Usage:**
*   Primary CTAs, download links, section anchors, or general navigation points.
*   Use for standalone clickable elements (e.g., Hero sections, pricing areas).
*   Do not use if the goal is a heading + description + button combo (use Call to Action module) or a form submission (use Contact Form/Email Optin modules).

**Settings & Structure:**
*   **Content Tab:** Controls the visible label (`Text`), destination link (`Link`), and optional loop functionality. Also manages display order (`Order`) and admin identification (`Meta`).
*   **Design Tab:** Manages visual appearance, including alignment (left, center, right) and responsive settings.
*   **Options Groups:** Shared styling controls include `Button` (text size, colors, border, radius, icon, hover behavior), `Spacing`, `Text`, `Box Shadow`, `Filters`, `Transform`, and `Animation`. 

**Common Patterns:**
*   **Ghost Button:** Transparent fill with a visible border; fills lightly on hover. Text color: `#0066CC`; Border Color: `#0066CC`; Background (Hover): `#E6F0FF`.
*   **Icon + Text:** Icon appears next to text, inheriting the text color. Padding: `12px 24px`. Font Size: `16px`.
*   **Gradient Button:** Uses a gradient for background and hover states (e.g., blue → purple on background; purple → dark purple on hover).
*   **Hero CTA:** Use bold colors, generous padding, and pill-shaped border radius to make the button focal. Center or left alignment depends on the hero layout.
*   **Ghost Pair:** Place two buttons side-by-side: one solid (primary action) and one transparent/bordered (secondary action).

**Technical Details & Best Practices:**
*   **Block Identifier:** `divi/button`.
*   **REST API Interaction:** Modifying content via REST API (`wp.apiFetch` PATCH) updates text, body, and settings attributes. Creating new modules via REST API may not render in the Visual Builder layer view; use browser automation for reliable creation.
*   **Module Selection Guidance:** Use Button for standalone CTAs; Call to Action for text+button combos; Contact Form/Email Optin for form submissions.

memories.summary: CTA module structure: heading, description, and clickable button for conversions.
memories.solution:
The Call to Action (CTA) module bundles a title, body text, and a prominent button into one visually distinct block designed for conversion-focused content. It is used for scenarios like newsletter signups, pricing prompts, or full-width content dividers.

**Key Settings & Content:**
*   **Title:** The main heading (supports dynamic content).
*   **Body:** Descriptive text between the title and button (rich text editor).
*   **Button Text:** Label for the CTA button. The button is hidden if this field is empty.
*   **Link:** Destination URL for the button, which can also make the entire module clickable.
*   **Background:** Controls background color, gradient, image, or video; multiple layers can be combined.
*   **Loop:** Enables dynamic repetition of the CTA based on a data source (e.g., posts).

**Design Options:** The visual appearance is controlled by shared options groups including Text, Title Text, Body Text, Button, Sizing, Spacing, Border, Box Shadow, Filters, Transform, and Animation.

*   **API Interaction:** Modifying existing content uses `wp.apiFetch` PATCH; creating new modules requires browser automation for reliable Visual Builder visibility.

memories.summary: Embedding external functionality via code and shortcodes.
memories.solution:
Use the Code module for three primary functions:
1. **Third-Party Embeds:** Paste embed codes (e.g., Calendly, Google Maps, payment processors) to integrate external services.
2. **Custom Scripting:** Add page-specific JavaScript for animations, scroll events, or custom form validation without modifying theme files.
3. **Shortcode Rendering:** Insert shortcodes (e.g., `[woocommerce_cart]`, `[gravityform id="1"]`) from plugins like WooCommerce or contact forms to render output within the layout structure.

For scheduling widgets, paste the embed code into a Code module and set a max-width in the Design tab for centering; also add top/bottom padding to prevent crowding adjacent modules.

For page-specific CSS, place a Code module in a fullwidth section at the top of the layout and enclose your CSS within `<style>` tags.

memories.summary: Code Module: Configuration options for content, design, and advanced behavior.
memories.solution:
The Code module settings are structured into three tabs: Content, Design, and Advanced.

**Content Tab:**
The main editing area accepts HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or shortcodes. CSS must be enclosed in `<style>` tags, and JavaScript in `<script>` tags. The editor preserves whitespace and does not apply formatting.
*   **Text (Code Editor):** Main editing area for code.
*   **Link:** Optionally wraps the module output in a clickable link.
*   **Background:** Controls background color, gradient, image, or video.
*   **Loop:** Toggles connection to the loop builder for dynamic templates.
*   **Order:** Sets display order when the parent uses Flexbox or Grid layout.
*   **Meta:** Assigns an admin label visible in the Visual Builder layers panel.

**Design Tab:**
The Design tab controls visual presentation using shared options groups:
*   Text: Font, weight, alignment, color, line height, text shadow.
*   Sizing: Width, max-width, height, min-height.
*   Spacing: Responsive margin and padding.
*   Border: Width, color, style, radius.
*   Box Shadow: Shadow effects.
*   Filters: CSS filters (e.g., brightness, contrast).
*   Transform: Advanced design effects (scale, translate, rotate, skew).
*   Animation: Entrance animation styles.

**Advanced Tab:**
The advanced settings are shared across multiple modules and include:
*   Attributes: CSS ID, classes, custom HTML attributes.
*   CSS: Custom CSS targeting specific elements.
*   HTML: Semantic HTML tag for the module wrapper (e.g., `div`, `header`, `section`).
*   Conditions: Display rules based on user role, page type, date, or logic.
*   Interactions: Hover, click, or scroll-triggered interactions.
*   Visibility: Device visibility toggles.
*   Transitions: Hover transition timing.
*   Position: CSS position and offsets.
*   Scroll Effects: Scroll-driven animation effects.

memories.summary: General notes on module content manipulation via REST API.
memories.solution:
Modifying existing modules using `wp.apiFetch` PATCH updates title, body text, and settings attributes.

**Warning:** Creating new modules via REST API produces front-end renderable content but may not appear in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation (e.g., Playwright) for reliable module creation.

**General Block Operations:**
*   **Read Content:** Parse `post_content` block JSON using a brace-depth parser.
*   **Modify Existing:** Use `wp.apiFetch` PATCH on the post endpoint to update attributes in `post_content`.
*   **Create New:** Browser automation (Playwright) is recommended due to potential Visual Builder visibility issues with REST creation.
*   **Batch Modify:** Requires sequential REST requests.

**Module-Specific Attributes & Identifiers:**
*   **Code Module (`divi/code`):** Raw content can be stored in `attrs.raw_content` (HTML, CSS, JS, or shortcodes).
*   **Comments Module (`divi/comments`):** Key attributes include `attrs.show_avatar`, `attrs.show_reply`, and `attrs.show_count`.
*   **Contact Form Module (`divi/contact-form`):** Attributes include `attrs.fields` (field configuration array), `attrs.email` (recipient email address(es)), `attrs.subject` (notification subject line), `attrs.success_message`, and `attrs.redirect_url`.
*   **Countdown Timer Module (`divi/countdown-timer`):** Attributes include `attrs.date_time` (target date/time) and `attrs.use_cookie` (evergreen cookie toggle).
*   **Divider Module (`divi/divider`):** Attributes include `attrs.show_divider`, `attrs.divider_style` (CSS border style), and `attrs.divider_weight` (line thickness in pixels).
*   **Email Optin Module (`divi/signup`):** Attributes include `attrs.provider` (email marketing service), `attrs.list` (target mailing list), `attrs.title`, `attrs.content`, and `attrs.button_text`.
*   **Woo Checkout Billing Module (`divi/woo-checkout-billing`):** No specific attributes listed, but general block operations apply.

memories.summary: modules/comments.md: Comments
memories.solution:
The Comments module displays and styles the WordPress comment section within Divi 5 layouts.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What it does:** Renders the WordPress comment list and reply form with full visual styling control.
    **When to use it:** Blog post templates, product feedback pages, community discussion sections
    **Key settings:** Show Author Avatar, Show Reply Button, Show Comment Count, Show Comment Meta, Fields styling
    **Block identifier:** `divi/comments`
    **ET Docs:** [Official documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/10260827-the-comments-module-in-divi-5)

!!! tip "When to Use This Module"
    - Displaying comments on blog post templates built with the Theme Builder
    - Adding a discussion section to pages, products, or custom post types
    - Replacing default theme comment styling with a fully customized design

!!! warning "When NOT to Use This Module"
    - For collecting structured data from visitors → use [Contact Form](contact-form.md)
    - For email newsletter signups → use [Email Optin](email-optin.md)
    - For user authentication forms → use [Login](login.md)

memories.summary: modules/comments.md: Comments > Overview
memories.solution:
The Comments module gives you complete visual control over the native WordPress comment system. Instead of relying on your theme's default comment template, this module lets you place the comment section anywhere in a layout and style every element — avatars, metadata, reply buttons, the submission form, and the comment count — through the Visual Builder's point-and-click interface.

The module is most commonly used inside Divi Theme Builder templates for blog posts, where it replaces the default comment output with a fully customizable version. It renders both existing comments (threaded with replies) and the "Leave a Reply" form, so visitors can read the conversation and participate without leaving the page.

Because the module pulls from WordPress's built-in comment system, all standard WordPress comment settings still apply. Moderation rules, required fields, comment threading depth, and avatar display preferences configured under **Settings > Discussion** in the WordPress dashboard are respected. The Comments module controls only the visual presentation, not the underlying comment behavior.

For additional reference, see the [official Elegant Themes documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/10260827-the-comments-module-in-divi-5).

[View A Live Demo Of This Module](https://www.16wells.dev/module-demos/comments/)

![Comments module](../assets/screenshots/modules/comments/element.png){ loading=lazy }
*The Comments module as it appears on the live demo.*

memories.summary: modules/comments.md: Comments > Use Cases
memories.solution:
1. **Custom Blog Post Templates** — Place the Comments module in a Theme Builder post template to control exactly where the comment section appears relative to the post content, author bio, and related posts.
2. **Product Feedback Pages** — Add a comment section to product or portfolio pages to collect user reviews and questions directly on the page, styled to match the site's design.
3. **Event Discussion Boards** — Enable comments on event pages so attendees can ask questions, share logistics, or coordinate before and after the event.

memories.solution: The Comments module settings are organized across three tabs: Content, Design, and Advanced.

memories.summary: modules/comments.md: Comments > Settings & Options > Content Tab
memories.solution:
The Content tab controls which comment elements are visible, along with linking, background, and layout options.

| Setting | Type | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| Show Author Avatar | toggle | Display or hide the commenter's avatar image next to each comment. Avatars are pulled from Gravatar based on the commenter's email address. |
| Show Reply Button | toggle | Display or hide the "Reply" link beneath each comment. Disabling this removes the ability for visitors to post threaded replies to specific comments. |
| Show Comment Count | toggle | Display or hide the total number of comments shown above the comment list (e.g., "3 Comments"). |
| Show Comment Meta | toggle | Display or hide the metadata line on each comment, which typically includes the commenter's name and the date/time of the comment. |
| Link | url | Optionally link the entire module to a URL, making the comment area clickable. |
| Background | background controls | Set a background color, gradient, image, or video behind the entire comments module. |
| Loop | toggle | Connect the module to the loop builder for dynamic templates that repeat across posts or custom post types. |
| Order | select | Control the module's display order when the parent row uses Flexbox or Grid layout modes. |
| Meta | admin label | Assign an admin label visible only in the Visual Builder to identify this module in the layers panel. |
