memories.summary: Module content management via REST API requires caution.
memories.solution:
Modifying existing modules using `wp.apiFetch` PATCH updates title, body text, and settings attributes. Creating new modules via REST API renders on the front end but may not appear in the Visual Builder layer view; use browser automation (e.g., Playwright) for reliable creation.

**General Module Operations:**
*   **Read content:** Parse `post_content` block JSON using a brace-depth parser.
*   **Modify existing:** Use `wp.apiFetch` PATCH on the post endpoint to update attributes in `post_content`.
*   **Create new:** Browser automation (Playwright) is recommended due to REST API limitations regarding Visual Builder visibility.
*   **Batch modify:** Sequential REST requests are required.

**Module-Specific Block Identifiers & Attributes:**

*   **Person Module (`divi/person`):**
    *   Attributes: `attrs.name`, `attrs.position`, `attrs.content`, `attrs.image_url`, `attrs.facebook_url`, `attrs.twitter_url`, `attrs.linkedin_url`.
    *   Guidance: Use Person for team member profiles with social links; use Blurb for general icon+text cards; use Testimonial for customer quotes.

*   **Portfolio Module (`divi/portfolio`):**
    *   Attributes: `attrs.posts_number`, `attrs.include_categories`, `attrs.fullwidth`.
    *   Guidance: Use Portfolio for project grids; use Filterable Portfolio for filterable grids; use Fullwidth Portfolio for edge-to-edge display.

*   **Post Navigation Module (`divi/post-navigation`):**
    *   Attributes: `attrs.show_prev`, `attrs.show_next`, `attrs.in_same_cat`.
    *   Guidance: Use Post Navigation for prev/next post links in Theme Builder templates; use Pagination for numbered pagination.

*   **Post Slider Module (`divi/post-slider`):**
    *   Attributes: `attrs.posts_number`, `attrs.include_categories`, `attrs.show_meta`.
    *   Guidance: Use Post Slider for dynamic post-based slideshows; use Slider for static slide content; use Blog for post grids.

*   **Post Title Module (`divi/post-title`):**
    *   Attributes: `attrs.title`, `attrs.meta`, `attrs.author`, `attrs.date`, `attrs.featured_image`.
    *   Guidance: Use Post Title for displaying post metadata in Theme Builder templates; use Heading or Text for static headings.

*   **Post Carousel Module (`divi/post-carousel`), Post Content Module (`divi/post-content`), Woo Checkout Payment Module (`divi/woo-checkout-payment`):** These modules have defined operation methods and attributes, but their block identifiers and operational statuses require verification. For Post Carousel, use it for a compact multi-post carousel; for a fullscreen single-post slideshow use Post Slider; for a traditional blog feed with excerpts use Blog; for a manual content slider use Slider.

*   **Remaining Modules:** The following modules (`divi/post-carousel`, `divi/post-content`, `divi/woo-checkout-payment`) have operation methods and attributes, but their block identifiers and operational statuses require verification.

memories.summary: modules/post-content.md: Post Content
memories.solution:
The Post Content module renders the full body content of a WordPress post or page within Theme Builder templates, including all text, images, embeds, and formatting from the post editor.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What it does:** Dynamically displays the main content body of the current post or page in a Theme Builder template.
    **When to use it:** Theme Builder templates for blog posts, pages, and custom post types
    **Key settings:** Heading Text, Body Text, Image, Background
    **Block identifier:** `divi/post-content`
    **ET Docs:** [Official documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/10587147)

!!! tip "When to Use This Module"
    - Building a Theme Builder template for blog posts that needs to display the post body content
    - Creating custom single-post layouts where the content area is styled separately from other elements
    - Designing page templates that render the WordPress editor content dynamically

!!! warning "When NOT to Use This Module"
    - For static text content authored directly in the Visual Builder — use [Text](text.md)
    - For displaying only the post title — use [Post Title](post-title.md)
    - For displaying the post comments section — use [Comments](comments.md)

memories.summary: modules/post-content.md: Post Content > Overview
memories.solution:
The Post Content module is an essential building block for any Theme Builder template. When you create a custom template for blog posts, pages, or custom post types in the Divi Theme Builder, the actual content authored in the WordPress editor needs a designated place to render. The Post Content module provides that outlet — it dynamically pulls the full body content from whatever post or page is being viewed and displays it within the template layout.

The content rendered by this module includes everything written in the WordPress block editor or classic editor: paragraphs, headings, lists, images, videos, embedded content, shortcodes, and any HTML markup. The module acts as a transparent passthrough that respects the formatting and structure of the original content while allowing you to apply consistent styling through the Design tab settings.

The Design tab offers controls for heading text and body text styling, which apply uniformly to all headings and body paragraphs within the rendered content. Image styling controls let you apply borders, shadows, or other visual treatments to images embedded in the post content. This is particularly useful for enforcing consistent visual standards across all posts without needing to style each one individually.

For additional reference, see the [official Elegant Themes documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/10587147).

<!-- ![Post Content module](../assets/screenshots/modules/post-content/element.png){ loading=lazy } -->
<!-- *The Post Content module rendering a blog post's body text, headings, and images within a Theme Builder template.* -->

memories.summary: modules/post-content.md: Post Content > Use Cases
memories.solution:
1. **Blog Post Template** — Place the Post Content module between the Post Title and Comments modules in a Theme Builder blog post template to create the standard reading layout where the main article content flows naturally between the header and discussion sections.
2. **Custom Page Template** — Use the module in a page template to render page content within a custom layout that includes a sidebar, header, footer, or other design elements not possible with the standard page builder approach.
3. **CPT Detail Template** — For custom post types (events, team members, recipes, etc.), the Post Content module renders whatever content was entered in the WordPress editor, allowing you to build a consistent detail page template while authors fill in the content through the standard editing interface.

memories.solution:

2. Open the Visual Builder on the template.
3. Click the gray **+** icon to add a new module to a row.
4. Search for "Post Content" in the module picker, then click to insert it.

For an animated walkthrough of adding and configuring this module, see the
[official Elegant Themes documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/10587147).

memories.summary: Post Slider dynamically generates interactive slideshows from published posts.
memories.solution:
The Post Slider module transforms WordPress posts into dynamic, query-generated slideshows. Each slide can display a post's featured image (as background or alongside text), title, excerpt, author, date, and an optional read-more button.

**Functionality & Use Cases:**
*   **Dynamic Content:** New content appears automatically upon publication.
*   **Use Cases:** Ideal for blog hero sections, homepage spotlights (limiting posts to 3-5), or focused category carousels.

**Settings Breakdown:**
*   **Content Tab:** Controls post selection and slide elements:
    *   `Number of Posts`: Max slides/posts in rotation.
    *   `Post Categories`: Filters posts; selecting none includes all published posts.
    *   `Read More Button`: Customizable text (default: "Read More"); toggle to remove the button entirely.
    *   `Sorting Method`: Controls post order (e.g., date descending/ascending).
    *   `Navigation Arrows`/`Bullet Navigation`: Toggles for manual slide advancement controls.
    *   `Post Meta`: Toggle to show/hide metadata (author, date, categories).
    *   `Featured Image`: Toggle determines if the featured image is used as a background or displayed alongside content.
    *   `Featured Image Placement`: Selects placement: full background overlay or side-by-side with text.
    *   `Link`: Makes the entire module wrapper clickable to a specified URL.
    *   `Background`: Fallback setting (color, gradient, image, video) visible when slides lack featured images.
    *   `Order`/`Meta`: Controls display order and custom admin label.
*   **Design Tab:** Provides visual control over the slider's appearance:
    *   `Overlay`: Configures background overlay color/opacity for text readability.
    *   `Navigation`: Customizes arrow controls and dot indicators (color, size, hover states).
*   **Advanced Tab:** Offers developer-oriented controls:
    *   Includes options groups like `Attributes`, `CSS`, `Conditions`, `Interactions`, `Visibility`, `Transitions`, `Position`, and `Scroll Effects`.

**Best Practices & Patterns:**
*   **Full-Screen Hero Slider:** Set min-height to 80vh or higher, use featured image as background, apply a dark overlay, and enable both navigation types for maximum user control.
*   **Compact Featured Posts Bar:** Use reduced min-height (250-300px) and limit posts (3-4). Disable post meta and body text to create a clean teaser.
*   **Category News Ticker:** Filter by one category, enable auto-advance with short interval, and use solid background colors instead of featured images for an editorial look.

**Troubleshooting & Gotchas:**
*   **No Slides:** Verify published posts have assigned featured images, the category filter is not empty, and `Number of Posts` > 0. Use a fallback background if posts lack featured images.
*   **Poor Readability:** If using light-colored featured images, use the Design tab's Overlay or add text shadows to titles/body for contrast.
*   **Inconsistent Height:** Set a fixed min-height in Sizing settings to prevent layout shifts between slides of varying content lengths.

memories.summary: Controls post title presentation across various content types and templates.
memories.solution:
The Post Title module allows precise control over the display of a post's title, metadata (author, date, comment count), and featured image. It is primarily used in Divi Theme Builder templates but works with any post type that has these elements (e.g., pages, custom posts, products). 

**Key Functionality:**
*   **Elements:** Individual toggles control the visibility of Title, Meta line, Author, Publish Date, Comment Count, and Featured Image.
*   **Context:** When placed in a post body template, it dynamically pulls data from the viewed post. It also supports the Divi loop system for repeating content structures.
*   **Customization:** The module offers comprehensive styling options across three tabs: Content, Design, and Advanced.

**Content Tab Controls:**
*   `Show Title`: Primary toggle for displaying the dynamic post title.
*   `Show Meta`: Master toggle controlling the visibility of the entire metadata line. Individual toggles (`Show Author`, `Show Publish Date`, `Show Comments Count`) only function when `Show Meta` is enabled.
*   `Loop`: Enables use within repeating content structures, sourcing data from the current loop item.
*   `Link`: Makes the entire module wrapper clickable and allows defining link behavior (same/new tab).
*   `Background`: Sets background color, gradient, image, or video for the container.

**Design Tab Controls:**
*   Provides shared options groups for visual styling of all elements: `Text`, `Title Text`, `Meta Text`, `Sizing`, `Spacing`, `Border`, `Box Shadow`, `Filters`, `Transform`, and `Animation`.

memories.summary: Displays service/product pricing in structured, comparative column formats.
memories.solution:
The Pricing Table module presents multiple plan tiers (e.g., Basic, Pro, Enterprise) side-by-side for comparing services, SaaS plans, or membership levels. Each table includes dedicated fields for a plan title, subtitle, price (with currency/frequency), feature list, and CTA button.

Key features include:
*   **Featured Table:** Visually highlights a recommended plan using distinct styling (e.g., different background color, drop shadow) to guide conversions.
*   **Feature Lists:** Supports bullet points; excluded items can be marked with strikethrough styling for clear comparison.
*   **Layout:** Multiple tables can be placed in a row for direct comparison.

Configuration details:
*   **Content Tab (Repeater):** Defines individual table data, including title, subtitle, price, currency, frequency, feature list, button text/URL, and the `featured` toggle.
*   **Design Tab:** Controls visual presentation. Specific typography groups exist for Subtitle Text, Price Text, Currency/Frequency Text, and Excluded Item Text. Styling options include Background Color/Gradient/Image/Video/Pattern/Mask, Show Drop Shadow (for featured tables), and controlling bullet point colors (Featured vs. Standard).
*   **Advanced Tab:** Allows fine-grained control via CSS ID, custom classes, conditional display logic (`Conditions`), interactions, visibility toggles, and scroll effects.

Use cases include SaaS subscriptions, service package pricing, and membership level comparisons. For advanced styling, custom CSS can be applied (e.g., `.et_pb_pricing_table.et_pb_featured_table { border-top: 4px solid #2ea3f2; transform: scale(1.05); }`).

memories.summary: Module content manipulation via REST API requires caution.
memories.solution:
Modifying existing module content using `wp.apiFetch` PATCH updates title, body text, and settings attributes. Creating new modules via REST API renders on the front end but may not appear in the Visual Builder layer view; use browser automation (e.g., Playwright) for reliable creation.

**General Module Operations:**
*   **Read content:** Parse `post_content` block JSON using a brace-depth parser.
*   **Modify existing:** Use `wp.apiFetch` PATCH on the post endpoint to update block attributes in `post_content`.
*   **Create new:** Browser automation (Playwright) is recommended for reliable creation, as REST creation may break Visual Builder visibility.
*   **Batch modify:** Requires sequential REST requests.

**Module-Specific Identifiers & Attributes:**

*   **Pricing Table (`divi/pricing-tables`):**
    *   Title: `attrs.title` (Plan name)
    *   Subtitle: `attrs.subtitle` (Plan description or tagline)
    *   Currency: `attrs.currency` (Currency symbol)
    *   Per: `attrs.per` (Billing frequency label)
    *   Price: `attrs.sum` (Numeric price value)
    *   Button Text: `attrs.button_text` (CTA button label)
    *   Button URL: `attrs.button_url` (CTA button destination)
    *   Features: Child items
*   **Search (`divi/search`):**
    *   Placeholder: `attrs.placeholder` (Input field placeholder text)
    *   Show Button: `attrs.show_button` (Toggle search submit button visibility)
*   **Shop (`divi/shop`):**
    *   Type: `attrs.type` (Product query type, e.g., recent, featured, sale)
    *   Posts Number: `attrs.posts_number` (Maximum products to display)
    *   Columns: `attrs.columns_number` (Number of grid columns)
    *   Orderby: `attrs.orderby` (Sort order field)
*   **Sidebar (`divi/sidebar`):**
    *   Area: `attrs.area` (Registered widget area to display)
    *   Orientation: `attrs.orientation` (Separator position or layout orientation)
*   **Slider (`divi/slider`):**
    *   Child slides: Nested blocks (Each slide has heading, body, button, and image attributes)
*   **Social Media Follow (`divi/social-media-follow`):**
    *   Child network items: Nested blocks (Each item has network type and profile URL)
*   **Tabs (`divi/tabs`):**
    *   Child tab items: Nested blocks (Each tab has title and content attributes)
*   **Woo Cart Totals (`divi/woo-cart-totals`):**
    *   No specific key attributes listed, but read/modify operations require testing.

**Module Selection Guidance:**
*   **Pricing Table:** Use for side-by-side plan comparisons. (Use Call to Action for single CTA blocks; Blurb or Toggle for feature lists.)
*   **Search:** Use for site search functionality. (Use Menu for navigation; Sidebar for widget-based search.)
*   **Shop:** Use for WooCommerce product grids. (Use Blog or Portfolio for general post grids.)
*   **Sidebar:** Use for displaying WordPress widget areas. (Use Menu for custom navigation; Search for search functionality.)
*   **Slider:** Use for static content slideshows. (Use Post Slider for post-based slideshows; Fullwidth Slider for edge-to-edge sliders; Video Slider for video collections.)
*   **Social Media Follow:** Use for social media profile links. (Use Person for team profiles with social links; Icon for standalone icons.)
*   **Tabs:** Use for horizontal tabbed content. (Use Accordion for vertical collapsible content; Toggle for independent collapsible items.)

memories.summary: Troubleshooting common issues with featured and misaligned pricing tables.
memories.solution:
### Featured Table Issues
If the featured table blends in, ensure:
- The **Featured** toggle is enabled on the correct Content tab item.
- In the Design tab > Layout, **Show Drop Shadow** is enabled.
- The background color differs from standard tables.
- Custom CSS isn't overriding default styles.

### Alignment Issues (Stacking Vertically)
If tables stack instead of aligning side by side:
- Ensure the parent row has sufficient columns or uses a Flexbox/Grid layout.
- Verify the module width in Sizing settings is not set to 100%.
- Note that on tablet and mobile, tables will stack vertically by default for readability.

memories.summary: Troubleshooting product display issues with Shop/Product modules.
memories.solution:
For any WooCommerce module (Shop, Add to Cart, Breadcrumbs), ensure WooCommerce is installed and activated.

**No Products Displaying:** Verify that at least one published product exists in WooCommerce. Check that the product status is 'Published' (not Draft). For Shop/Product modules, confirm the Include Categories filter is not empty, and the Type filter matches your data (e.g., 'Featured Products' requires products to be marked as featured).

**Add to Cart Button Issues:** If the button fails, check for JavaScript conflicts. Open the browser developer console for errors. Ensure WooCommerce AJAX add-to-cart is enabled under `WooCommerce > Settings > Products`. Note that variable product buttons may redirect to the product page instead of adding directly to the cart.

**Module Not Rendering/Displaying:** The module must be placed on a product page template (not a regular page) and assigned to a valid, published product. For breadcrumbs, ensure the product has at least one category assigned; otherwise, minimal or empty trails may appear.

memories.summary: Using Woo Cart Products for custom cart layouts.
memories.solution:
The `divi/woo-cart-products` module renders the main WooCommerce cart table (items, images, quantities, prices). It is designed exclusively for use within a Theme Builder template assigned to the WooCommerce cart page.

**Functionality:** The module allows customers to view items, update quantities, apply coupon codes, and remove items directly from the table. Customization options include toggling visibility for product images, coupon fields, update buttons, and removal icons. It pairs with `Woo Cart Totals` and `Woo Cross Sells` modules to replace the default cart page.

**Design & Layout:** The module offers extensive styling control via three tabs (Content, Design, Advanced). Key design options include:
*   **Layout:** Choose between Horizontal (default table) or Vertical (card-based, better for mobile).
*   **Styling Controls:** Customize the appearance of the Table Header, Body Text, individual Rows/Cells, Images, Coupon Fields, and Buttons.
*   **Advanced Options:** Utilize shared design options like `Text`, `Sizing`, `Spacing`, `Border`, `Box Shadow`, etc., for granular control. The module supports saving configurations as presets or adding them to the Divi Library.

**Use Cases:** It can be used to create custom branded cart pages, minimal layouts (by hiding images/coupons), or two-column designs (placing it alongside totals in a sidebar).

memories.summary: The Sidebar module integrates WordPress widgets into Divi layouts.
memories.solution:
The Sidebar module bridges the Divi Visual Builder with the traditional WordPress widget system, allowing placement of any registered widget area (e.g., categories, recent posts, custom menus) into page layouts. Widget areas are managed via Appearance > Widgets; changes reflect globally.

**Usage:**
*   **Blog Layout:** Place alongside Post Content for a two-column layout with widgets (recent posts, search).
*   **Footer/Custom Templates:** Use in Theme Builder or footer columns to display widget content without coding.

**Implementation Steps:**
1.  Insert the module via Visual Builder (+) and search for 'Sidebar'.
2.  In the Content tab, select the desired registered WordPress widget area from the 'Widget Area' dropdown.
3.  Use the Design tab to adjust separator position, title, and body typography. 

**Configuration Options:**
*   **Content Tab:** Allows selection of the `Widget Area`. Also supports module-level linking (URL, target) and background styling (color, gradient, image, video, pattern, mask). Includes toggles for `Enable Loop` (dynamic content generation) and `Order` (Flexbox/Grid placement).
*   **Design Tab:** Controls visual layout. Key setting is `Separator Position` (select: top, bottom, hidden). Typography settings allow independent control over title and body text styling.
*   **Advanced Tab:** Provides comprehensive controls including CSS ID/classes (`Attributes`), custom CSS per element target (`CSS`), display rules (`Conditions`), device visibility toggles (`Visibility`), positioning (`Position`), scroll effects, and interactions.

memories.summary: Testimonial display patterns: grids, featured quotes, and rotators.
memories.solution:
For a **Testimonial Grid**, place three Testimonial modules in a three-column row. Apply white background, rounded corners, consistent padding, subtle box shadow, and uniform image sizing to each card.

For a **Featured Quote with Background**, use a single Testimonial module in a full-width row. Set a dark background color or image for the section, switch text colors to light, increase body font size, and center-align all text.

For **Rotating Testimonials**, either place individual testimonials on each slide using the Slider module, or stack multiple toggles in one column and use conditional display logic/JavaScript for automatic cycling.

*Minimal Testimonial Rotator:* To create a typography-focused rotator without background images, set slides to use a solid background color. Set the slide heading to the customer name and the body text to their quote. Leave button fields empty and reduce vertical padding while center-aligning the text.

memories.summary: Displays linked social media icons for profiles across multiple platforms.
memories.solution:
The Social Media Follow module displays a row of customizable social media icons, linking visitors to specified profiles on various platforms (e.g., Facebook, Twitter/X, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, Pinterest, TikTok). 

**Usage:** Ideal for site footers, author bio sections, and contact pages.

**Configuration:**
*   **Social Networks (Repeater):** Manages individual network items. Each item requires a selected `Social Network` (determining default icon/brand color) and the full `Profile URL`. 
*   **Icon Settings (Parent Level):** Controls global settings like `Link Target`, which dictates if all profile links open **In The Same Window** (default) or **In A New Tab**. Individual items do not override this.
*   **Design:** Allows setting horizontal `Alignment` (left, center, right), customizing the overall `Icon` appearance (color, size, hover state), and styling optional `Follow Button` containers. 
*   **Advanced/CSS:** Supports custom CSS targeting (`.et_pb_social_media_follow li a`) for advanced styling (e.g., monochrome look, circular shapes) and PHP filters to programmatically add attributes like `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

**Module Identifier:** `divi/social-media-follow`

memories.summary: Social Media Follow module settings for controlling link targets and appearance.
memories.solution:
**Fixing Link Target (Module)**:
1. Open the page in the **Visual Builder**. 
2. Click a social icon, then use the breadcrumb to navigate back to the parent **Social Media Follow** module settings (e.g., `Footer › Section › Row › Column › … › Social Network`).
3. In the **Content** tab, expand the **Icon** section on the **parent** module.
4. Set **Link Target** to **In A New Tab**. This setting applies globally to all icons in that instance.

**Global Scope**: If the module is used across multiple pages (e.g., global header/footer), edit the global template once to apply the change site-wide. 

**Conflict Resolution**: If both Theme Options icons and a Social Media Follow module appear on the same page, it is recommended to keep the module (more flexible) and clear the social URLs under **Divi → Theme Options → General**.

**Troubleshooting:**
*   **Icons Not Linking**: Verify that the **Profile URL** field contains a complete, publicly accessible URL including `https://`.
*   **Icon Colors/Alignment**: Check for custom CSS or module overrides. Review the icon color settings at the module level and check the column's alignment setting if icons are misaligned.

memories.summary: Organizes content into switchable panels for comparison or detailed viewing.
memories.solution:
The Tabs module groups related content into distinct, switchable panels using clickable headers. Only one panel is visible at a time, keeping the layout compact and allowing presentation of significant information without excessive scrolling.

**Use Cases:**
*   Product Specifications: Presenting details like description, specs, reviews, or shipping in separate tabs for quick comparison.
*   Service Tiers/Pricing Plans: Displaying multiple pricing options or service levels to allow visitors to compare them by switching panels.
*   Categorized Content Blocks: Organizing resource sections (e.g., tutorials, documentation) where each tab represents a different content category.
*   Location/Branch Selector: Presenting information for various office locations or store branches in one compact section.
*   Comparison View: Toggling between two states or options (e.g., 'Before'/'After', 'Plan A'/'Plan B') when seeing them one at a time is clearer than side-by-side.

**Structure & Settings:**
*   **Content Tab:** Manages individual tab items and module links/metadata.
    *   `Tabs (Repeater)`: Used to add, edit, delete, or reorder individual tabs. Each item requires a `Title` (the clickable header label) and `Content` (rich text body supporting HTML, images, lists, etc.).
    *   Other settings include linking the entire module (`Link`), setting a background (`Background`), controlling repetition (`Loop`), display order (`Order`), and internal identification (`Meta`).
*   **Design Tab:** Controls visual styling for headers, content, and overall layout.
    *   `Tab Text`: Allows independent styling (font family, size, color, etc.) for active and inactive tab headers.
    *   Shared options groups control general appearance: `Body Text`, `Sizing`, `Spacing`, `Border`, `Box Shadow`, `Filters`, `Transform`, and `Animation`. These settings apply to the module container or individual panels.
*   **Advanced Tab:** Provides low-level controls for custom attributes, CSS targeting, and dynamic display logic.
    *   Options include: `Attributes` (CSS ID, classes, custom HTML attributes), `CSS` (custom CSS per element target: headers, active header, content area, individual panels), `Conditions` (display rules based on user role, page type, etc.), `Visibility` (device-specific toggles), `Transitions`, `Position`, and `Scroll Effects`.

**Behavior:**
*   Headers display horizontally in wide columns but automatically stack vertically in narrow columns for accessibility. Only one panel is visible at any time.

**Comparison to other modules:**
*   **Accordion:** Tabs present all headers simultaneously in a row (instant access), while Accordions stack headers vertically with expand/collapse behavior. Use tabs when frequent comparison or switching between sections is needed; use accordions for sequential or FAQ-style content.
*   **Toggle:** Used for independently collapsible items that can all be open at once.

memories.summary: The Testimonial module displays structured social proof (quotes/reviews) with author details.
memories.solution:
The Testimonial module is designed to present customer quotes and endorsements. Each testimonial includes a quote body, author image, author name, job title, company attribution, and an optional decorative quote icon.

**Usage & Placement:**
- **Social Proof:** Ideal for displaying customer reviews, featured endorsements, or case study highlights near CTAs/pricing to build trust (third-party validation).
- **Layouts:** Supports single featured quotes (full-width) or multi-column grids of reviews.
- **Integration:** Can be paired with Blurb or Text modules when attributing a quote to a specific project or result.

**Key Elements & Settings:**
- **Content Fields:** Author Name, Job Title, Company, Body (quote text), Image (portrait/headshot).
- **Structural Controls:** Supports both portrait and landscape orientations. Allows toggling individual elements on/off.
- **Advanced Styling:** Provides granular typography controls for every element (Author Text, Position Text, Company Text, Body Text). Includes options for background styling (color, gradient, image, video, pattern, mask), sizing, spacing, border, box shadow, filters, transform, and animation.
- **Functionality:** Can be made entirely clickable via `Module Link URL` to direct users to another page or section. Supports dynamic content connections (`Dynamic Content` toggle).

**Technical Identifiers:**
- **Block Identifier:** `divi/testimonial`
- **Primary CSS Selectors (Examples):** `.et_pb_testimonial`, `.et_pb_testimonial_description`, `.et_pb_testimonial_portrait`
- **PHP Hook Example:** `add_filter( 'et_module_shortcode_output', 'add_testimonial_stars', 10, 2 );`

memories.summary: REST API module creation vs modification rules.
memories.solution:
Modifying existing modules via REST API (`wp.apiFetch` PATCH) updates title, body text, and settings attributes.
**Creating new modules via REST API** produces content that renders on the front end but may not appear in the Visual Builder layer view. For reliable module creation, use browser automation (e.g., Playwright).

Read operations for all modules involve parsing `post_content` block JSON using a brace-depth parser.

The following modules have associated content attributes and identifiers:
*   **Testimonial Module:** Block identifier: `divi/testimonial`. Attributes include `attrs.author`, `attrs.job_title`, `attrs.company_name`, `attrs.content` (Body), and `attrs.portrait_url`.
*   **Text Module:** Block identifier: `divi/text`. Attribute includes `attrs.content` (Body, rich text content).
*   **Toggle Module:** Block identifier: `divi/toggle`. Attributes include `attrs.title`, `attrs.content` (Collapsible body), and `attrs.open`.
*   **Video Slider:** Block identifier: `divi/video-slider`. Contains nested blocks for child video items, each needing a video URL and overlay image.
*   **Video Module:** Block identifier: `divi/video`. Attributes include `attrs.src` (Primary video source), `attrs.src_webm` (WebM alternative), and `attrs.image_src` (Overlay thumbnail).
*   **Woo Add to Cart:** Block identifier: `divi/wc-add-to-cart`. No specific attributes listed.
*   **Woo Breadcrumbs:** Block identifier: `divi/woo-breadcrumbs`. No specific attributes listed.
*   **Woo Cart Products:** Block identifier: `divi/woo-cart-products`. No specific attributes listed.

memories.summary: The Text module is a versatile content block providing rich editing for structured or raw HTML content.
memories.solution:
The Text module (`divi/text`) is Divi's core content block, offering a full-featured visual editor and raw HTML mode for adding paragraphs, headings (H1-H6), lists, links, and custom markup to any page. It imposes no structural constraints, making it the default choice for general content that doesn't require a dedicated module layout.

**Use Cases:**
*   **Long-Form Content:** Ideal for article-style writing; set max-width (700-800px) and center to optimize reading experience.
*   **HTML Embeds/Custom Markup:** Accepts raw HTML, making it useful for embedding third-party widgets, forms, iframes, or script-based content lacking a dedicated module.
*   **Styled Typography:** Allows combining headings, body text, and lists in one block with distinct typography settings applied to each element.

**Settings & Controls:**
*   **Content Tab:** Contains the main `Body` editor (rich text/HTML). Also includes controls for making the entire module a clickable link (`Module Link URL`, `Module Link Target`), background styling (color, gradient, image, video, pattern, mask), and layout control (`Module Order`).
*   **Design Tab:** Provides granular typography and visual styling. Settings are split into: 
    *   **Heading-specific:** Font, size, color, letter spacing, line height, shadow.
    *   **Body Text:** Typography settings for paragraph text.
    *   **Shared Options Groups:** Controls for overall module appearance (e.g., `Text` options group handles font/color/alignment; `Sizing` controls width/max-width; `Spacing` manages margins/padding; `Border`, `Box Shadow`, `Filters`, `Transform`, and `Animation`).

**Related Modules:**
*   Use **Blurb** for pairing text with an icon or image (feature blocks).
*   Use **Heading** for standalone section titles.
*   Use **Code** for raw code (CSS/JS) that should bypass the visual editor.

**Troubleshooting:**
*   **Content Disappearing:** If content vanishes in the Visual Builder, check for unclosed HTML tags; switch to text/HTML view to fix malformed markup.
*   **Typography Not Applying:** Confirm the correct typography group (Heading Text vs. Body Text) is being edited. Check for conflicting styles from child themes or plugins with higher CSS specificity. Clear all caching layers (plugin, server, browser).
*   **Dynamic Content Failure:** Verify the dynamic content source contains data and that Loop settings are correctly configured, ensuring exact field name matching.

memories.summary: The Breadcrumbs Module provides hierarchical navigation and SEO structure.
memories.solution:
The Divi **Breadcrumbs Module** displays a clickable trail showing the current page's location within the site hierarchy (e.g., Home → Blog → Category → Post). It aids visitor orientation, allows easy navigation up the content hierarchy, and signals clear content structure to search engines.

**Usage & Placement:**
*   For general use, place it in a **[Theme Builder](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12022773-build-custom-templates-using-the-theme-builder-in-divi-5)** header to display the trail on every page.
*   For WooCommerce product pages, use the **[Woo Breadcrumbs Module](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12032985-the-woo-breadcrumbs-module-in-divi-5)** instead of the standard module.

**Adding the Module:**
When in the Visual Builder, click the **Green Plus** icon to insert a **[Row](https://intercom.help/elegantthemes/en/articles/10316106-the-divi-row)**, then click the **Gray Plus** icon inside it and select the **Breadcrumbs module**.

**Settings Tabs:**
The module settings are divided into three tabs: **Content**, **Design**, and **Advanced**.

*   **Content Tab:** Configures shared options like the home item's text and link, separator character (e.g., `/**`, `**>**`), and general background/link behavior. Settings include:
    *   `Home Text`: Label for the first trail item (defaults to "Home"). Supports [Dynamic Content](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/13627810-advanced-content-management-using-dynamic-content-in-divi-5).
    *   `Home URL`: Destination for the first item (defaults to site's home page). Supports [Dynamic Content](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/13627810-advanced-content-management-using-dynamic-content-in-divi-5).
    *   `Separator`: Character between items (e.g., `/**`, `**>**`, `**\|**`).
    *   `[Link]`: Makes the entire module clickable, directing users to a specified page/section/URL.
    *   `[Elements]`: Toggles optional pieces of the trail on or off.
    *   `[Background]`: Sets background color, gradient, image, video, or pattern.
    *   `[Loop]`: Enables repetition across multiple items.
    *   `[Meta]`: Sets the module's label and forces visibility while editing.

*   **Design Tab:** Controls the visual styling of the four sub-elements: **Breadcrumb**, **Breadcrumb link**, **Home link**, and **Separator**. Each element exposes standard Divi 5 Composable Settings (Background, Text, Sizing, Spacing, Border, Box Shadow). Advanced options include:
    *   `Layout`: Selects the visual style and item alignment.
    *   `[Sizing]`, `[Spacing]`, `[Border]`, `[Box Shadow]`:
        *   Control overall module dimensions/padding/borders.
    *   Additional Groups: `[Filters]`, `[Transform]`, `[Animation]` (for visual effects).

*   **Advanced Tab:** Provides deep control for experienced designers, including:
    *   `[Attributes]`: Assigns CSS ID, reusable classes, or custom HTML attributes.
    *   `[CSS]`: Allows adding custom CSS.
    *   `[HTML]`: Selects the semantic wrapper tag (e.g., **nav** or **div**).
    *   `[Conditions]`: Shows/hides based on criteria (status, category, date).
    *   `[Interactions]`: Triggers custom behaviors upon element interaction.
    *   `[Visibility]`: Hides the module based on device (phone, tablet, desktop).
    *   `[Transitions]`: Sets animation duration for hover/state changes.
    *   `[Position]`: Pins or positions the module relative to its container.
    *   `[Scroll Effects]`: Animates the module during scrolling.

**Development Notes:**
*   Custom CSS can be targeted using `/* TODO: Add CSS targeting .et_pb_breadcrumbs for custom styling */`.
*   PHP filters are available for manipulating the breadcrumb trail (`// TODO: Add PHP filters for breadcrumb trail manipulation`).

memories.solution:

**Styling Controls:** Dividers (customize color, size, rotation for top/bottom dividers); Sizing (width, height, padding/margin); Spacing (top, bottom, left, right padding and margin); Border (width, color, style, radius); Box Shadow (blur, spread, offset, color); Filters (hue rotation, saturation, brightness, contrast, blur, opacity, blend modes); Transform (scale, rotate, skew, translate); Animation (entrance, loop, exit animations).

memories.summary: Table of Contents module settings for structure and appearance.
memories.solution:
The Table of Contents module in Divi 5 allows users to configure its content, design, and behavior:

**Content Tab:** Determines the source of links (page headings); options include making the entire module clickable (linking to another page/section/external site), adding other Divi modules as nested elements, setting background (color, gradient, image, video), enabling Loop Builder for dynamic content repetition, choosing display order, and setting a label/visibility meta.
**Design Tab:** Controls appearance: Scroll behavior (smooth-scrolling, highlighting active section); Layout (Flexbox or CSS Grid arrangement); Text styling is granularly controlled for the Title Text, List Text, and specific heading levels (Level 1 through Level 6), plus Marker Text and Empty State Text. Also includes standard module controls: Sizing, Spacing, Border, Box Shadow, Filters, Transform, Animation.
**Advanced Tab:** Provides advanced customization: Attributes (CSS ID/classes/custom HTML attributes); CSS (custom code); HTML (semantic tag selection); Conditions (show/hide based on dynamic criteria); Interactions (show/hide on click or hover); Visibility (device-specific control); Transitions (animation duration); Position (precise placement, including sticky positioning); Scroll Effects (scroll-triggered behavior).

memories.summary: Instagram Feed Module settings in Divi 5 (General, Content, Design, Advanced)
memories.solution:
The Instagram Feed Module in Divi 5 has distinct setting tabs:

**1. General Tab:**
*   **Green Plus/Gray Plus Icon:** Used for inserting a row or viewing available Divi modules.
*   **Instagram module:** Click to load the module, or use Search.
*   **Account:** Connects the Instagram account whose posts are displayed.
*   **Feed:** Controls the number of Instagram posts shown.

**2. Content Tab:**
*   **Account:** Used to connect the Instagram account and requires an `Instagram Access token` (obtained via a multi-step process involving Facebook Developers, creating an app, requesting permissions like `instagram_basic`, generating the access token, and copying it). The module uses this token and the provided Account name.
*   **Feed:** Selects how many posts are displayed.
*   **Link:** Makes the entire feed clickable, allowing users to navigate to another page, section, or external site.
*   **Button:** Allows choosing whether to display a 'Follow Us on Instagram' button and setting its text.
*   **Elements:** Specifies which other module should be nested inside the Instagram Feed module.
*   **Background:** Controls background styles for the feed.
*   **Meta:** Sets the Label text and forces its visibility in the Visual Builder.

**3. Design Tab:**
*   **Layout:** Choose between Block and Flexbox layout.
*   **Image:** Styles applied to each image in the feed.
*   **Button:** Styling for the 'Follow us' button.
*   **Feed:** General styling (layout, background, sizing, spacing).
*   **Item:** Styling for individual items/images (background, sizing, spacing).
*   **Sizing / Spacing / Border / Box Shadow / Filters / Transform / Animation:** Advanced design controls for the module's appearance and effects.

**4. Advanced Tab:**
*   **Attributes:** Assign CSS ID, reusable CSS classes, or custom HTML attributes.
*   **CSS:** Add custom CSS.
*   **HTML:** Choose the semantic HTML tag.
*   **Conditions:** Display the module dynamically based on set rules.
*   **Interactions:** Create custom interactions (e.g., showing/hiding Icon List).
*   **Visibility:** Control visibility across different devices.
*   **Transitions:** Set animation duration.
*   **Position:** Precise placement control.
*   **Scroll Effects:** Control module behavior during scrolling.

**Connection Process Summary:** To connect the account, users must go through Facebook Developers to create an app, request permissions (`instagram_basic`), generate a token, and then input this `Instagram Access token` into the Content Tab's Account settings.

memories.summary: The Section is the outermost container; it holds rows and defines full-width page zones.
memories.solution:
The Section (`divi/section`) is the foundational structural element, spanning the full width of a page. It acts as the primary layout foundation, dividing content into distinct horizontal zones (or 'bands').

**Anatomy:** Every section contains:
*   **Container:** The outer wrapper controlling background, borders, spacing, and layout rules.
*   **Rows:** Child elements nested inside the section's layout (uses Flexbox or Grid).
*   **Modules:** Individual content blocks placed inside rows.

**Section Types:**
*   **Regular Section:** Standard type spanning full page width but contains a max-width container to constrain readable content.
*   **Fullwidth Section:** Has no container constraints; child content expands 100% of the browser viewport width (ideal for edge-to-edge backgrounds).
*   **Specialty Section:** Configured with advanced layout controls (Grid) for complex multi-column structures without explicit rows.

**Settings & Options:**
*   **Content Tab:** Allows setting a `Link` (making the section clickable), background (solid color, image, video, gradient), enabling `Loop` builder for dynamic content, and assigning a custom `Meta` label.
*   **Design Tab:** Controls visual aspects like background, spacing, borders, animations, and responsive behavior for all contained elements.

**Common Patterns:**
*   **Hero Section:** Achieved by using a full-width section with a background image/overlay, containing a row that centers text (Heading, Text, Button) within a column.

memories.summary: The Row is the intermediate container; it organizes columns and modules inside a Section.
memories.solution:
The Row (`divi/row`) is the horizontal layout container situated between Sections (full-width) and Columns (modules). It controls column structure, alignment, spacing, and visual styling, defining how content is organized into distinct horizontal bands.

**Anatomy:** Every row consists of:
*   **Container:** The outer wrapper controlling background, spacing, borders, and layout rules for the row itself.
*   **Columns:** Child containers; their number and width are determined by the row's structure.
*   **Modules:** Individual content blocks (Text, Image, Button, etc.) placed inside columns.

**Column Structures:** Rows support multiple built-in configurations:
*   1 Column: Full-width single column.
*   2 Equal Columns: Two columns of equal width.
*   2 Unequal (2/1): Two columns with 2/3 and 1/3 widths.
*   2 Unequal (1/2): Two columns with 1/3 and 2/3 widths.
*   3 Columns: Three columns of equal width.
*   3 Unequal: Three columns with custom width ratios.
*   4 Columns: Four columns of equal width.
*   Specialty Row: Allows multiple column widths for advanced layouts.

**Settings & Options:**
*   **Content Tab:** Includes options to `Change Column Structure` (presets or specialty rows), make the entire row clickable (`Link`), set a background, enable `Loop` builder, control `Order` (for Flexbox/Grid reordering), and assign a custom `Meta` label.
*   **Design Tab:** Controls sizing (width, height, padding), spacing (internal/external margin/padding), borders, box shadow, CSS filters, transforms, animations, and transitions.
*   **Advanced Tab:** Allows adding custom attributes (ID, classes), writing custom `CSS`, changing the semantic `HTML Tag` (`div` default), setting `Conditions` (show/hide based on roles/devices), defining `Interactions` (on scroll/hover), controlling per-device `Visibility`, and managing precise positioning using CSS properties.

memories.summary: The SVG module allows direct placement of vector graphics with native styling control in Divi 5.
memories.solution:
The SVG Module is a new feature introduced in Divi 5, alongside other modules (Timeline, Breadcrumbs, Table of Contents, Instagram Feed). Unlike inserting an SVG as a standard image, this module exposes the source vector's strokes and fills as editable Divi settings, allowing users to restyle the artwork without modifying the original file. 

**Settings:**
*   **Design Tab:** Exposes native controls for `Stroke` and `Stroke Width` styling.
*   **Advanced Tab:** Allows setting a custom HTML ID (`CSS ID`), custom CSS classes (`CSS Class`), and applying specific styles via `Custom CSS`.

**Notes:**
*   This module is exclusive to Divi 5. 
*   For troubleshooting SVG uploads, consult the dedicated guide on WordPress upload-permission setup.

memories.summary: The Tooltip Module provides various ways to display context-sensitive popups.
memories.solution:
The Tooltip module is a feature in Divi 5 used to display contextual content (popups) relative to an anchor element. The target element is defined by the `anchor` setting, which can be any module (button, image, text, icon, etc.). The popup content itself is housed within a child `Tooltip module`. 

**Use Cases:**
*   **Form Field Hints:** Explains expected field input without cluttering forms.
*   **Icon/Image Labels:** Displays captions or short descriptions on hover over an icon or thumbnail.
*   **Definitions/Footnotes:** Surfaces extra context for a term inline, on demand.
*   **Mini Promo Cards:** Shows small rich-content panels (text + modules) next to buttons or products.

**Configuration Settings:**

**1. Content Tab:**
*   **Text:** Edits the popup's content using the rich text editor.
*   **Link:** Makes the entire module linkable (to a page, section, or external URL).
*   **Elements:** Allows adding nested modules to the tooltip.
*   **Background:** Sets the background color, gradient, image, or video. The default is solid black.
*   **Loop:** Repeats content from a data source.
*   **Order:** Controls module order when generated dynamically.
*   **Meta:** Labels the module and enables `Force Visible` (a Builder option) to preview the popup on the canvas during design.

**2. Design Tab:**
*   **Show Tooltip on:** Determines how the tooltip appears:
    *   `Hover`: Shows content when hovering over the target element.
    *   `Click`: Shows content when clicking the target element.
    *   `Always`: Content is always visible, requiring no interaction.
*   **Tooltip Movement:** Controls positioning behavior:
    *   `Anchored`: Default display position (top of the target). Position can be adjusted via `Tooltip Position`.
    *   `Follow Cursor`: The tooltip follows the mouse cursor based on the chosen show option.
*   **Tooltip Position:** Chooses where the tooltip displays relative to the anchor element.
*   **Tooltip Skid:** Shifts the tooltip along the target edge (cross-axis offset).
*   **Tooltip Distance:** Sets the gap from the target along the placement direction (main-axis offset).
*   **Tooltip Open/Close Delay:** Sets the delay before the tooltip opens or closes.
*   **Show Tooltip Arrow:** Displays a small pointer arrow pointing toward the parent module.
*   **Layout:** Controls how child modules inside the tooltip are arranged.
*   **Body Text:** Styles the popup text (font, size, color, spacing).
*   **Sizing:** Sets the popup's width, max width, height, and alignment.
*   **Spacing:** Adjusts padding/margin. Default padding is 3px top/bottom, 6px left/right.
*   **Border:** Adds borders and rounds corners (default radius: 3px).
*   **Box Shadow:** Adds depth with a drop shadow.
*   **Filters:** Applies visual effects (hue, saturation, blend modes).
*   **Transform:** Allows scaling, rotating, skewing, or moving the popup.
*   **Animation:** Adds motion effects upon appearance.

**3. Advanced Tab:**
*   **Attributes:** Assigns CSS ID and classes for custom styling.
*   **HTML:** Adds custom HTML attributes to the module.
*   **Conditions:** Shows or hides the tooltip based on rules (e.g., login status, device).
*   **Interactions:** Triggers actions in response to visitor interaction.
*   **Visibility:** Disables the tooltip on specific screen sizes (`Disabled On`) and controls content overflow.
*   **Transition:** Sets timing and speed for hover transitions.
*   **Position:** Controls placement and the module's `Z-Index` (floats high by default).
*   **Scroll Effects:** Adds scroll-based motion and sticky behavior.

**Technical Details:** The popup is designed to float above other content on a high z-index, ensuring it is never hidden behind other elements.

memories.summary: Creates independently collapsible content panels for FAQs, specs, and guides.
memories.solution:
The Toggle module creates a self-contained, clickable panel with an expandable body area. It is ideal for presenting large amounts of information in a compact format (e.g., FAQ sections, product specifications, step-by-step instructions) where users need to view only specific content subsets. Unlike the Accordion module, multiple toggles can be open simultaneously. 

**Usage:**
1. **Open Visual Builder:** Click the plus icon in a row and search for 'Toggle'.
2. **Configure Content:** Set the clickable `Title` (text) and the collapsible `Body` (rich text). Set the desired default state (`Open State`).
3. **Design Settings:** Control icons, colors, and typography via the Design tab.
4. **Advanced Options (Content Tab):** Supports setting a `Module Link URL` and `Module Link Target`. Also allows defining background styles (color, gradient, image, video, pattern, mask) and module order (`Module Order`).
5. **Design/Appearance:** Customize icons (Open Icon, Close Icon), colors, and typography for both open and closed states.
6. **Best Practices:** Stack multiple toggles in a single column for FAQ pages or progressive disclosure of long content. Set all to `closed` by default for better scanning experience.

memories.summary: Video Slider presents multiple videos in a navigable carousel format.
memories.solution:
The Video Slider module displays multiple videos in a single, space-efficient carousel with clickable thumbnails and navigation arrows. It supports video sources from self-hosted uploads (MP4), YouTube, or Vimeo. The main player area shows the selected video, while a row of thumbnails allows browsing. Each video item can have its own custom overlay image. Key settings include: 

*   **Content Tab:** Manages individual videos (source/upload, overlay image) and global controls like navigation arrows visibility (`Elements` toggle), default overlay image, and background styling. It also includes `Order` for Flexbox/CSS Grid reordering.
*   **Design Tab:** Controls the visual appearance of controls, player area, and overall module style. Shared design options (Sizing, Spacing, Border, Box Shadow, Filters, Transform, Animation) apply to the container.

Block identifier: `divi/video-slider`

Use Cases:
*   **Portfolios:** Showcasing collections of project highlights or testimonials in a compact carousel.
*   **Learning:** Organizing instructional video series (course catalogs).
*   **Product Features:** Presenting multiple feature videos for comprehensive product overviews.

When embedding only one video, use the [Video](video.md) module. For image-based slideshows, use [Slider](slider.md) or [Gallery](gallery.md).

memories.solution:
The Video module embeds a single video player supporting self-hosted files (MP4), YouTube, and Vimeo. It allows for an optional overlay thumbnail and custom play icon styling. Key settings include: 

*   **Content Tab:** Manages the primary video source (URL/upload) and assigns a specific overlay image.
*   **Design Tab:** Controls visual styling of the player area and controls. Shared design options apply to the container.

Block identifier: `divi/video`

Use Cases:

*   Embedding single tutorials or testimonials.

When displaying multiple videos in a carousel, use the [Video Slider](video-slider.md) module.

memories.summary: Video module handles various sources, responsive display, and custom overlays.
memories.solution:
The Video module allows embedding videos via direct file upload (MP4 or supported format) through the media library, or by providing a URL from supported third-party hosts like YouTube or Vimeo. It renders a responsive player that adapts to its parent column width.

**Key Features & Settings:**
*   **Video Source:** Can be uploaded MP4/supported file or a URL (YouTube/Vimeo). The module auto-detects the source type.
*   **Overlay Image:** A static image can be set over the video before playback. Options include uploading a custom image, selecting from the media library, or using **Generate From Video** to automatically create a thumbnail frame.
*   **Display Control:** Includes settings for `Order` (number/select) to control display order in Flexbox/CSS Grid and `Meta` (admin label/visibility) for layer panel identification.

**Design Customization:**
The Design tab controls the visual presentation:
*   **Play Icon:** Customize color, size, and hover state of the play button on the overlay image.
*   **Overlay Styling:** Configure opacity, color tints, or blending effects for the pre-play overlay layer.

**Best Practices & Use Cases:**
The module is suitable for product demonstrations, tutorial content, hero section media, and general embeds. For multiple videos in a navigable carousel, use the [Video Slider](video-slider.md) module instead.

**Performance/Troubleshooting:**
*   Use compressed MP4 files and consider a CDN for self-hosted video to manage load times.
*   Verify embedded URLs are correct and publicly accessible (private/unlisted YouTube videos may fail).
*   Ensure the custom overlay image is actually assigned, and that **Generate From Video** requires an accessible source.

memories.summary: Renders WooCommerce add-to-cart button, quantity field, and stock status on custom product templates.
memories.solution:
The Woo Add to Cart module renders the standard WooCommerce purchasing interface (button, optional quantity selector, and stock status) when placed in a custom single product page template built using the Divi Theme Builder.

**Usage:**
*   **Placement:** Place the module below the price and above the product meta for a conventional e-commerce flow. For variable products, it acts as a configurator.
*   **Product Types:** The output adapts based on the WooCommerce product type (simple, variable, grouped, or external/affiliate).

**Key Settings & Functionality:**
*   **Block Identifier:** `divi/wc-add-to-cart`
*   **Content Tab:** Controls assignment to a specific product and visibility of elements. Options include toggling the quantity field (`Show Quantity Field`) or stock status (`Show Stock`). Optionally, the entire module can be made clickable via a URL link.
*   **Variable Products:** Renders dropdown selectors for each attribute (size, color, etc.). Dedicated styling controls are available for these selectors and their labels.
*   **Design Tab:** Provides granular control over visual elements:
    *   `Button`: Styles the add-to-cart button (background, padding, hover effects).
    *   `Fields`: Customizes the quantity input field appearance.
    *   `Dropdown Menus`: Styles variation selectors.
    *   `Field Labels`: Styles labels above variation dropdowns.
*   **Code Hooks:** The module can be filtered using PHP hooks like `woocommerce_product_single_add_to_cart_text` (to change button text) or `woocommerce_quantity_input_args` (to set min/max quantity).

**Required Context:** Requires WooCommerce to be installed and active. Must be assigned to a valid WooCommerce product.

memories.summary: Displays dynamic WooCommerce breadcrumb navigation on e-commerce pages.
memories.solution:
The Woo Breadcrumbs module renders the navigational path (e.g., Home > Category > Product) dynamically from WooCommerce's category taxonomy, showing customers their location within the store hierarchy.

**Usage:**
*   **When to use:** Product page templates, category archive templates, custom shop layouts.
*   **Required Context:** Requires WooCommerce to be installed and active. Must not be used on non-WooCommerce pages or for general site navigation (use a dedicated plugin).
*   **Block Identifier:** `divi/woo-breadcrumbs`

**Configuration Settings:**
*   **Content Tab:** Controls the data source, including which product's path to display (`Product`), the text and URL for the home link (`Home Text`, `Home Link`), the visual separator character (`Separator`), and background settings.
*   **Design Tab:** Handles visual styling via shared options groups (Text, Sizing, Spacing, Border, Box Shadow, Filters, Transform, Animation). All breadcrumb text styling is managed here.

**Implementation Steps:**
1.  Ensure WooCommerce is active and navigate to the Theme Builder.
2.  Add the module using the Visual Builder on product page templates or category archives.
3.  After configuration, click **Save**. The module can also be saved as a preset in the Divi Library for reuse.

**Customization:**
*   The separator character can be customized via PHP hooks and custom CSS to achieve specific visual styles (e.g., chevron).

memories.summary: Woo Product Images module patterns for standard e-commerce layouts.
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Images module is used in various layout patterns:

1.  **Two-Column Product Hero:** Place the module in a left column (50-60% width) of a two-column row, reserving the right column for stacked elements like the product title, price, rating, short description, and add-to-cart button.
2.  **Full-Width Gallery:** Use the module in a full-width row when displaying products with many gallery images to maximize horizontal space for thumbnails and larger image previews.
3.  **Minimal Product Card:** To create a clean card presentation, hide the gallery thumbnails and sale badge, showing only the featured image. Style this setup with rounded corners and a subtle shadow.

memories.summary: Advanced module settings provide low-level control over display, styling, and behavior.
memories.solution:

*   **CSS**: Apply custom CSS targeting specific elements (e.g., table rows/cells, form fields, stock text).
*   **HTML**: Select the semantic HTML tag for the module wrapper.
*   **Conditions**: Define display rules based on user role, page type, date, or logic.
*   **Interactions**: Control hover, click, or scroll-triggered behaviors.
*   **Visibility**: Toggle visibility based on device (device visibility toggles).
*   **Transitions**: Set hover animation timing.
*   **Position**: Define CSS position and offsets.
*   **Scroll Effects**: Implement scroll-driven animations. 

Specific element targets for CSS vary by module:
*   `woo-cart-products`: table, rows, cells, buttons, images
*   `woo-cart-totals`: table, rows, cells, button, fields
*   `woo-checkout-billing`: form, fields, labels, notices
*   `woo-checkout-details`: table, rows, cells, headings
*   `woo-checkout-information`: heading, label, textarea
*   `woo-checkout-payment`: radio buttons, tooltip, button, form notices
*   `woo-checkout-shipping`: general element targeting
*   `woo-cross-sells`: general element targeting
*   `woo-notice`: general element targeting
*   `woo-product-stock`: stock text, container

memories.summary: Renders WooCommerce billing form fields for custom checkout page design.
memories.solution:
The Woo Checkout Billing module renders the standard WooCommerce billing address form (including first name, last name, company, country/region, street address, city, state/county, postcode/ZIP, phone, and email) on the checkout page. It is designed exclusively for Theme Builder templates assigned to the WooCommerce checkout page.

**Key Functionality:**
*   **Layout Options:** Supports three layouts: `Default` (standard widths), `Fullwidth` (all fields span full width), or `2-Column` (fields arranged in a two-column grid).
*   **Customization:** Allows styling of the billing form via several design options:
    *   **Fields:** Style input elements (border, background color, padding, border radius, focus states).
    *   **Form Notice:** Style validation error messages (background color, text color, border, padding).
    *   **Title Text/Field Labels:** Customize the appearance of headings and label text.
*   **Advanced Settings:** Includes standard module settings like Background, Loop, Order, Meta — Admin Label, and device visibility controls.

**Usage Pattern (Two-Column Compact Checkout):** To create a compact checkout, place this module alongside `Woo Checkout Shipping` in adjacent one-half columns. Set both modules to the `Fullwidth` layout option for optimal field filling.

memories.summary: modules/woo-checkout-billing.md: Woo Checkout Billing > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Billing Fields Not Appearing"
    If the module renders but shows no form fields, verify that the template is assigned to the WooCommerce checkout page in the Theme Builder. The billing form requires the checkout page context to load. Also ensure that WooCommerce is properly configured with at least one payment method and shipping zone.

!!! warning "Validation Errors Not Styled"
    If form validation errors appear with default WooCommerce styling instead of your custom styles, check that you are using the Form Notice design option in the module settings. Custom CSS targeting `.woocommerce-error` may also be needed for full control. Validation styling only appears when a customer attempts to submit the form with missing required fields.

!!! tip "Fields Not Matching on Mobile"
    If form fields zoom in on iOS when tapped, ensure the font size is at least 16px on mobile devices. iOS Safari automatically zooms into inputs with font sizes below 16px. Set this in the responsive settings of the Fields design option or via custom CSS with a media query.

memories.summary: modules/woo-checkout-information.md: Woo Checkout Information
memories.solution:
The Woo Checkout Information module provides a text field for customers to add order notes and special instructions during WooCommerce checkout.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What it does:** Renders the WooCommerce "Additional Information" section with an order notes textarea on the checkout page.

memories.summary: modules/woo-checkout-information.md: Woo Checkout Information > Overview
memories.solution:
The Woo Checkout Information module renders the "Additional Information" section of the WooCommerce checkout page. By default, this section contains a single textarea field labeled "Order Notes" where customers can type special instructions, delivery preferences, gift messages, or any other communication they want to include with their order. The notes are saved to the order and visible to the store administrator in the WooCommerce order details.

The module includes an Elements toggle that lets you show or hide the section title ("Additional Information"). This is useful when you want to integrate the notes field seamlessly into a custom layout without a heading, or when you prefer to add your own heading above the module using a Text or Heading module for more design control.

While the default WooCommerce configuration includes only the order notes field, developers can add additional fields to this section using WooCommerce's `woocommerce_checkout_fields` filter. Any fields added to the "order" field group will appear within this module. For the official Elegant Themes documentation, see the [Woo Checkout Information help article](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12095378).

!!! info "WooCommerce Required"
    This module requires WooCommerce to be installed and active. It will not appear in the module picker without WooCommerce.

memories.summary: modules/woo-checkout-information.md: Woo Checkout Information > Use Cases
memories.solution:
1. **Delivery Instructions** — Allow customers to specify delivery details like gate codes, preferred delivery times, or instructions for leaving packages. This is especially valuable for food delivery, florist, or any business where delivery specifics directly affect service quality.

2. **Gift Message Capture** — For gift-oriented stores, the order notes field serves as a natural place for customers to include personalized messages. Style the field with a larger height and inviting placeholder text like "Add a gift message (optional)" to encourage use.

3. **Streamlined Checkout Placement** — Place this module between the shipping and payment modules in your checkout flow. Hide the title for a cleaner look and add a custom heading module above with text like "Anything we should know?" to create a more conversational checkout tone.

memories.summary: modules/woo-checkout-information.md: Woo Checkout Information > How to Add the Woo Checkout Information Module
memories.solution:
1. Ensure WooCommerce is installed and activated. Navigate to the Theme Builder and create or edit the template assigned to the WooCommerce checkout page.
2. Open the Visual Builder on your checkout page template. Click the gray **+** icon to add a new module to a row.
3. Search for "Woo Checkout Information" in the module picker or find it in the WooCommerce category, then click to insert it. The module will display the order notes field automatically.

modules/woo-checkout-information.md: Woo Checkout Information > Common Patterns
memories.solution:
1. **Optional Notes Below Shipping** — Place the Woo Checkout Information module between the shipping form and the payment module. Hide the title and use a Text module above it with text like "Any special instructions?" in a softer color. This positions the notes as a secondary, optional step that does not interrupt the checkout flow.

2. **Gift Message Field** — Change the field label and placeholder via PHP hooks to "Gift Message" with placeholder text like "Write your message here (we'll include it with the gift)." Style the textarea with a slightly larger minimum height and a warmer border color to create an inviting writing space that feels separate from the transactional parts of checkout.

3. **Full-Width Notes in Single-Column Checkout** — In a single-column checkout layout, place this module at full width with generous top and bottom margin via the Spacing options. The wide textarea gives customers ample room to type longer notes. Style the border to match the billing and shipping field styling for visual consistency.

memories.summary: modules/woo-checkout-information.md: Woo Checkout Information > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Order Notes Field Not Appearing"
    If the module renders but shows no textarea, a plugin or custom code may be removing the order notes field via the `woocommerce_checkout_fields` filter. Check your theme's functions.php and active plugins for code that unsets `$fields['order']['order_comments']`. Also verify the template is assigned to the WooCommerce checkout page.

!!! warning "Notes Not Saved to Order"
    If customers report that their notes are not appearing in the order, verify that the field name is `order_comments` (the WooCommerce default). Custom implementations that change the field name may not save correctly. Check WooCommerce > Orders and click into a specific order to view the "Customer provided note" section.

!!! tip "Hiding This Module When Not Needed"
    If your store does not need order notes, you can either remove this module from the checkout template entirely or use the PHP hook to unset the order comments field. Removing unnecessary form fields simplifies the checkout process and can improve conversion rates.

memories.summary: Woo Checkout Details module displays the order summary table on the WooCommerce checkout page.
memories.solution:
The Woo Checkout Details module renders a read-only table showing all products, quantities, subtotals, shipping costs, taxes, and the final total amount on the WooCommerce checkout page. It is designed to serve as a confirmation summary for customers before placing an order.

**Usage:**
*   Use in custom WooCommerce checkout page templates within the Theme Builder.
*   Pair with billing, shipping, and payment modules for a complete checkout flow.
*   Can be placed in a sidebar column (e.g., one-third width) and set to sticky using Position settings to keep the summary visible while filling out forms.

**Technical Details:**
*   **Block identifier:** `divi/woo-checkout-details`
*   The data is pulled automatically from the active WooCommerce cart session, mirroring the standard WooCommerce order review table structure.
*   Unlike modules for the cart page (e.g., Woo Cart Products), this module does not allow quantity editing or item removal; changes must be made on the cart page.

**Styling Controls:**
The Design tab allows styling of:
*   Title Text (e.g., 'Your Order' heading).
*   Column Label (Product, Total headers).
*   Body Text (product names, quantities, prices).
*   Table structure (overall appearance, borders, spacing).
*   Individual Table Row and Cell appearances.

**Content Controls:**
The Content tab allows setting a background color, gradient, image, or video for the entire module container. It also includes standard layout controls like `Loop` toggle, `Order` select, and custom admin labels.

memories.summary: Woo Notice module displays dynamic WooCommerce system messages on custom templates.
memories.solution:
The Woo Notice module renders standard WooCommerce notices (success, error, info) within custom Theme Builder templates. It adapts its output based on the selected **Page Type** (Product, Cart, or Checkout), ensuring customers receive immediate feedback on actions like adding products to cart, applying coupons, or resolving checkout validation errors.

**Usage Contexts:**
*   **Product Page:** Displays add-to-cart confirmations with a link to the cart.
*   **Cart Page:** Shows messages related to coupon applications, quantity updates, and stock issues.
*   **Checkout Page:** Handles form validation errors and payment processing feedback.

The module is designed for custom page templates (Product, Cart, Checkout) built in Divi Theme Builder. It requires WooCommerce to be installed and active, as notices are generated dynamically by user actions.

**Technical Details:**
*   **Block identifier:** `divi/wc-notice`
*   **Settings Tabs:** Content, Design, Advanced.
*   **Content Tab Settings:**
    *   `Page Type`: Selects the WooCommerce context (Product, Cart, or Checkout).
    *   `Product`: Allows selecting a specific product for previewing notice output in the Visual Builder.
    *   `Background`: Sets background color, gradient, image, or video behind the container.
    *   `Meta`: Assigns an admin label and controls visibility within the Visual Builder.
*   **Design Tab Settings:** Controls visual presentation (typography and styling) for notice text, buttons, and the module container. Customization options include: Title Text, Body Text, and Button styling.
*   **Custom CSS Selectors:**
    *   Success notices: `.et_pb_wc_notice .woocommerce-message` (Green)
    *   Error notices: `.et_pb_wc_notice .woocommerce-error` (Red)
    *   Info notices: `.et_pb_wc_notice .woocommerce-info` (Blue)
    *   View Cart button: `.et_pb_wc_notice .woocommerce-message .button`

**Implementation:** To use, navigate to **Divi > Theme Builder**, edit the relevant WooCommerce template, and insert the module. After configuration, save changes using the purple **Save** button or `Ctrl+S`/`Cmd+S`.

memories.summary: Displays cross-sell products on the cart page to boost AOV.
memories.solution:
The Woo Cross Sells module displays complementary product suggestions on the WooCommerce cart page. It is designed for use in custom cart page templates built in the Divi Theme Builder.

**Functionality:**
The module dynamically shows cross-sell products linked to items currently in the cart, encouraging additional purchases before checkout (Cart Page Upselling).

**Configuration:**
1. **Prerequisites:** Requires WooCommerce installed and active. Cross-sells must be configured under a product's **Linked Products** section within the WooCommerce product editor.
2. **Placement:** Must be placed on a custom cart page template, not general pages or single product pages.
3. **Integration:** Can be combined with `Woo Cart Products` and `Woo Cart Totals` modules to create a complete, branded cart layout.

**Settings & Options:**
The module has three tabs: Content, Design, and Advanced.
*   **Content Tab:** Controls link behavior (`Link`), background (`Background`), dynamic template context (`Loop`), flexbox positioning (`Order`), and admin visibility (`Meta`).
*   **Design Tab:** Styles product cards. Customizable elements include `Title Text` (font, size, color) and `Price Text` (font, color, size).
*   **Code Examples:** Custom CSS selectors are available for styling the container (`.et_pb_wc_cross_sells`), heading, individual product cards (`.et_pb_wc_cross_sells .cross-sells .products li`), titles, prices, and buttons.

**Usage Guidance:**
*   Use `divi/wc-cross-sells` for cross-sell suggestions on the cart page.
*   Use `woo-related-products` for related products on single product pages.
*   Use `shop.md` for general product grids.

**Troubleshooting:**
*   If not rendering: Verify WooCommerce is active, the module is on a cart template, and visibility settings are correct.
*   If no products show: Ensure cross-sells are configured under **Product Data > Linked Products**, they are published/in stock, and they aren't duplicates of cart items.
*   Stale data: If suggestions don't update after cart changes, clear page caching.

memories.summary: Woo Product Images module displays featured image and gallery thumbnails.
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Images module renders the WooCommerce product's featured image, along with interactive gallery thumbnails, sale badge, and zoom/lightbox functionality. It is designed for use on product page templates or custom layouts in the Theme Builder.

**Key Features & Usage:**
*   Displays the main product featured image, gallery thumbnails, sale badge, and supports interactive zoom/lightbox viewing.
*   Supports three toggle controls to independently show/hide: Featured Image, Gallery Thumbnails, and Sale Badge.
*   **Block identifier:** `divi/wc-product-images`
*   **Use Cases:** Ideal for building custom product page templates or displaying photo galleries with zoom functionality. It is not suitable for general image galleries (use [Gallery]) or single standalone images (use [Image]).
*   **Required Context:** Requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated, and must be placed on a product page template (not a regular page).

**Configuration Settings:**
*   **Content Tab:** Controls which elements are displayed. Options include toggles for `Show Featured Image`, `Show Gallery Images`, and `Show Sale Badge`. Also allows setting the `Link` URL, selecting the content source (`Content (Product)`), enabling the Loop Builder (`Loop`), and defining flexbox order (`Order`).
*   **Design Tab:** Controls visual styling. Options include dedicated settings for: `Image` (styling for featured image/thumbnails), `Sale Badge` (background color, text color, etc.), and shared design options like `Sizing`, `Spacing`, `Border`, `Box Shadow`, `Filters`, `Transform`, and `Animation`.
*   **Saving:** After configuration, save changes by clicking the **Save** button or using `Ctrl+S`/`Cmd+S`. Exit the builder using `Ctrl+Shift+E`.

memories.summary: Woo Notice module troubleshooting guide for rendering issues.
memories.solution:
If the Woo Notice module fails to render, verify that: WooCommerce is installed and activated; The Page Type setting matches the template context (Product, Cart, or Checkout); The module is placed on a dedicated WooCommerce page template, not a regular page; Visibility settings are not hiding it for the current device.

If the module renders but shows no notices, this is expected unless a notice-triggering action occurs. Notices appear only after events like adding an item to the cart (product page), applying/removing a coupon (cart page), or submitting checkout form validation errors (checkout page).

Notices are session-based and typically display once per page load. Check for AJAX updates or caching plugins that might interfere with WooCommerce session data.
