memories.summary: Displays WooCommerce product gallery images in a slider or grid format.
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Gallery module renders all assigned WooCommerce product gallery images as a standalone visual element on custom single product page templates.

**Usage:**
- **When to use:** Custom single product page templates built in the Divi Theme Builder, especially for dedicated image browsing or editorial-style showcases.
- **Layout Modes:** Supports two layouts: **Slider** (horizontal carousel) and **Grid** (four-column layout).
- **Block Identifier:** `divi/wc-gallery`
- **Requirements:** Requires WooCommerce to be installed. Gallery images must be added via the WooCommerce product editor.

**Key Settings & Behavior:**
- **Content Tab:** Allows selection of the target product, and toggles for `Show Pagination` (only in Grid mode) and `Show Title and Caption` (only in Grid mode).
- **Design Tab:** Controls the layout (`Slider`/`Grid`), image styling (border, shadow), and text elements. Text styling options are only active when using Grid layout with titles/captions enabled.

**Best Practices:**
- Use Slider for focused, one-image-at-a-time viewing (e.g., high-detail photography).
- Use Grid with titles/captions for detailed visual documentation (e.g., furniture materials, technical products).
- Position the module below main product info to provide supplementary context.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Navigate to **Divi > Theme Builder** and edit the WooCommerce product template.
2. Add the module using the Visual Builder.
3. Save changes (or use `Ctrl+S`/`Cmd+S`).

memories.summary: REST API content manipulation requires careful handling of module creation vs modification.
memories.solution:
Modifying existing modules via REST API (`wp.apiFetch` PATCH) updates settings attributes. Creating new modules via REST API produces front-end renderable content but may not appear in the Visual Builder layer view. For reliable module creation, use browser automation (Playwright). All operations require parsing `post_content` block JSON using a brace-depth parser.

**Module Operations Summary:**
| Module | Block Identifier |
| :--- | :--- |
| Woo Product Gallery | `divi/wc-gallery` |
| Woo Product Images | `divi/wc-product-images` |
| Woo Product Information | `divi/wc-product-information` |
| Woo Product Meta | `divi/wc-meta` |
| Woo Product Price | `divi/wc-product-price` |
| Woo Product Rating | `divi/wc-product-rating` |
| Woo Product Reviews | `divi/woo-product-reviews` |
| Woo Product Upsell | `divi/wc-upsells` |

**Key Content Attributes:**
* **Woo Product Images:**
    * Show Featured Image: `attrs.show_featured_image` (Toggle featured image visibility)
    * Show Gallery Images: `attrs.show_gallery_images` (Toggle thumbnail gallery visibility)
    * Show Sale Badge: `attrs.show_sale_badge` (Toggle sale badge visibility)
* **Woo Product Information:**
    * Product: `attrs.product` (Product ID reference)
    * Show Title: `attrs.show_title` (Toggle section title visibility)
* **Woo Product Meta:**
    * Product SKU, categories, and tags are managed here.
* **Woo Product Price:**
    * Product: `attrs.product` (Product ID reference)
* **Woo Product Rating:**
    * Product: `attrs.product` (Product ID reference)
    * Show Star Review: `attrs.show_star_review` (Toggle star visibility)
    * Show Customer Reviews Count: `attrs.show_reviews_count` (Toggle review count text)
* **Woo Product Reviews:**
    * Show Author Avatar: `attrs.show_author_avatar` (Toggle reviewer avatars)
    * Show Comment Count: `attrs.show_comment_count` (Toggle review count display)
    * Show Meta: `attrs.show_meta` (Toggle reviewer metadata)
    * Show Rating: `attrs.show_rating` (Toggle star ratings)

**Module Selection Guidance:**
* **Product Gallery:** Use Woo Product Gallery. For main featured image/thumbnail strip, use Woo Product Images. For non-WooCommerce galleries, use Gallery.
* **Structured Attributes:** Use Woo Product Information for structured attributes and specs. For product description text, use Woo Product Description. For tabbed display (description, attributes, reviews), use Woo Product Tabs.

memories.summary: REST API content manipulation requires careful handling of module creation vs modification.
memories.solution:

| Woo Product Images | `divi/wc-product-images` |

| Woo Product Rating | `divi/wc-product-rating` |
| Woo Product Reviews | `divi/woo-product-reviews` |
| Woo Product Upsell | `divi/wc-upsells` |

memories.summary: Advanced settings are shared across multiple product modules.
memories.solution:
Most product modules (Woo Product Images, Woo Product Information, Woo Product Meta, Woo Product Price) share a common set of advanced options for developer control. These include:

*   **Attributes:** Assign CSS ID, reusable CSS classes, or custom HTML attributes for advanced styling via child themes/custom CSS.
*   **CSS:** Allows adding custom CSS specific to the module.
*   **HTML:** Choose the semantic HTML tag for the module wrapper.
*   **Conditions:** Display rules (user role, page type, date, logic) for dynamic content display.
*   **Interactions:** Hover, click, or scroll-triggered interactions.
*   **Visibility:** Device visibility toggles.
*   **Transitions:** Controls hover transition timing and animation duration.
*   **Position:** CSS position and offsets for placement.
*   **Scroll Effects:** Control module behavior and transformation during scrolling.

(Note: The Save/Exit buttons are also present in the advanced settings.)

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-meta.md: Woo Product Meta
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Meta module displays a WooCommerce product's metadata — including SKU, categories, and tags — on custom single product page templates.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What it does:** Renders the product SKU, category links, and tag links with configurable layout and visibility toggles.
    **When to use it:** Custom single product page templates built in the Divi Theme Builder
    **Key settings:** Separator, Show SKU, Show Categories, Show Tags, Layout (Inline/Stacked)
    **Block identifier:** `divi/wc-meta`
    **ET Docs:** [Official documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12034567)

!!! tip "When to Use This Module"
    - Building a custom single product page that needs to display SKU, category, and tag metadata
    - Creating a product page layout where customers can navigate to related products via category or tag links
    - Displaying inventory identifiers (SKU) for products where customers reference part numbers

!!! warning "When NOT to Use This Module"
    - For general product details like weight and dimensions — use [Woo Product Information](woo-product-information.md)
    - For the product title — use [Woo Product Title](woo-product-title.md)
    - For product descriptions — use [Woo Product Description](woo-product-description.md)

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-meta.md: Woo Product Meta > Overview
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Meta module provides a structured way to display the organizational and identification metadata associated with a WooCommerce product. This metadata typically includes the product SKU (Stock Keeping Unit), the categories the product belongs to, and any tags assigned to it. Each metadata element is rendered as a labeled line — for example, "SKU: WC-SHIRT-001" or "Categories: Clothing, Summer Collection" — with categories and tags rendered as clickable links that navigate to their respective archive pages.

The module includes individual toggles for each metadata element, so you can display any combination of SKU, categories, and tags depending on what is relevant to your store. A Separator setting controls the visual delimiter between multiple categories or tags on the same line (such as commas, pipes, or other characters).

The Design tab offers a Layout option to arrange the metadata items either inline (side by side on one line) or stacked (each on its own line). This flexibility lets you integrate the module into compact product cards or expanded detail sections equally well.

For additional reference, see the [official Elegant Themes documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12034567).

!!! info "WooCommerce Required"
    This module requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated on your WordPress site. Products must have metadata (SKU, categories, or tags) assigned for the module to display content.

<!-- ![Woo Product Meta module](../assets/screenshots/modules/woo-product-meta/element.png){ loading=lazy } -->
<!-- *The Woo Product Meta module displaying SKU, categories, and tags in a stacked layout.* -->

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-meta.md: Woo Product Meta > Use Cases
memories.solution:
1. **Product Detail Footer** — Place the meta module below the product description and add-to-cart area to provide supplementary identification and classification information, following the conventional e-commerce product page structure.
2. **Category Navigation Aid** — Display category and tag links so customers can browse related products by clicking through to category or tag archive pages, improving product discoverability across your catalog.
3. **B2B Product Identification** — For wholesale or B2B stores, enable only the SKU display to give purchasing managers the part number reference they need for reordering, while hiding categories and tags that are less relevant in a business context.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-meta.md: Woo Product Meta > How to Add the Woo Product Meta Module
memories.solution:
1. Navigate to **Divi > Theme Builder** and create or edit a template assigned to WooCommerce product pages.
2. Open the Visual Builder on the product template.
3. Click the gray **+** icon to add a new module to a row.
4. Search for "Woo Product Meta" in the module picker, then click to insert it.

For an animated walkthrough of adding and configuring this module, see the
[official Elegant Themes documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12034567).

memories.solution: The Woo Product Meta module settings are organized across three tabs: Content, Design, and Advanced.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-meta.md: Woo Product Meta > Settings & Options > Content Tab
memories.solution:
The Content tab controls which product's metadata is displayed, which metadata elements are visible, and how they are separated.

| Setting | Type | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| Product | product selector | Choose which published WooCommerce product's metadata to display. In Theme Builder templates, this defaults to the current product dynamically. |
| Separator | select | Choose the character or delimiter used to separate multiple categories or tags on the same line (e.g., comma, pipe, slash). |
| Show SKU | toggle | Display or hide the product's SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) identifier. |
| Show Categories | toggle | Display or hide the product's category assignments as clickable links to category archive pages. |
| Show Tags | toggle | Display or hide the product's tag assignments as clickable links to tag archive pages. |
| Link | url | Optionally make the entire module clickable, directing users to a different page or URL. |
| Background | background controls | Set a background color, gradient, image, or video behind the product meta module container. |
| Order | select | Set the flexbox order of the module relative to sibling elements in the same row. |
| Meta | admin label | Assign an admin label and control module visibility inside the Visual Builder. |

<!-- ![Woo Product Meta Content tab settings](../assets/screenshots/modules/woo-product-meta/settings-content.png){ loading=lazy } -->

modules/woo-product-meta.md: Woo Product Meta > Common Patterns
memories.solution:
1. **Standard Product Footer Metadata** — Position the module below the add-to-cart button and above the product reviews using the Stacked layout. Apply a subtle top border and muted text color to visually separate the metadata from the primary product content, following conventional e-commerce page structure.

2. **Compact Inline Meta Strip** — Use the Inline layout with a pipe separator and reduced font size to create a single-line metadata strip. This works well in space-constrained product card layouts or sidebar product detail widgets.

3. **Category-Only Navigation** — Enable only the Show Categories toggle and hide SKU and tags. Style the category links as pill-shaped badges using custom CSS for a tag-cloud visual that invites browsing through related product categories.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-meta.md: Woo Product Meta > Saving Your Work
memories.solution:
After configuring the product meta module:

- **Save changes** — Click the purple **Save** button at the bottom of the Visual Builder, or press `Ctrl+S` (Windows) / `Cmd+S` (Mac).
- **Exit the builder** — Click the **X** button or use `Ctrl+Shift+E` to return to the WordPress dashboard.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-meta.md: Woo Product Meta > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Module Not Rendering"
    If the Woo Product Meta module does not appear on the front end, verify that:

    - WooCommerce is installed and activated
    - The module is placed on a product page template (not a regular page)
    - A valid, published product is assigned to the module
    - At least one metadata toggle (Show SKU, Show Categories, or Show Tags) is enabled

!!! warning "SKU Not Displaying"
    If the SKU line does not appear even with Show SKU enabled, check that:

    - The product has a SKU value entered in the **Product Data > Inventory** section of the WooCommerce product editor
    - The SKU field is not empty or set to a whitespace-only value

!!! tip "Categories or Tags Showing as Empty"
    If the category or tag line renders its label but shows no values, verify that the product has been assigned to at least one product category or tag in the WooCommerce product editor sidebar panels.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-price.md: Woo Product Price > Overview
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Price module pulls the price directly from the WooCommerce product data fields and renders it with full typographic control. When a product has a sale price configured, the module automatically displays both the original price (with strikethrough formatting) and the sale price, making the discount immediately visible to customers.

The module provides independent styling controls for the regular price, the original sale price (crossed out), and the new sale price, allowing you to create strong visual hierarchy that draws attention to discounts and promotions.

For additional reference, see the [official Elegant Themes documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12034706).

!!! info "WooCommerce Required"
    This module requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated on your WordPress site. Prices are pulled from the WooCommerce product editor's pricing fields.

3. **Price in Product Header** — Position the price module alongside the product title in a horizontal layout using flexbox ordering, creating a compact product header with title and price side by side.

memories.solution:
!!! warning "Module Not Rendering"
    If the Woo Product Price module does not appear on the front end, verify that:

    - WooCommerce is installed and activated
    - The module is placed on a product page template or a page with a valid product context
    - The module is not inside a disabled section or row
    - Visibility settings are not hiding it on the current device

!!! warning "Price Shows as Empty or Zero"
    If the module renders but displays no price or shows $0.00, check that:

    - The product has a regular price set in **Product Data > General** in the WooCommerce product editor
    - For variable products, at least one variation has a price defined
    - The product is published and not in draft status

!!! warning "Sale Price Not Showing Strikethrough"
    If a product is on sale but the original price does not show the strikethrough formatting, verify that:

    - Both a regular price and a sale price are configured in the WooCommerce product editor
    - The sale schedule has not expired (check the sale date range if set)
    - Custom CSS is not overriding the `text-decoration` property on the `del` element

!!! tip "Price Format Looks Wrong"
    If the currency symbol, decimal places, or thousands separator appear incorrect, check your WooCommerce currency settings under **WooCommerce > Settings > General**. The module inherits the global WooCommerce price format.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-rating.md: Woo Product Rating
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Rating module displays the average star rating for a WooCommerce product based on customer reviews, with optional review count text.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What it does:** Renders the average product star rating derived from WooCommerce customer reviews, with customizable star appearance and optional review count display.
    **When to use it:** Product page templates, custom product layouts in the Theme Builder
    **Key settings:** Product selector, Show Star Review, Show Customer Reviews Count, Layout (Inline/Stacked), Star Rating styling
    **Block identifier:** `divi/wc-product-rating`
    **ET Docs:** [Official documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12040851)

!!! tip "When to Use This Module"
    - Displaying the average review rating on custom product page templates as social proof
    - Positioning the star rating near the product title or price for quick trust signals
    - Styling the rating display to match your store's visual design

!!! warning "When NOT to Use This Module"
    - On non-WooCommerce pages — this module requires a product context
    - For full review listings with text — use [Woo Product Reviews](woo-product-reviews.md)
    - For product grids with ratings — use [Shop](shop.md) (ratings are built in)

memories.summary: Product Rating Module: Controls display, layout, and advanced styling.
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Rating module settings are organized into three tabs: Content, Design, and Advanced.

**Content Tab:**
- **Content (Product):** Selects the product supplying rating data (defaults to current product on dynamic templates).
- **Show Star Review:** Toggle to display/hide star visualization (default: enabled).
- **Show Customer Reviews Count:** Toggle to display/hide review count text (e.g., "(12 customer reviews)") (default: enabled).
- **Link:** Optionally makes the entire module clickable, directing users to a specific URL.
- **Background:** Sets background color, gradient, image, or video.
- **Loop:** Toggle for enabling Loop Builder in dynamic contexts.
- **Order:** Sets the flexbox order relative to sibling elements.
- **Meta:** Assigns an admin label and controls module visibility within the Visual Builder.

**Design Tab:**
- **Layout:** Selects orientation: **Inline** (stars/count side-by-side) or **Stacked** (stars above count).
- **Star Rating:** Customizes star alignment, color (filled/unfilled), size, and letter spacing.

**Advanced Tab:**
- Provides developer controls including CSS ID, classes, custom HTML attributes, custom CSS per element, semantic HTML tag choice, display rules (**Conditions**), interactions (hover/click/scroll), device visibility (**Visibility**), transition timing (**Transitions**), position (**Position**), and scroll effects (**Scroll Effects**).

**Usage Patterns:**
- **Below-Title Social Proof:** Place module below product title, above price. Use inline layout with medium gold stars and subtle gray review count link that scrolls to reviews.
- **Compact Rating Badge:** Position next to product price in the same row. Hide review count text; show only small stars for a compact trust signal.
- **Prominent Review Callout:** Use stacked layout with large stars, bold review count, and light background/padding for attention on high-review products.

memories.summary: Displays WooCommerce reviews and submission form on product pages.
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Reviews module pulls review data directly from WooCommerce, displaying both the existing list of reviews (including avatar, name, date, star rating, and comment text) and a submission form for logged-in customers. It is designed to be a key component in custom product page templates.

**Requirements & Functionality:**
*   Requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated.
*   Reviews must be enabled under `WooCommerce > Settings > Products`.
*   Only approved reviews are displayed, respecting WooCommerce's moderation settings.
*   The module allows placement in dedicated sections (e.g., full-width row) or alongside other content (e.g., description).

**Settings & Controls:**
*   **Content Tab:** Allows selection of the product for review display (defaults dynamically on Theme Builder templates). Toggles control visibility for: `Show Author Avatar`, `Show Comment Count`, `Show Meta` (reviewer name/date), and `Show Rating`. Also allows setting a custom module label (`Meta — Admin Label`) and controlling placement order (`Order`).
*   **Design Tab:** Provides styling controls for all visual elements, including the review form textarea (`Fields`), review count heading (`Review Count Text`), form title (`Form Title Text`), metadata (`Meta Text`), comment content (`Comment Text`), star rating appearance (`Star Rating`), and submit button (`Button`). It also offers advanced design options like `Image` (avatar styling), `Text` (review count text style), `Sizing`, `Spacing`, `Border`, `Box Shadow`, `Filters`, `Transform`, and `Animation`.
*   **Advanced Tab:** Offers low-level control via shared options groups: `Attributes` (CSS ID, classes, custom HTML attributes), `CSS` (custom CSS per element target), `Conditions` (display rules based on user role/page type), `Interactions`, `Visibility` (device toggles), `Transitions`, `Position`, and `Scroll Effects`. Advanced controls include setting the module's semantic HTML tag (`HTML`) and controlling its placement order (`Order`).

memories.summary: Configure Woo Product Reviews for optimal visibility and functionality.
memories.solution:
For maximum visibility, place the module in a dedicated full-width row below product details, enabling all display options (avatar, meta, rating, comment count) and styling the star rating color to match the brand.

For a refined aesthetic (e.g., luxury goods), disable author avatar and meta information for a clean, quote-style layout, and style the comment text with a larger font and italic styling.

To create a cohesive experience, use Button design options to style the review submission button with the site's CTA color, and customize Fields styling to give the textarea a branded border color on focus.

**Troubleshooting:**
*   **No Reviews Displaying:** Verify the product has at least one approved review. Ensure reviews are enabled under `WooCommerce > Settings > Products`. Confirm the Content setting points to the correct product (or is dynamic on a Theme Builder template).
*   **Review Form Not Showing:** Check that WooCommerce settings allow customer reviews (`WooCommerce > Settings > Products`). Verify the user must be logged in if required by WooCommerce.
*   **Star Ratings Not Displaying:** Ensure the Show Rating toggle is enabled in the module's Content tab, and verify star ratings are enabled under `WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Enable star rating on reviews`.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-stock.md: Woo Product Stock
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Stock module displays the stock status and inventory count for a WooCommerce product.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What it does:** Shows the product stock quantity and availability status (in stock, out of stock, on backorder) pulled from WooCommerce inventory settings.
    **When to use it:** Product page templates, custom product layouts in the Theme Builder
    **Key settings:** In Stock Text styling, Out of Stock Text styling, On Backorder Text styling, Loop Builder
    **Block identifier:** `divi/woo-product-stock`
    **ET Docs:** [Official documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12041304)

!!! tip "When to Use This Module"
    - Displaying stock availability on custom product page templates
    - Creating urgency with low-stock indicators near the add-to-cart area
    - Showing distinct styling for in-stock, out-of-stock, and backorder statuses

!!! warning "When NOT to Use This Module"
    - On non-WooCommerce pages — this module requires a product context
    - When stock management is disabled in WooCommerce — the module will show no data
    - For product pricing — use [Woo Product Price](woo-product-price.md)

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-stock.md: Woo Product Stock > Overview
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Stock module pulls inventory data directly from the WooCommerce product listing's Inventory section and displays the stock quantity and status on the front end. It supports three stock states — in stock, out of stock, and on backorder — each of which can be styled independently through the Design tab.

This module is particularly useful for products where stock visibility drives purchasing decisions. Showing "Only 3 left in stock" creates urgency that can increase conversion rates. For products on backorder, the module communicates availability expectations so customers know what to expect before purchasing.

The stock data is fully dynamic. When you update inventory quantities in WooCommerce (either manually or through order fulfillment), the module output updates automatically on the front end. For the module to display any data, stock management must be enabled on the individual product under Product Data > Inventory, and the "Stock quantity" field must be filled in.

The module also supports the Loop Builder, allowing you to display stock information for multiple products in a dynamic loop context outside of the standard product page template.

!!! info "WooCommerce Required"
    This module requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated. It will not appear in the module picker if WooCommerce is absent.

[View the official Elegant Themes documentation for this module.](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12041304)

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-stock.md: Woo Product Stock > Use Cases
memories.solution:
1. **Urgency-Driven Product Page** — Place the stock module directly below or beside the [Woo Product Price](woo-product-price.md) module and above the add-to-cart button. Style the in-stock text in green and use a bold font weight. When stock drops to low quantities, the visible count creates urgency that encourages immediate purchasing.

2. **Backorder Communication** — Style the on-backorder text in a distinct color (such as amber or orange) to clearly communicate that the product is available but will ship later. This sets customer expectations upfront and reduces support inquiries about delivery timelines.

3. **Inventory Dashboard Layout** — Use the Loop Builder integration to display stock status for multiple products on a single page. This can serve as an internal reference for store managers or as a public "availability" page showing which products are currently in stock.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-stock.md: Woo Product Stock > How to Add the Woo Product Stock Module
memories.solution:
1. Ensure WooCommerce is installed, activated, and that the product has stock management enabled under Product Data > Inventory with a stock quantity entered.
2. Open the Visual Builder on a product page template or any page. Click the gray **+** icon to add a new module to a row.
3. Search for "Woo Product Stock" in the module picker or find it in the WooCommerce category, then click to insert it.

memories.solution: The Woo Product Stock module settings are organized across three tabs: Content, Design, and Advanced.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-stock.md: Woo Product Stock > Settings & Options > Content Tab
memories.solution:

| Setting | Type | Description |

| Content | select | Choose the product for which you want to display the stock status. On Theme Builder templates, this defaults to the current product dynamically. |
| Link | url | Optionally make the entire module clickable, directing visitors to a specified URL. |
| Background | background controls | Set a background color, gradient, image, or video behind the module. |
| Loop | toggle | Enable the Loop Builder to display stock information in a dynamic loop context for multiple products. |
| Order | select | Control the module's placement order within Flexbox and Grid parent layouts. |
| Meta — Admin Label | text | Set a custom label for the module in the Visual Builder's layer panel. |
| Meta — Disable On | device toggles | Control builder-level visibility across devices. |

The Design tab provides independent styling controls for each stock status state, allowing you to visually differentiate between in-stock, out-of-stock, and backorder products.

**Module-specific settings:**

memories.solution:
1. **Price and Stock Pairing** — Place the Woo Product Stock module directly below the [Woo Product Price](woo-product-price.md) module in the same column. This gives customers immediate visibility into both cost and availability, which are the two most important factors in a purchasing decision.

2. **Color-Coded Status Badges** — Use the independent text styling for each stock state to create badge-like displays. Green background with green text for in-stock, red for out-of-stock, and amber for backorder. This provides instant visual communication of product availability.

3. **Low-Stock Urgency** — Combine the stock module with WooCommerce's low stock threshold setting. When stock drops below the threshold, WooCommerce changes the display text to show the remaining quantity. Style this with a bold red font to create urgency and drive conversions.

memories.solution:
!!! warning "Create vs. Modify"
    Modifying existing module content via REST API (`wp.apiFetch` PATCH) updates
    settings attributes. **Creating new modules via REST API** produces content
    that renders on the front end but may not appear in the Visual Builder layer
    view. Use browser automation for reliable module creation.
    See [REST API Content Playbook](../playbooks/rest-api-content.md).

**Block identifier:** `divi/woo-product-stock` — *Needs Testing*

| Operation | Method | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|--------|-------|
| Read content | Parse `post_content` block JSON | Needs Testing | Use brace-depth parser — see [Content Encoding](../internals/content-encoding.md) |
| Modify existing | `wp.apiFetch` PATCH on post endpoint | Needs Testing | Update block attributes in `post_content` |
| Create new | Browser automation (Playwright) | Needs Testing | REST creation may break VB visibility |
| Batch modify | Sequential REST requests | Needs Testing | See [REST API Content Playbook](../playbooks/rest-api-content.md) |

**Key content attributes** — *JSON paths need verification*:

| Attribute | JSON Path | Notes |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Product | `attrs.product` | Target product for stock display |
| Loop | `attrs.loop` | Enable Loop Builder context |

!!! tip "Module Selection Guidance"
    For stock status and quantity use Woo Product Stock; for pricing use Woo Product Price; for general product details use Woo Product Information.

!!! note "Divi 5 Only"
    This page documents Divi 5 behavior exclusively. The Woo Product Stock module in Divi 5 benefits from the updated rendering engine and supports Conditions, Interactions, Scroll Effects, and the Loop Builder not available in Divi 4.

!!! info "WooCommerce Required"
    This module requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated. Stock management must be enabled on individual products for the module to display data. WooCommerce 7.0 or later is recommended for full Divi 5 compatibility.

memories.summary: Woo Product Stock: Troubleshooting stock display and updates.
memories.solution:
To ensure a module displays product stock information:
- Verify that 'Manage stock' is enabled in the WooCommerce product editor (Product Data > Inventory) and a stock quantity is entered. Products without this setting will not show stock data.

If the displayed stock count does not reflect recent orders, confirm that WooCommerce is configured to reduce stock upon order completion (WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Inventory > Manage Stock). Also, clear all page caching to prevent stale content.

Stock status may vary per product because WooCommerce allows enabling stock management individually. Check each product's Inventory tab; products set to 'Do not manage stock' will not provide data.

memories.summary: Woo Products: Troubleshooting display issues and pagination.
memories.solution:
If the module shows no products:
- Ensure at least one published product exists in WooCommerce.
- Verify that the Product Type filter matches your content (e.g., 'Featured' requires featured products, 'Sale' requires sale prices).
- Confirm that the Product Offset is not set higher than the total available products.

If unexpected products appear:
- Check the Product Type and Order settings.
- Verify the Product Offset Number.
- If using 'Category', confirm correct category selections.
- Clear any WooCommerce caching plugins to view updated results.

For pagination issues (controls visible but non-functional):
- Check for JavaScript conflicts with other plugins.
- Ensure the total number of available products exceeds the set Product Count, as pagination only activates when more items than the limit are present.

memories.summary: Woo Related Products: Settings and configuration options.
memories.solution:
The module offers extensive control over related product display via multiple tabs:

**Content Tab:**
- **Product:** Selects the source product (defaults to current on Theme Builder).
- **Product Count:** Sets the maximum number of products displayed.
- **Column Layout:** Defines the number of columns for the grid.
- **Order:** Controls sorting options (date, title, price, popularity, rating, random).
- **Included Categories:** Filters results by specific WooCommerce categories.
- **Product Offset Number:** Skips a specified number of products to prevent repetition.
- **Show Name/Image/Price/Rating/Sale Badge:** Toggles visibility for product details.
- **Link:** Optionally makes the entire module clickable, directing to a URL.

**Design Tab (Styling):**
- **Overlay:** Configures featured image overlay effects (color, icon, hover).
- **Image:** Customizes featured image appearance (border radius, box shadow, object fit).
- **Star Rating:** Adjusts star display (alignment, colors, size, spacing).
- **Sale Badge:** Customizes sale badge appearance (background color, text color, font, etc.).
- **Text/Product Title Text/Price Text/Sale Price Text:** Allows granular styling of various text elements.

**Advanced Tab (Low-Level Control):**
- Offers control over HTML attributes, custom CSS, conditional display logic, and scroll effects.
- **Attributes:** Assigns CSS ID, reusable classes, or custom HTML attributes.
- **CSS:** Allows adding custom CSS to the module.
- **Conditions:** Sets dynamic display rules (user role, page type, date).
- **Visibility:** Controls device visibility.
- **Transitions/Position/Scroll Effects:** Manages advanced layout and animation behavior.

**Hooks (PHP):**
The module can be customized using filters:
- `et_module_shortcode_output`: Filters the output to modify content, e.g., changing 'Related products' heading.
- `woocommerce_output_related_products_args`: Modifies arguments for related product queries (e.g., setting `posts_per_page` and `columns`).

**Use Cases:**
*   **Hero Product Title:** Place at the top of a template; style large/bold; set HTML tag to `<h1`> for SEO prominence.
*   **Compact Product Header:** Position in multi-column rows alongside price/rating modules, using moderate styling for key information at a glance.
*   **Loop-Based Product Listing:** Use the Loop Builder to create custom product listing layouts with unique title typography control (better than [Shop](shop.md) or [Woo Products](woo-products.md)).

*   **Block identifier:** `divi/woo-product-title`
*   **Required Context:** Requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated; cannot be used on non-WooCommerce pages (e.g., post or page titles).

*   **Settings:** Controls include font family, size, weight, color, line height, letter spacing, and text shadow via the Design tab; advanced options allow selecting the semantic HTML tag.

**Module Selection Guidance:** Use Woo Product Tabs for full tabbed interfaces, Woo Product Description for standalone descriptions, and Woo Product Reviews for standalone reviews.

memories.summary: Controls product title display, styling, and advanced behavior.
memories.solution:
The Woo Product Title module allows control over which product's title is displayed (Content setting). It supports dynamic contexts via the Loop Builder toggle. 

**Design Tab Controls:**
The Design tab provides full typography controls for the title text, including font family, weight, style, alignment, color, size, letter spacing, line height, and text shadow. These settings support responsive adjustments (desktop, tablet, phone).
*   **Module-specific design options include:** Sizing, Spacing, Border, Box Shadow, Filters (hue shifts, saturation), Transform (scaling, rotating, skewing), and Animation.

**Advanced Tab Controls:**
The Advanced tab offers low-level control over HTML attributes, custom CSS, conditional display logic, and scroll effects.
*   **Key options include:** Attributes (CSS ID, classes, custom HTML attributes), CSS (custom CSS for specific elements), Conditions (display rules based on user role, page type, date, etc.), Visibility (device toggles), Transitions (hover transition timing), Position (CSS position/offsets), and Scroll Effects (scroll-driven animation).
*   **HTML Tag Selection:** Choose the semantic HTML tag (h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, p, span). For proper SEO hierarchy on product pages, use `h1` for the primary title.

**Code Examples & Hooks:**
*   **Custom CSS Example:** The module can be styled using selectors like `.et_pb_wc_title h1` and `@media` queries for responsiveness. A decorative underline can be added using pseudo-elements (e.g., `h1::after`).
*   **PHP Filter Hook:** Use `add_filter('et_module_shortcode_output', ...)` to programmatically modify the output, such as appending product SKU information.

**Usage Patterns & Best Practices:**
*   **Title + Price + Rating Row:** Place this module with Woo Product Price and Woo Product Rating modules in a single row for a complete product header.
*   **Overlay Title on Image:** Position the title absolutely over the Woo Product Images module using Advanced tab settings, applying text shadow or semi-transparent backgrounds for readability.
*   **Breadcrumb-Style Title:** Style with moderate font size and lighter weight, placing it above a breadcrumb trail. 

**Technical Notes & Gotchas:**
*   **SEO Hierarchy:** Only one module on a product page should use `h1` to maintain proper heading structure.
*   **REST API Interaction:** When creating new modules via REST API (`wp.apiFetch`), the content may render but might not appear in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation for reliable creation.
*   **Troubleshooting:** If styling changes are ignored, check for CSS conflicts and increase specificity using Custom CSS. If no title displays, ensure a product is set and that the template is assigned to product pages.

memories.solution:
1. **Below-Product Recommendations** — Place the upsell module in a full-width row below the product details section with a light background and clear heading. Set the column layout to 3 or 4 and enable all product card elements to create a comprehensive "You May Also Like" section.

2. **Minimal Image Grid** — Show only product images and names (disable price, rating, and sale badge) for a clean, gallery-like upsell presentation that invites exploration without overwhelming with information.

3. **Sale-Focused Upsells** — Enable the sale badge and style the sale price text with a contrasting color to draw attention to discounted premium alternatives. This is effective when upsell products are temporarily on sale, creating additional urgency for the upgrade.

memories.summary: modules/woo-product-upsell.md: Woo Product Upsell > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Module Not Rendering"
    If the Woo Product Upsell module does not appear on the front end, verify that:

    - WooCommerce is installed and activated
    - The module is placed on a product page template (not a regular page or cart template)
    - A valid, published product is assigned to the module
    - Visibility settings are not hiding it on the current device

!!! warning "No Upsell Products Showing"
    If the module renders but displays no products, check that:

    - The current product has upsell products configured under **Product Data > Linked Products > Upsells**
    - The linked upsell products are published (not draft or trashed)
    - The linked upsell products are not hidden from the catalog
    - The Product Count setting is greater than 0

!!! tip "Product Offset Hiding All Results"
    If the Product Offset Number is set higher than the number of available upsell products, no products will display. Reduce the offset value or add more upsell products to the parent product's linked products configuration.

memories.summary: modules/woo-products.md: Woo Products
memories.solution:
The Woo Products module displays a gallery of WooCommerce products with options for featured, sale, and custom product collections.

!!! abstract "Quick Reference"
    **What it does:** Shows a configurable grid of WooCommerce products with images, titles, prices, ratings, and sale badges.
    **When to use it:** Homepage product showcases, category landing pages, custom shop layouts, product page upsells
    **Key settings:** Product Type, Product Count, Column Layout, Order, Show elements (Name, Image, Price, Rating, Sale Badge), Pagination
    **Block identifier:** `divi/woo-products`
    **ET Docs:** [Official documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12042132)

!!! tip "When to Use This Module"
    - Displaying curated product collections on homepage or landing pages
    - Showing featured, on-sale, best-selling, or top-rated products in a styled grid
    - Building custom shop layouts with product type filtering and pagination

!!! warning "When NOT to Use This Module"
    - On non-WooCommerce sites — this module requires WooCommerce
    - For related products on a product page — use [Woo Related Products](woo-related-products.md)
    - For non-product content grids — use [Blog](blog.md) or [Portfolio](portfolio.md)

memories.summary: modules/woo-products.md: Woo Products > Overview
memories.solution:
The Woo Products module displays a gallery of products from your WooCommerce catalog in a grid layout. It provides extensive filtering options to control which products appear, including product type (latest, featured, sale, best selling, top rated, or by category), product count, column layout, sort order, and the ability to offset products for pagination or rotating displays.

Each product card in the grid can display the featured image, product name, price, star rating, and sale badge. All of these elements are individually toggleable through the Content tab, allowing you to create anything from a minimal image-only grid to a full product card with all details visible. The grid responds to screen size automatically, adjusting the column count for tablet and mobile devices.

The module differs from the [Shop](shop.md) module in its filtering approach. While the Shop module focuses on recent, featured, sale, and best-selling product types with category filtering, the Woo Products module adds the ability to filter by specific product type categories and includes a product offset setting for more precise control over which products appear. Both modules render similar product grid layouts, but Woo Products is designed more for curated product showcases than full shop page replacements.

!!! info "WooCommerce Required"
    This module requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated. It will not appear in the module picker if WooCommerce is absent.

[View the official Elegant Themes documentation for this module.](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/12042132)

memories.summary: modules/woo-products.md: Woo Products > Use Cases
memories.solution:
1. **Homepage Featured Products** — Set the Product Type to "Featured" and the Product Count to 4 or 6 with a matching column layout. Enable all display elements and style the product cards with box shadows and hover effects. Place this in a dedicated section below the hero to immediately surface your best products.

2. **Sale Products Banner** — Filter by "Sale" product type and place the module inside a section with a bold background color. Add a heading row above with text like "Limited Time Offers." Enable the Sale Badge and style it with the Sale Badge design options for maximum visibility. The grid updates automatically as you mark products on sale in WooCommerce.

3. **Category Product Showcase** — Set the Product Type to "Category" and select specific categories to display. Use a higher product count (8-12) with 3 or 4 columns and enable pagination. This creates a mini shop experience for a specific product category that can be placed on any page.

memories.summary: modules/woo-products.md: Woo Products > How to Add the Woo Products Module
memories.solution:
1. Ensure WooCommerce is installed, activated, and that at least one product is published in your WordPress dashboard under Products.
2. Open the Visual Builder on the page you want to edit. Click the gray **+** icon to add a new module to a row.
3. Search for "Woo Products" in the module picker or find it in the WooCommerce category, then click to insert it.

memories.summary: modules/woo-products.md: Woo Products > Settings & Options > Content Tab
memories.solution:
The Content tab controls which products display, how they are sourced and sorted, and what elements are visible on each product card.

| Setting | Type | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| Product Type | select | Choose the product query type: Default, Latest, Featured, Sale, Best Selling, Top Rated, or Category. This determines the base set of products the module pulls from your WooCommerce catalog. |
| Product Count | number input | Set the maximum number of products to display in the grid. Controls how many product cards appear. |
| Column Layout | select | Set the number of columns in the product grid. Affects how many products appear per row on desktop. |
| Order | select | Control the sort order of products. Options include date, title, price, popularity, rating, and other WooCommerce sort fields. |
| Product Offset Number | number input | Skip a specified number of products from the beginning of the query results. Useful for creating paginated layouts or showing different product sets in multiple module instances on the same page. |
| Show Pagination | toggle | Enable or disable pagination controls below the product grid when the total product count exceeds the Product Count setting. |
| Show Name | toggle | Display or hide the product title on each card. |
| Show Image | toggle | Display or hide the product featured image. |
| Show Price | toggle | Display or hide the product price, including sale pricing when applicable. |
| Show Rating | toggle | Display or hide the star rating on each product card. Ratings come from WooCommerce product reviews. |
| Show Sale Badge | toggle | Display or hide the "Sale" badge overlay on products that are currently on sale. |
| Link | url | Optionally make the entire module clickable, directing visitors to a specified URL. |
| Background | background controls | Set a background color, gradient, image, or video behind the module. |
| Order (Flexbox) | select | Control the module's placement order within Flexbox and Grid parent layouts. |
| Meta — Admin Label | text | Set a custom label for the module in the Visual Builder's layer panel. |
| Meta — Disable On | device toggles | Control builder-level visibility across devices. |

memories.summary: Woo Related Products module displays related items on product pages.
memories.solution:
The Woo Related Products module shows products related to the current one (based on shared categories/tags) in a configurable grid. It is designed for use in Product Page Templates.

**Functionality & Use Cases:**
*   Increases engagement and AOV by suggesting related items ('You may also like').
*   Can be used for targeted recommendations using the **Included Categories** filter (e.g., showing only other running shoes).
*   The **Product Offset** setting prevents duplicate suggestions across similar product pages.
*   Ideal placements include full-width sections at the bottom of a page or compact sidebar columns.

**Technical Details:**
*   **Block identifier:** `divi/woo-related-products`
*   Requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated, and products must have categories or tags assigned.
*   The module allows individual toggling of elements on the product card: featured image, name, price, star rating, sale badge. Image overlay controls are available for hover effects.

**Module Settings:**
*   Settings are organized into Content, Design, and Advanced tabs.
*   **Content Tab:** Controls filtering (e.g., Included Categories), sorting, product count, column layout, and visible elements.
*   **Design Tab:** Provides visual controls for the grid (image overlays, typography, sale badges, star ratings).

memories.summary: REST API module interaction guidelines and specific block attributes.
memories.solution:
### Module Interaction Notes
*   **Modifying existing modules:** Use `wp.apiFetch` PATCH on the post endpoint to update settings attributes.
*   **Creating new modules:** REST creation may render content but might not appear in the Visual Builder (VB) layer view. For reliable module creation, use browser automation (Playwright).
*   **Batch modification:** Requires sequential REST requests and adherence to the [REST API Content Playbook](../playbooks/rest-api-content.md).
*   **Reading content:** Parse `post_content` block JSON using a brace-depth parser.

### Block Identifiers (Needs Testing)
*   Woo Products: `divi/woo-products`
*   Woo Related Products: `divi/woo-related-products`

### Key Content Attributes
**Woo Products (`divi/woo-products`)**
| Attribute | JSON Path | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Product Type | `attrs.type` | Product query type (default, latest, featured, sale, etc.) |
| Product Count | `attrs.posts_number` | Maximum products to display |
| Column Layout | `attrs.columns_number` | Number of grid columns |
| Order | `attrs.orderby` | Sort order field |
| Product Offset | `attrs.offset_number` | Number of products to skip |

**Woo Related Products (`divi/woo-related-products`)**
| Attribute | JSON Path | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Product | `attrs.product` | Target product for related products lookup |
| Product Count | `attrs.posts_number` | Maximum related products to display |
| Column Layout | `attrs.columns_number` | Number of grid columns |
| Order | `attrs.orderby` | Sort order field |
| Included Categories | `attrs.include_categories` | Category filter for related products |
| Product Offset | `attrs.offset_number` | Number of products to skip |

memories.solution:
The Image options group provides comprehensive visual controls for featured images displayed by modules. Settings are found in the Design tab → Image.

**What it controls:** Border, rounded corners, box shadow, CSS filters (hue, saturation, brightness, contrast, etc.), and blend mode.
**Available on:** Modules with featured images (Image, Blurb, Blog, Person, Testimonial, Portfolio, Gallery, Post Slider).
**Responsive:** Yes — image styling values can be set per breakpoint.

| Setting | Type | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| Image/Icon Placement | Dropdown | Positions the image or icon relative to content: Top or Left. |
| Image/Icon Alignment | Dropdown | Sets horizontal alignment (Left, Center, Right) when placement is Top. |
| Image Rounded Corners | Input / linked toggle | Sets corner radius values, uniformly or per-corner when unlinked. |
| Border Width | Input | Defines border thickness in pixels (minimum 1px). |

memories.summary: Controls link relationship attributes (rel) on button links for SEO/security.
memories.solution:
The `rel` attribute specifies the relationship between a page and its linked destination, impacting search engine interpretation, browser security, and referrer data transmission.

**Available values:**
*   `nofollow`: Prevents passing link equity; use for sponsored, paid, or user-generated links.
*   `noopener`: Closes a security vulnerability when opening links in new tabs.
*   `noreferrer`: Prevents the destination page from knowing the visitor's source.
*   `external`: Signals the link points to a different website.
*   `bookmark`: Links to an anchor within the current site.

**Usage:** Found in the Advanced Tab $\rightarrow$ Attribute for modules with button elements (e.g., Button, CTA). Link attributes are static across all breakpoints.

**Security Best Practice:** For external links, combine `noopener` and `noreferrer`.

memories.summary: Configures data source and display rules for blog feeds (Content).
memories.solution:
The Content options group controls the data queried and formatted for modules displaying content feeds (e.g., Blog module).

**Settings Reference:**
*   **Post Type:** Selects the content type to display (posts, pages, media, projects, etc.).
*   **Post Count:** Number of posts per page.
*   **Included Categories:** Filters by specific categories (all included by default).
*   **Date Format:** Customizes date display using PHP format codes (e.g., "F j, Y").
*   **Content Length:** Toggle to show either the post excerpt or full content.
*   **Use Post Excerpts:** If enabled, uses manually written excerpts; otherwise, auto-generates them.
*   **Excerpt Length:** Character limit for auto-generated excerpts (default 270).
*   **Post Offset Number:** Skips a specified number of posts before the feed begins.

**Usage:** Found in the Content tab. The Elements group controls visibility, while typography groups handle styling.

memories.summary: Background options allow layering of color, gradient, image, video, pattern, and mask.
memories.solution:
The Background option group provides customizable background styling (color, gradient, image, video, pattern, and mask) for all Divi 5 elements (sections, rows, columns, modules). These six types can be layered simultaneously using opacity and blending controls. All settings support responsive device toggling.

**Settings Reference:**
*   **Background Color:** Solid color fill; supports opacity adjustment and layers beneath other backgrounds.
*   **Background Gradient:** Uses the unified **Gradient Picker** (Divi 5.7+) for linear/radial gradients, color stops, gradient variables, and layering.
*   **Background Image:** Allows uploading or selecting an image; controls include position, size, repeat behavior, blend mode, and parallax scrolling.
*   **Background Video:** Embeds video via file upload or URL input.
*   **Background Pattern:** Applies a decorative repeating pattern; includes color, opacity, size, and blend mode controls.
*   **Background Mask:** Adds a custom shape/overlay mask; provides controls for color, size, aspect ratio, and orientation.

memories.summary: Box Shadow options add depth by controlling shadow position, blur, spread, and color.
memories.solution:
The Box Shadow option group applies customizable shadows to all Divi 5 elements (sections, rows, columns, modules) to create depth. Controls include the shadow's horizontal/vertical position, softness (blur), size (spread), color, and placement (inner/outer).

**Settings Reference:**
*   **Box Shadow Horizontal Position:** Offset control; positive values shift right, negative values shift left.
*   **Box Shadow Vertical Position:** Offset control; positive values shift down, negative values shift up.
*   **Box Shadow Blur Strength:** Controls shadow softness/diffusion (higher = wider).
*   **Box Shadow Spread Strength:** Controls shadow size/density (positive = expand, negative = shrink).
*   **Shadow Color:** Sets the shadow color.
*   **Box Shadow Position:** Selects between outer (outside) and inner (inset) placement.

memories.solution:

**What it controls:** Horizontal text alignment (left, center, right, justify) and applying a drop shadow effect to all body content.

**Available on:** Modules containing descriptive text, such as Text, Blurb, CTA, Toggle, Accordion, and Testimonial modules. The settings are responsive, allowing per-breakpoint configuration.

**Settings Reference:**
*   **Text Alignment:** Sets the horizontal alignment for all module body text.
*   **Text Shadow:** Toggles a drop shadow effect; when active, allows customization of:
    *   Shadow Direction (horizontal and vertical offset)
    *   Blur Strength (controls diffusion/softness)
    *   Shadow Color (supports site palette and custom values)

memories.solution:

**What it controls:** Font selection, weight, size, color, alignment, letter spacing, line height, and text shadow.

**Available on:** Modules designed to render configurable heading content (e.g., Heading module).

**Settings Reference:**
*   **Heading Level:** Assigns the semantic HTML tag (H1-H6).
*   **Font Controls:** Allows setting typeface, weight, and style (italics, small caps, underline, strikethrough).
*   **Advanced Styling (Divi 5.7+):**
    *   **Heading Gradient Fill:** Fills text with a gradient.
    *   **Heading Image Fill:** Fills glyphs with an image.
    *   **Heading Text Stroke:** Outlines letterforms for contrast.
*   **Layout Controls:** Includes Heading Text Alignment, Heading Text Size, Heading Letter Spacing, and Heading Line Height.
*   **Shadow:** Adds a drop shadow effect (configurable direction, blur radius, and color).

memories.summary: Module Elements CSS fields target specific parts of a module.
memories.solution:
Module Elements CSS provides dedicated input fields for targeted adjustments, accepting only CSS property declarations (not full rule blocks). Every module type exposes different element fields reflecting its internal structure. Three core pseudo-element fields are always available:

*   **Before**: Applies CSS properties to the `::before` pseudo-element.
*   **Main Element**: Applies CSS properties directly to the primary module wrapper element.
*   **After**: Applies CSS properties to the `::after` pseudo-element.

Additionally, modules have specific fields (e.g., Title, Body, Button, Image) that accept property declarations only.

memories.solution:

* Show Read More Button: Toggle (Controls 'Read More' button visibility).
* Show Author: Toggle (Controls author name visibility).
* Show Date: Toggle (Controls publication date visibility).
* Show Categories: Toggle (Controls category listing visibility).
* Show Comment Count: Toggle (Controls comment count display).
* Show Excerpt: Toggle (Controls excerpt text visibility).
* Show Pagination: Toggle (Controls pagination link visibility).

memories.summary: Defines a module as a clickable hyperlink element.
memories.solution:
The Link options group allows any supported module to function as a hyperlink, making the entire element clickable rather than just specific internal links or buttons. When a Module Link URL is set, clicking anywhere on the module navigates the visitor to the specified destination.

**Settings:**
* **Location:** Content tab of the module's settings panel.
* **Functionality:** Specifies the destination URL and whether the link should open in the same window (default) or a new tab. This feature wraps the entire element, ensuring all areas are clickable.

memories.solution:
The Meta options group is used exclusively within the Divi 5 Visual Builder to improve organization and workflow efficiency; it has no effect on front-end output.

**Settings:**
* **Element Label (Text input):** Assigns a custom name that appears in the layer panel, breadcrumbs, and tooltips for easier navigation. A consistent naming convention is recommended (e.g., Section: Hero -> Row: Content).

    * While in Builder: Element remains visible when the Visual Builder is active.
    * While Editing Element: Element is visible only when its settings panel is open.

memories.summary: Controls typography for pagination links (Blog/Portfolio modules).
memories.solution:
**Available on:** Blog and Portfolio modules.

**What it controls:** Font, weight, size, color, alignment, letter spacing, line height, and text shadow for page navigation links.

**Location:** Design Tab → Pagination Text.

**Settings Reference:**
*   `Pagination Font`: Selects the typeface (Font selector).
*   `Pagination Font Weight`: Adjusts boldness from light to extra-bold (Selector).
*   `Pagination Font Style`: Applies stylistic treatments like italics, capitalization, small caps, underline, or strikethrough (Toggle options).
*   `Pagination Text Alignment`: Positions text as left, center, right, or justified (Alignment selector).
*   `Pagination Text Color`: Sets the color of pagination links (Color picker).
*   `Pagination Text Size`: Defines font size (Range slider / input).
*   `Pagination Letter Spacing`: Controls character spacing (Range slider / input).
*   `Pagination Line Height`: Sets vertical line spacing (Range slider / input).
*   `Pagination Text Shadow`: Adds a shadow effect with controls for position, blur strength, and color.

**Code Examples:**
```css
/* Style pagination links */
.et_pb_blog_grid .wp-pagenavi a,
.et_pb_blog_grid .wp-pagenavi span {
  font-size: 14px;
  font-weight: 500;
  color: #636e72;
}
```

memories.summary: Comprehensive typography controls for body content in text modules.
memories.solution:
**Available on:** Text-based modules (Text, Accordion, Blurb, CTA, etc.).

**What it controls:** Font family, weight, style, size, color, alignment, letter spacing, line height, and advanced effects like gradient/image fills and text stroke.

**Location:** Design Tab → Text.

**Settings Reference:**
*   `Font`: Selects the typeface (Dropdown / custom upload).
*   `Font Weight`: Adjusts boldness (Select).
*   `Font Style`: Applies treatments like italic, uppercase, underline, and strikethrough (Multi-select toggles).
*   `Text Alignment`: Sets horizontal alignment (Button group: left, center, right, justified).
*   `Text Color`: Defines the body text color (Color picker).
*   `Text Gradient Fill`: Fills text glyphs with a gradient (Gradient picker). Supports gradient variables (Divi 5.7+).
*   `Text Image Fill`: Fills text glyphs with an image (Image selector). (Divi 5.7+)
*   `Text Stroke`: Outlines letterforms with configurable width and color (Composite). (Divi 5.7+)
*   `Text Size`: Controls font size (Range slider / text input, accepts px, em, rem).
*   `Letter Spacing`: Adjusts horizontal character spacing (Range slider / text input).
*   `Line Height`: Sets vertical line spacing (Range slider / text input).
*   `Text Shadow Horizontal Position`: Controls shadow X offset (Range slider).
*   `Text Shadow Vertical Position`: Controls shadow Y offset (Range slider).
*   `Text Shadow Blur Strength`: Adjusts shadow softness (Range slider).
*   `Text Shadow Color`: Sets the shadow color (Color picker).

**Code Examples:**
```css
.my-module p {
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  font-size: 18px;
  line-height: 1.7;
  letter-spacing: 0.02em;
  color: #444444;
}
```

```css
.my-module p {
  text-shadow: 1px 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);
}
```

memories.summary: Controls CSS position, offsets, and stacking order for elements in the page layout.
memories.solution:
The Position options group controls how an element is placed on the page, affecting its CSS `position` method, directional offsets, and z-index. It is available on all modules, sections, rows, and columns within the Divi 5 Visual Builder (Advanced tab). 

**Positioning Methods:**
*   **Relative (Default):** Stays in the normal document flow; offsets shift it visually without affecting surrounding elements.
*   **Absolute:** Removed from the document flow; positioned relative to its nearest positioned ancestor (or viewport if none exists).
*   **Fixed:** Removed from the document flow; locked to the viewport, remaining visible regardless of scrolling.

**Settings Reference:**
*   **Position:** Defines the positioning method. Options are Relative, Absolute, and Fixed.
*   **Vertical Offset:** Shifts element up/down. Positive values move it down; negative values move it up.
*   **Horizontal Offset:** Shifts element left/right. Positive values move it right; negative values move it left.
*   **Z-Index:** Controls stacking order. Higher values place the element in front of lower values, useful for overlapping designs.

**Usage Notes:**
*   Position values are responsive and can be configured per breakpoint.
*   For custom styling, use CSS IDs or classes (e.g., `position: fixed; top: 20px; right: 20px; z-index: 999;`).
*   Alternative layout methods include using Transform Options (`translate`) with position, Flexbox Layout, or CSS Grid.

memories.summary: options-groups/read-more.md: Read More Options > Overview
memories.solution:
The Read More options group provides typographic styling for the "Read More" link that appears below post excerpts in feed layouts. This link directs visitors to the full post content and is a key interactive element in any blog listing.

These settings are located in the Design tab of the module settings panel. They offer the standard set of text styling controls: font selection, weight, style, alignment, color, size, letter spacing, line height, and text shadow. This consistency with other typography groups makes it straightforward to create a cohesive design across all text elements.

Styling the Read More link distinctly from body text helps draw attention to the call-to-action. Common approaches include using a contrasting color, bold weight, uppercase text, or increased letter spacing to make the link visually prominent and clearly actionable.

For additional reference, see the [official Elegant Themes documentation](https://help.elegantthemes.com/en/articles/10248771).

memories.summary: Controls element visibility and overflow across devices (Phone, Tablet, Desktop).
memories.solution:
**Visibility Control:**
*   **Scope:** Available on all modules, sections, rows, and columns in the Visual Builder.
*   **Setting:** Use **Disable On** checkboxes under the Advanced tab to hide elements independently for Phone, Tablet, or Desktop. Multiple devices can be selected simultaneously.
*   **Workflow:** To configure visibility, hover over the element, click the gear icon, go to the Advanced tab, and open the Visibility option group.
*   **Previewing:** Elements disabled on the current preview breakpoint appear at 50% opacity but remain visible for editing.

**Overflow Control (Horizontal & Vertical):**
*   Controls how content exceeding an element's boundaries is handled. Controlled separately.
*   **Options:**
    *   `Visible`: Content overflows normally.
    *   `Hidden`: Content is clipped at the element boundary.
    *   `Scroll`: A scrollbar appears when content overflows.
    *   `Auto`: A scrollbar appears only when needed.

**Breakpoints:**
*   Default breakpoints are Phone, Tablet, and Desktop. Additional options include Phone Wide, Tablet Wide, Widescreen, Ultra Wide (optional). Custom Breakpoints can be enabled via `../builder/custom-breakpoints.md`.

**Best Practices:**
*   Reserve visibility toggles for structural changes; use responsive styling for minor adjustments (e.g., font size).
*   Use overflow settings when content unexpectedly clips on small screens, rather than hiding the entire element.
*   Limit layout versions to one desktop and one mobile version, and use admin labels to identify variants clearly.

memories.solution:
Playbooks are LLM-first documentation designed for AI assistants helping users build or modify Divi 5 websites. They teach *how* to accomplish tasks step-by-step, unlike reference docs which answer *what* a setting does.

**Core Playbook Topics (Divi 5):**
*   **Design System Setup:** Configure global typography, colors, and design variables first for consistent site-wide styling. Audit the target design by identifying tokens like Heading font/color, Body text color, Accent color, Link color, Section background colors, H1-H6 sizes, Body text size (e.g., 17px), and Line heights.
*   **Build a Page:** Provides an end-to-end workflow for creating new Divi 5 pages.
*   **Visual Builder Operations:** Covers the dual-frame architecture, panels, Layers navigation, settings tabs, saving behavior, and responsive editing of the Visual Builder (VB).
*   **CSS in Divi 5:** Guides on when to use Design tab vs Custom CSS vs Free-Form CSS vs child theme, including specificity rules and the selector keyword.
*   **HTML Workarounds:** Techniques for content that survives WordPress sanitization, such as table-based cards, inline SVG icons, logo bars, and styled layouts.
*   **Responsive Design:** Covers desktop-first breakpoints, device-specific overrides, max-width media queries, and mobile-first patterns.
*   **REST API Content Management:** Details programmatic content creation rules: the create-vs-modify rule, brace-depth parsing, sequential chaining, content encoding, and save validation patterns.
*   **Theme Builder Operations:** Instructions for creating global headers, footers, post templates, and category-specific template assignments.
*   **Browser Automation:** Playbook for automating the Visual Builder using Playwright and Claude in Chrome.
*   **Known Limitations:** A playbook covering 20 rules on Divi 5 quirks (e.g., REST API content, TinyMCE sync, SSR gaps, CSS specificity). It warns that Divi defaults to 14px body text and 30px headings; global design setup is mandatory.
*   **Troubleshooting Tree:** A systematic decision tree for diagnosing common VB, rendering, CSS, and REST API problems.

memories.summary: Divi 5 Gallery Taxonomy setup details.
memories.solution:
The `gallery_category` is a custom hierarchical taxonomy registered against the `attachment` post type. It is visible in the Media Library admin column, exposed via REST API, and surfaces under the Media menu.

To ensure correct term counts on attachment taxonomies:
- Use `update_count_callback => '_update_generic_term_count'` because attachments are `post_status=inherit`, not `publish`. The default counter only counts `publish` posts, causing term counts to remain zero. The generic counter ignores status.

Setting `hierarchical = true` provides nested categories and renders the proper term-edit UI on the attachment edit screen (more than a comma-separated text input). However, even with this setting, the attachment details modal still displays custom taxonomies as plain text.

memories.summary: Divi 5 Filterable Gallery uses callbacks to inject data attributes into gallery wrappers for filtering.
memories.solution: The plugin utilizes two server-side hooks: `render_block` (for Divi 5's gallery render pipeline, slug=`et_pb_gallery`, block name=`divi/gallery`) and `et_module_shortcode_output` (for Divi 4 fallback paths). The process involves walking the rendered HTML to find each gallery item by class, looking up the attachment ID, and injecting `data-categories="slug-1,slug-2"` onto the wrapper element. Note that Divi 5 wraps images in both `et_pb_gallery_item` (outer, togglable) and `et_pb_gallery_image` (inner); the XPath must match either via an `or` clause to ensure all wrappers are captured.

memories.summary: Generating Divi 5 Global Variables JSON from existing style guides or tokens.
memories.solution:
To create a Divi 5 Global Variables import, generate a single JSON file containing `context: "et_builder"`, `global_colors` (palette swatches), and `global_variables` (colors, numbers, fonts, strings, links).

This process is format-agnostic:
1. **From Tokens**: Use design tokens (JSON/CSV/table) as the source of truth.
2. **From Prose**: If only prose exists, extract only explicitly specified values (HEX colors, px values, font family names, URLs, etc.).

**Minimal Token Table Format**: A deterministic approach uses a table structure:
| name | type | value | notes (optional) |
|---|---|---|---| 
| `color.brand.navy` | `colors` | `#1A2332` | Primary brand background |
| `font.heading.family` | `fonts` | `Roboto` | Headlines |
| `type.h1.size` | `numbers` | `48px` | Desktop |
| `space.2` | `numbers` | `16px` | Spacing scale |
| `radius.sm` | `numbers` | `4px` | Buttons/inputs |
| `link.site` | `links` | `https://example.com` | Canonical URL |

**Allowed Divi Variable Types**: `colors`, `numbers`, `fonts`, `strings`, `links`, `images`.

**Recommended Coverage**: Includes primary/secondary colors, neutrals, semantic colors (success/warning/error/info), heading/body font families and type scale (H1–H5 + body), container max width, readable text max width, small spacing scale, 1–3 radii, 1–3 shadows, website URL, support email, phone, and key CTA text.

**Stable IDs**: For re-import consistency, use stable string IDs derived from token names:
* **Colors**: `gcid-<slug>` (e.g., `gcid-color-brand-navy`)
* **Variables**: `gvid-<slug>` (e.g., `gvid-type-h1-size`)

**Import Process**: Import the JSON via **Divi → Divi Library → Import & Export**, ensuring **Import Global Variables** is enabled.

memories.summary: Troubleshooting and best practices for importing design variables into Divi 5.
memories.solution:
### Troubleshooting Warnings
* **Fonts not rendering**: The variable must be imported first, but the actual font files (uploaded or served by Google Fonts) must also be available on the site. Import variables, then ensure fonts are loaded before final QA.
* **JSON import fails/blocked**: Some hosts or security plugins may block JSON uploads.
* **Missing styles after import**: If layouts look wrong, you likely imported them *before* setting up presets/variables. Re-import in the recommended order (Variables $\rightarrow$ Layouts).
* **Theme Builder changes**: Theme Builder templates include assignment rules. On non-clean sites, export your Theme Builder first, then re-import selectively.

### Library Import JSON Pitfalls
If importing JSON into the Divi Library (`et_builder_layouts`) and the item appears in the admin list but not in the Visual Builder's **Saved Layout** / **Add From Library** pickers, check the file’s `terms` array. For full page layouts, the `layout_type` must use slug `layout`, not `page`.

### Tools
* A community Claude skill can generate this JSON from style guide prose and/or a token table: **[divi-styleguide-variables](https://github.com/16wells/divi-styleguide-variables)**.

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Overview
memories.solution:
Divi 5 provides two customizer interfaces that control the default visual appearance of your entire site. The **Theme Customizer** handles site-wide structural elements such as the header, navigation menus, logo placement, body text, heading typography, footer layout, and general color schemes. The **Module Customizer** controls the default size, font, color, and spacing values for each individual module type, so changes propagate across every instance of that module site-wide.

Both customizers use the WordPress Customizer framework, which means every change you make is previewed live before you publish. This makes it safe to experiment with global style adjustments without affecting the live site until you click **Save & Publish**.

The customizers complement the Visual Builder's per-element styling. Settings made in the customizer act as defaults — they apply everywhere unless overridden at the individual module, row, or section level in the builder. This hierarchy means you can establish a consistent baseline in the customizer and then fine-tune specific instances in the builder as needed.

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Accessing the Customizers > Theme Customizer
memories.solution:
1. Log in to WordPress as an Administrator.
2. Navigate to **Divi > Theme Customizer** in the WordPress admin sidebar.
3. The WordPress Customizer interface opens with Divi's theme panels in the left sidebar and a live preview of your site on the right.

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Accessing the Customizers > Module Customizer
memories.solution:
1. Log in to WordPress as an Administrator.
2. Navigate to **Divi > Module Customizer** in the WordPress admin sidebar.
3. The Customizer opens with a panel for each Divi module type.

!!! tip "Access via the Admin Bar"
    When logged in and viewing the front end of your site, you can also access the Theme Customizer from the WordPress admin bar under **Customize**.

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Theme Customizer Panels
memories.solution: The Theme Customizer organizes settings into several top-level panels, each containing sub-panels for specific site elements.

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Theme Customizer Panels > General Settings
memories.solution:
Controls fundamental site-wide styling properties.

| Sub-Panel | Settings |
|-----------|----------|
| **Layout** | Website content width (px), sidebar width, use boxed layout toggle, section height, row width, gutter width |
| **Typography** | Body text size, body line height, body font, header text size (H1-H6), header font, header font weight, header text color, header letter spacing, header line height |
| **Background** | Default page background color, default page background image, background image position, background size |
| **Color Scheme** | Accent color (site-wide highlight color used for links, buttons, and active states) |

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Theme Customizer Panels > Buttons
memories.solution:

| Button Border Width | Default border thickness |
