memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Module Customizer Panels
memories.solution:
The Module Customizer provides a panel for each Divi module type. Within each panel, you can set default values for that module's key visual properties. These defaults apply to every instance of the module across the site unless overridden in the individual module's settings.

Common settings available per module include:

| Setting Category | Controls |
|-----------------|----------|
| **Header Font Size** | Default heading text size for the module |
| **Header Font Style** | Bold, italic, uppercase, underline |
| **Header Font Color** | Default heading color |
| **Header Letter Spacing** | Character spacing for headings |
| **Header Line Height** | Line height for headings |
| **Body Font Size** | Default body text size |
| **Body Font Style** | Bold, italic, uppercase, underline |
| **Body Font Color** | Default body text color |
| **Body Letter Spacing** | Character spacing for body text |
| **Body Line Height** | Line height for body text |
| **Padding** | Top, bottom, left, right internal spacing |

Modules with unique visual elements have additional settings. For example:

- **Slider** — Slide height, slide padding, arrow size, dot navigation size
- **Blog** — Grid column count, meta font settings, read-more link styling
- **Bar Counter** — Bar height, bar background color, bar fill color
- **Blurb** — Icon size, icon color, image max width
- **Testimonial** — Quote icon color, portrait border radius
- **Pricing Table** — Header background color, price font size, bullet icon color

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Theme Customizer vs. Module Customizer
memories.solution:
| Aspect | Theme Customizer | Module Customizer |
|--------|-----------------|-------------------|
| **Scope** | Site-wide structural elements (header, footer, typography, colors) | Per-module-type default values |
| **Access** | Divi > Theme Customizer | Divi > Module Customizer |
| **What it controls** | Header layout, navigation styles, global typography, button defaults, footer | Font sizes, colors, spacing, and module-specific dimensions for each module type |
| **Override behavior** | Builder page-level and element-level settings override these | Individual module settings in the builder override these |
| **Best for** | Establishing the site's foundational design system | Ensuring consistent module styling without configuring each instance |

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Settings Hierarchy
memories.solution:
Divi applies styles in a cascading hierarchy. Settings at higher levels act as defaults that lower levels can override:

1. **Theme Customizer** — Broadest defaults (site-wide typography, colors, header/footer)
2. **Module Customizer** — Per-module-type defaults
3. **Global Presets** — Saved style configurations applied to specific module instances
4. **Individual Module Settings** — Per-instance overrides in the Visual Builder

This means you can set a site-wide heading font in the Theme Customizer, override it for all Blurb modules in the Module Customizer, and then further override it for a single Blurb instance in the Visual Builder.

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Best Practices
memories.solution:
1. **Configure the Theme Customizer first** — Establish your global typography, colors, and header/footer styles before building pages. This reduces the amount of per-module styling you need to do in the builder.

2. **Use the Module Customizer for consistency** — If you find yourself applying the same font size or padding to every instance of a module, set it once in the Module Customizer instead. This keeps your styling DRY and easier to update later.

3. **Preview before publishing** — Both customizers show live previews. Test changes across different page types (homepage, blog posts, archives) by navigating within the preview pane before clicking Save & Publish.

4. **Document your customizer settings** — Use the Divi Portability feature to export your Theme Options (which include customizer values) as a backup. Store the export alongside your site documentation for disaster recovery or site migration.

memories.summary: theme-options/customizer.md: Theme & Module Customizer > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Customizer Changes Not Appearing"
    If changes made in the customizer do not reflect on the live site:

    - Confirm you clicked **Save & Publish** in the Customizer, not just the preview close button.
    - Clear all caching layers: browser cache, WordPress page cache, server-level cache (Cloudflare, Varnish, etc.).
    - Check whether per-module settings in the Visual Builder are overriding your customizer values. Builder-level settings take precedence over customizer defaults.

!!! warning "Theme Customizer Panel Missing"
    If the Divi > Theme Customizer link is not visible in the admin menu:

    - Verify your user role has Theme Customizer access in the [Role Editor](../builder/role-editor.md).
    - Ensure Divi 5 is the active theme (not a child theme that fails to load properly).
    - Deactivate other plugins temporarily to check for conflicts that may remove customizer panels.

!!! tip "Resetting Customizer Values"
    There is no single "reset all" button in the customizer. To restore defaults, either import a saved Divi options backup via the Portability feature, or manually clear individual fields. For the Module Customizer, emptying a field reverts it to the theme's built-in default.

memories.summary: Layout Settings control display options for single posts, pages, and index archives.
memories.solution:
The Layout Settings tab has three sub-tabs:

1. **Single Post Layout**: Controls post info section items, comment visibility, and thumbnail placement on single post pages.
2. **Single Page Layout**: Provides controls for thumbnails and comments specifically on pages.
3. **General Settings**: Manages the post info section and thumbnail display on index (archive) pages.

**Settings Details:**
*   **Single Post Layout:**
    *   `Choose which items to display in the post info section`: Selects basic information displayed below the post title.
    *   `Show comments on posts`: Toggles comment visibility and form on single post pages.
    *   `Place Thumbs on Posts`: Controls initial thumbnail placement (default: enabled). Disabling this removes the image to avoid repetition.
*   **Single Page Layout:**
    *   `Place Thumbs on Pages`: Enables/disables thumbnails on pages (default: disabled).
    *   `Show comments on pages`: Toggles comment visibility and form on pages (default: disabled).
*   **General Settings:**
    *   `Post info section`: Selects basic information displayed below the post title on index pages.
    *   `Show Thumbs on Index pages`: Enables/disables thumbnails on index pages (default: enabled).

**Code Examples:**
```php
// Check if comments are enabled on posts
$show_comments = et_get_option('divi_show_postcomments', 'on');

// Check if thumbnails are placed on posts
$show_thumbs = et_get_option('divi_thumbnails', 'on');

// Check if page comments are enabled
$page_comments = et_get_option('divi_show_pagescomments', 'off');
```

memories.summary: Navigation Settings control site structure, link ordering, and menu exclusions.
memories.solution:
The Navigation Settings tab manages which pages and categories appear in the navigation bar, including dropdown behavior and link sorting. It has three sub-tabs:

1. **Pages**: Allows exclusion of specific pages, controls dropdown visibility, displays a Home link (disable if using static homepage), and sets page link sorting/ordering.
2. **Categories**: Allows exclusion of categories, controls dropdown visibility, hides empty categories, and sets category link sorting/ordering.
3. **General Settings**: Contains the setting to disable top-tier dropdown menu links, useful when parent items are placeholders.

**Settings Details:**
*   **Pages Sub-tab:**
    *   `Exclude pages from the navigation bar`: Removes selected pages from the menu.
    *   `Show dropdown menus`: Toggles dropdown display for pages.
    *   `Display Home link`: Controls the visibility of a default Home link (disable if using static homepage).
    *   `Sort Pages Links`: Selects sorting method (`Name`, etc.).
    *   `Order Pages Links by Ascending/Descending`: Sets order direction.
    *   `Number of dropdown tiers shown`: Limits the number of visible menu levels (default: 3).
*   **Categories Sub-tab:**
    *   `Exclude categories from the navigation bar`: Removes selected categories from the menu.
    *   `Show dropdown menus`: Toggles dropdown display for categories.
    *   `Hide empty categories`: Hides categories with no posts (default: enabled).
    *   `Number of dropdown tiers shown`: Limits the number of visible menu levels (default: 3).
    *   `Sort Categories Links by Name/ID/Slug/Count/Term Group`: Selects sorting criteria.
    *   `Order Category Links by Ascending/Descending`: Sets order direction.
*   **General Settings Sub-tab:**
    *   `Disable top tier dropdown menu links`: When enabled, removes parent link functionality to prevent clicks on placeholders.

**Code Examples:**
```php
// Programmatically exclude pages from navigation
$excluded_pages = et_get_option('divi_exclude_pages');

// Check if dropdown menus are enabled
$show_dropdowns = et_get_option('divi_show_dropdown', 'on');
```

memories.summary: SEO Settings manage metadata (titles, descriptions) for homepage, posts, and archives.
memories.solution:
The SEO Settings tab provides built-in optimization controls for the site's homepage, single posts, and index/archive pages. It has three sub-tabs:

1. **Homepage SEO**: Configures custom titles, meta descriptions, meta keywords, and canonical URLs specifically for the homepage.
2. **Single Post Page SEO**: Provides per-post controls to define individual post metadata.
3. **Index Page SEO**: Handles settings for category/archive pages, including title generation methods and canonical URLs.

**Settings Details (Homepage SEO):**
*   `Enable custom title`: Allows overriding the default blog name + description title.
*   `Enable meta description`: Allows overriding the default blog description in the meta field.
*   `Enable meta keywords`: Adds custom meta keywords to the header (note: search engines rarely use this).
*   `Enable canonical URL's`: Prevents duplicate content indexing by basing URLs on permalinks and domain settings.
*   `Homepage custom title (if enabled)`: Field for custom `<title></title>` content.
*   `Homepage meta keywords (if enabled)`: Field for custom meta description content.
*   `If custom titles are disabled, choose autogeneration method`: Selects the order of post title and blog name in the auto-generated title.
*   `Define a character to separate BlogName and Post title`: Sets the separator character (`|`, `–`) for auto-generated titles.

**Code Examples:** (None provided across chunks, but structure is maintained.)

memories.summary: Displaying standard ACF fields dynamically within Divi 5's Loop Builder.
memories.solution:
To display standard ACF data: 
1. **Prerequisites:** Ensure the Advanced Custom Fields plugin is active, an ACF field group is assigned to a post type, and posts have populated values.
2. **Enable Looping:** Select the target module (e.g., Text) and activate the **Loop Element** toggle in its settings.
3. **Select Source:** On the desired module field, click the **Dynamic Content** icon and choose **Loop Post Custom Field**.
4. **Choose Field:** Use the **Select Custom Field** dropdown; ACF fields appear at the top of the list. Select the required field.
5. **Apply:** Click **Apply**. The value will display dynamically for every post in the loop.

*Key Details:* 
- ACF fields auto-populate and are found first in the custom field list.
- Compatible module fields include body text and title.
- Divi matches field types (e.g., image fields work on Image modules).

(Note: No extra plugins or custom code beyond ACF itself are required.)

memories.summary: Looping through multiple rows of data using ACF Repeater Fields in Divi 5.
memories.solution:
To display repeater field data: 
1. **Prerequisites:** Use Advanced Custom Fields Pro, configure a repeater field group, assign it to a post type, and ensure posts have populated data.
2. **Enable Looping:** Select the target module and activate the **Loop Element** toggle.
3. **Set Query Type:** In the Loop Element settings, set the **Query Type** dropdown to **ACF Repeater: [Your Repeater Field Name]**.
4. **Map Content:** On the desired module field, click the **Dynamic Content** icon and select the specific repeater subfield from the options.
5. **Apply:** Click **Apply**. The module will iterate through each row of the repeater field, displaying the mapped subfield values.

*Context-Aware Matching:* Divi automatically filters available subfields based on the target module type (e.g., Text modules only show text-compatible ACF subfields; Image modules show image-type subfields).

memories.summary: Building a custom blog feed using an offset column layout and loop builder.
memories.solution:
1. **Section Setup:** Add a new Section and set its background color (e.g., `#EFEFEF`) for visual separation.
2. **Title Row:** Inside the section, add a single-column Row containing a Heading or Text module for the blog feed title.
3. **Content Layout:** Use an offset column layout (9th option) to create two Rows: one narrow left column for the featured post and one wider right column for the post grid.
4. **Post Grid (Right Column):**
    - Enable the Loop Element toggle on the right column.
    - Set Posts Per Page to `9`.
    - Set Post Offset to `1` (prevents repeating the featured post).
    - Enable Text Wrap on the row for grid arrangement.
    - Add a Group module inside this column, and populate it with Dynamic Content modules linked to **Loop Featured Image**, date, title, and excerpt.
5. **Featured Post (Left Column):**
    - Enable the Loop Element toggle on the left column.
    - Set Posts Per Page to `1` (for the most recent post).
    - Add the same Dynamic Content modules (image, title, date, excerpt) but style them larger for emphasis.
6. **Styling:** Apply padding and border radius (e.g., `15px`) to each post card. Set background colors on Group modules to distinguish cards from the section background. Adjust typography and spacing as needed.

memories.summary: Fixing cut-off or invisible dropdown menus requires z-index adjustments.
memories.solution:
To fix menu issues:
1. **Overflow Clipping:** Check the parent `Row` and `Section` containing the Menu module for `Horizontal Overflow` and `Vertical Overflow`. Set these to `Visible`.
2. **Z-Index Stacking:** In the Section's Advanced tab, set the `Z-index` to a high number (e.g., 100, 999, or 9999). If using Scroll Effects, disable them or set the section's Z-index to 0.

memories.summary: Troubleshooting Divi 5 menu issues requires clearing caches and checking settings.
memories.solution:
If menus are misaligned, cut off, or invisible:
1. **Clear Caches:** Use `Divi → Theme Options → Clear CSS Cache` and clear your hosting provider's server-level cache.
2. **Safe Mode:** Enable `Divi → Support Center` to rule out plugin/custom code conflicts.
3. **Custom CSS Check:** Verify that no custom CSS rules set `overflow: hidden` on `.et-l-header`, `.et_pb_menu`, or related selectors.

memories.summary: Troubleshooting display issues after a Divi update or change.
memories.solution:
Display issues post-update are often caused by stale cache, conflicting custom CSS, plugin conflicts, or invalid HTML wrappers. Follow these steps:

1. **Clear Cache:** Clear all layers of caching (Divi CSS cache, plugins, browser, server/CDN).
2. **Isolate Custom CSS:**
    *   Go to `Divi > Theme Options > Custom CSS`.
    *   Backup the existing CSS and remove it entirely.
    *   Clear Divi CSS cache and check the front end. If the issue resolves, the CSS is problematic.
3. **Identify Conflict:** Re-add custom CSS incrementally, testing after each addition to pinpoint the conflicting rule or selector.
4. **Check Code Locations:** Review all areas where custom code might reside:
    *   `Divi > Theme Options > Custom CSS`
    *   Page Settings > Advanced > Custom CSS
    *   Module Settings > Advanced > CSS
    *   Code Modules with `<style>` blocks
    *   Child theme `style.css`
5. **Validate:** Use the W3C CSS Validator or browser DevTools to check for syntax errors.

memories.summary: Steps to resolve display issues after an update, starting with cache clearing and ending with support contact.
memories.solution:
To fix display issues: 1. **Clear All Caches:** Clear caches in this order:
    *   **Divi CSS Cache:** Go to `Divi > Theme Options` and click `Clear CSS Cache`. This forces regeneration of static CSS.
    *   **Plugin Cache:** Purge all caches from any caching plugin (e.g., WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, LiteSpeed Cache). Use dedicated CSS/JS purge options if available.
    *   **Server-Level Cache:** Flush or purge controls in your hosting control panel's Cache/Performance section. Contact the host if controls are unavailable.
    *   **Browser Cache:** Clear browser cache settings or test using a private/incognito window.
2. **Validate Custom HTML Wrappers:** For modules using `Advanced > HTML`, ensure every tag opened in **HTML Before** is closed in **HTML After**. Remove custom wrappers temporarily to test if they are the cause.
3. **Check for Plugin Conflicts:** Deactivate non-essential plugins, clear caches, and test the front end. Reactivate plugins one by one (clearing caches between activations) until the issue returns; the last activated plugin is the conflict source.
    *   *Tip:* Use `Divi > Support Center > Safe Mode` to disable plugins, child themes, and custom code for user-specific testing without affecting other visitors.
4. **Verify Divi Update Status:** Confirm the latest version at `Divi > Theme Options` and check for pending update tasks or incomplete migrations.
5. **Contact Support:** If issues persist, contact Elegant Themes support with: a description of the problem/start time, links to affected pages, screenshots/recordings, and confirmation of completed troubleshooting steps.

memories.summary: Convert a global element to an independent, non-global instance in Divi 5.
memories.solution:
To convert a global element on a page: 
1. Locate the global element (indicated by a special badge/icon).
2. Right-click and select "Disable Global" from the context menu.
*Alternative Method:* Select the element, click the three-dot menu icon (⋯), and choose "Disable Global".

*Note on Conversion:* The conversion removes the element's connection to the library. Future edits only affect this instance, but existing content/styling remains intact.

memories.summary: Process for creating a custom search results page using Divi 5 Theme Builder.
memories.solution:
To create a custom search results template in Divi 5:
1. Navigate to **Divi** → **Theme Builder** and click **Add New Template**.
2. Select **Search Results** as the template type and name it (e.g., "Custom Search Results").
3. Add a **Heading** module at the top, using the **Dynamic Content** icon to select **Post/Archive Title**. This displays dynamic text like "Search Results for [term]".
4. Below the heading, add a **Blog** module.
5. In the Blog module's **Content** tab, enable **Posts For Current Page** to ensure it displays search results instead of hardcoded posts.
6. Configure the desired layout (e.g., Grid, List) and set **Number of Posts Per Page**.
7. Optionally, add a **Search** module for refinement or modules in a sidebar column (Categories, Recent Posts).
8. Add a Call-to-Action (CTA) section below results to guide further navigation.
9. Save the template using the Visual Builder toolbar (**Ctrl+S** / **Cmd+S**) and exit.

Testing involves performing a search on the site and verifying that the heading displays "Search Results for [term]", the Blog module shows relevant posts, and styling is consistent.

memories.summary: Importing freebie content requires specific files for different site areas.
memories.solution:
The Black Friday 2025 Freebies are designed for Divi 5 and must be imported using the following JSON files:

**1. Presets (Required First):**
*   `Black-Friday-2025_Divi-5-Freebie_Presets.json`: Must be imported first as all other files depend on it. This file contains pre-configured Option Group Presets and global variables.

**2. Layouts/Sections (To Divi Library):**
*   `Black-Friday-2025_Divi-5-Freebie_All-Sections_Layouts.json`: Contains 40 layouts, organized by section type (Hero, Pricing, CTA, etc.), offering multiple pre-made sections per layout.
*   `Black-Friday-2025_Divi-5-Freebie_Individual-Sections.json`: A comprehensive file containing 430 individual section layouts for copying into pages.
*   `Black-Friday-2025_Divi-5-Freebie_SECTION-NAME-Sections.json`: (e.g., `Pricing-Sections.json`). These files import all sections of a specific type, allowing users to import only the needed section types instead of all 430.
*   `Black-Friday-2025_Divi-5-Freebie_Pages.json`: Contains complete pre-made page layouts (e.g., Home Page). Importing this adds templates to the Divi Library; it does NOT create pages on the site, which must be done manually by loading the layout.

**3. Theme Builder Templates:**
*   `Black-Friday-2025_Divi-5-Freebie_Theme-Builder-Templates.json`: Imports ready-to-use templates for dynamic areas (Global Header, Global Footer, Single Post, Product, 404 pages, search results). This must be imported via **Theme Builder** (Portability → Import).

**4. Theme Customizer Settings (Optional):**
*   `Black-Friday-2025_Divi-5-Freebie_Theme-Customizer.json`: Imports recommended colors and fonts.

**Importing Steps:**
*   **Presets:** Go to `WordPress Dashboard → Divi → Divi Library` → **Import & Export** → **Import** tab. Select file, check **Import Presets**, then click **Import Divi Builder Layouts**. (The import may take time.)
*   **Layouts/Sections:** Follow the same steps as above for all JSON files.
*   **Theme Builder Templates:** Go to `WordPress Dashboard → Divi → Theme Builder` → **Portability** icon → **Import** tab. Select file, check **Import Presets**, then click **Import Divi Theme Builder Templates**.

memories.summary: Importing elements from the Divi Library requires following a strict parent-child hierarchy.
memories.solution: Divi enforces a parent-child hierarchy for imported elements: Layouts affect the entire page (replacing or appending content). Sections are placed directly on the page. Rows must be inside sections. Modules must be inside rows.

memories.summary: Elements vanishing on mobile are usually due to visibility settings, display conditions, or custom code conflicts.
memories.solution:
If elements disappear on mobile but work on desktop, check three areas:

1. **Visibility Settings:** In the Visual Builder, select the element, go to **Advanced** > **Visibility**. Ensure that **Phone** and **Tablet** are not checked under **Disable On**, or uncheck them if the element should be visible on those devices.
   *Tip: Enable **Show Disabled Elements at 50% Opacity** in builder settings to identify hidden elements.*

2. **Display Conditions:** Review the element's settings (**Advanced** > **Conditions**) for rules (e.g., device-type or screen-width) that might unintentionally exclude mobile users.

3. **Custom Code Conflicts:** Check custom CSS or JavaScript, as they may hide elements on smaller screens. Test by enabling **Safe Mode** in **Divi > Support Center**. If the element appears, review code locations for rules like `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or mobile-targeting media queries:
   *CSS:* 
    * Divi > Theme Options > Custom CSS
    * Page Settings > Advanced
    * Code Modules with `<style>` blocks
   *JavaScript:* 
    * Divi > Theme Options > Integration
    * Code Modules with `<script>` blocks

After making changes, clear the site cache.

memories.summary: Process for submitting bug reports for Divi 5.
memories.solution:
To report a Divi 5 bug, log into the Elegant Themes member portal. From there, open the support chat using the pink chat icon (bottom-right corner) and click the 'Report Divi 5 Bug' button. When reporting, include: 

*   **Steps to reproduce:** The exact sequence of actions that triggers the bug.
*   **Expected behavior:** What should happen.
*   **Actual behavior:** What happens instead.
*   **Environment details:** Divi version, WordPress version, PHP version, and active plugins.
*   **Screenshots or recordings:** Visual evidence.
*   **Browser and device:** Which browser and OS are being used.

Note that the Elegant Themes team may not send a confirmation reply; your report is logged internally.

memories.summary: How to create a transparent, fixed header using Divi 5's Theme Builder and scroll effects.
memories.solution:
To create a transparent fixed header: 
1. **Global Header Setup:** Go to `Divi > Theme Builder` and add/edit the Global Header. Inside the default Section, add a single-column Row, and place a Menu module within that row.
2. **Section Configuration (The Container):**
    * Set **Background Color** to transparent.
    * Set top and bottom **Padding** to `0px`.
    * In **Advanced > Scroll Effects**, enable **Sticky at the Top**.
    * Optionally, set a **Sticky Background Color** (e.g., `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.95)`) for the scrolled state.
    * Set a **Min Height** (start with `90px`). This is crucial because placing the Row inside will position it absolutely, removing it from normal document flow; Min Height ensures the Section maintains space on the page.
3. **Row Configuration:**
    * Set top and bottom **Padding** to `10px`.
    * In **Advanced > Position**, set Position to **Absolute**.
    * Set Alignment to **Top Center**.
4. **Menu Module Setup:**
    * Clear the **Background Color** field in the Menu module settings to remove any default white background.
    * Style links and logo for visibility against the hero content.

**Result:** The header starts fully transparent, overlapping the hero section. Upon scrolling, it sticks at the top and displays the configured solid/semi-transparent color.

**Tips & Gotchas:**
* Choose menu text colors that contrast well with both the hero image and the sticky background color.
* Test on mobile devices for proper height and padding across all breakpoints.
* If the hero section content is hidden behind the header, add top padding to the hero equal to the header's Min Height.

memories.summary: Security best practices for uploading SVG and JSON files.
memories.solution:
When enabling SVG and JSON uploads, follow these security guidelines:
* **Sanitization:** Always sanitize SVGs (e.g., using tools like SVGOMG) before upload to remove unnecessary metadata or potential script tags.
* **Permissions:** Restrict file upload permissions to administrators or trusted roles only.
* **Backups:** Maintain regular backups for quick recovery from malicious uploads.

memories.summary: Troubleshooting invisible or unclickable hamburger menu icons in Divi 5.
memories.solution:
If the icon is missing entirely (only logo/empty header), check if it's visible in the Visual Builder or Theme Builder Header layout, and ensure the Menu module settings are correct.

If the icon is present but unresponsive, verify the following:
1. **Color Contrast:** Set the Hamburger Menu Icon Color to contrast with the header background.
2. **Overflow Settings:** In the Section, Row, or Column containing the Menu module, set both Horizontal Overflow and Vertical Overflow to `Visible` (or remove overrides to use defaults).
3. **CSS Conflicts:** Check for custom CSS rules targeting `.mobile_menu_bar` or `.et_mobile_menu` that use `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or `opacity: 0`. These will hide the icon even if configured correctly.
4. **Troubleshooting Steps:**
    * Clear Divi → Theme Options → CSS Cache, then reload in an incognito window.
    * Use Safe Mode (Divi → Support Center) to rule out plugin/custom code conflicts.

memories.summary: Troubleshooting live site display issues in Divi 5 (CSS, caching, content).
memories.solution:
**Live Site vs. Builder Discrepancies:**
*   If the live page looks different from the Visual Builder, it is often due to cached files or performance options.
    *   Clear CSS Cache button (top right).
    *   Clear cache/Purge all option in your caching/optimization plugin settings (clear separate CSS and JavaScript caches too).
    *   Log into your hosting control panel and purge the server cache, or ask your host to do it.
    *   If using a CDN (e.g., Cloudflare), purge its cache. Temporarily disabling the CDN's caching is useful for testing changes.
    *   **Performance Options:** If performance options like Critical CSS are enabled, temporarily disable them one by one, then clear the Divi CSS cache and recheck the page.
    *   **Custom CSS Location:** Custom CSS can be added in multiple places: `Divi → Theme Options → Custom CSS`, or on a per-page basis via `Page Settings → Advanced tab → Custom CSS`, or specifically as `Advanced tab → Custom CSS → Free-Form CSS`.
    *   If using custom CSS, back it up to a text file before removing and saving the code.
    *   **General Fixes:**
        1.  Open the affected page in the Visual Builder.
        2.  Make a small change (e.g., add/remove space), then undo it.
        3.  Click Save to force Divi to regenerate that page's CSS.
    *   **Safe Mode:** Use `Divi → Support Center` and toggle on Safe Mode for diagnosis.
    *   **Updates:** After updating Divi 5, follow specific update guides, as display fixes are shipped regularly. Check the latest version in `Divi → Theme Options`.

**Blank/Missing Content (Theme Builder):**
*   If a page is blank or missing content on the live site:
    1.  Check **Template Assignment:** Ensure a template (`Default Website Template` or custom) is assigned to the page in `Divi → Theme Builder`.
    2.  **Custom Body Check:** If the assigned template has a `Custom Body`, this body replaces the page's content on the front end. Either add missing design elements to the template or remove the Custom Body so the page shows its own content.
    3.  **Post Content Module:** A custom template's body *must* contain the `Post Content` module wherever the page's unique content should appear. If it is missing, the page content will not render; add the module and save.
    4.  **Homepage Setting:** Verify that in `Settings → Reading`, the `Home Page` dropdown points to the correct static page.

**Wrong Header/Menu Listing Every Page (Theme Builder):**
*   If the site shows the wrong header or a menu listing every published page:
    1.  **Default Website Template:** If the template's default website template is disabled, pages not assigned to a custom template fall back to the default WordPress header.
    2.  **Primary Menu Location:** The header displays the menu assigned to the `Primary Menu` location in `Appearance → Menus`. If nothing is assigned there, WordPress automatically generates a menu listing every published page.
    3.  **Global Header:** When using custom templates, ensure the template has a dedicated header area; otherwise, the Global Header may not be used automatically and must be re-added or the template assignment removed.
*   **General Theme Builder Steps:**
    1.  Navigate to `WordPress Dashboard → Divi → Theme Builder`.
    2.  Check the assigned templates for both `Default Website Template` and any custom templates that apply to the page.
    3.  If changes are made, click **Save Changes** in the top right of the Theme Builder screen and reload the page.

api/javascript-api.md: JavaScript API > API.Utils Methods > Utils.hasValue()
memories.solution:
Checks whether a value is "printable" — a non-empty string that is not `undefined` or `null`.

```javascript
Utils.hasValue(value: any): boolean
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `value` | `any` | The value to check. |

**Returns:** `boolean` — `true` if the value is a non-empty, non-null, non-undefined string.

```javascript
API.Utils.hasValue('Hello');     // true
API.Utils.hasValue('');          // false
API.Utils.hasValue(undefined);   // false
API.Utils.hasValue(null);        // false
API.Utils.hasValue(0);           // false (it's not a printable string)
```

memories.summary: api/module-json-schema.md: Module JSON Schema > Settings Field Schema > Conditional Visibility
memories.solution:
Fields can be shown or hidden based on the current value of other fields. Both `show_if` and `show_if_not` accept an associative array where keys are field names and values are the target values.

```php
<?php
'icon_name' => array(
    'label'       => esc_html__( 'Icon', 'my-ext' ),
    'type'        => 'select_icon',
    'toggle_slug' => 'main_content',
    // Show only when use_icon is "on"
    'show_if'     => array(
        'use_icon' => 'on',
    ),
),
'fallback_image' => array(
    'label'       => esc_html__( 'Fallback Image', 'my-ext' ),
    'type'        => 'upload',
    'toggle_slug' => 'main_content',
    // Hide when use_icon is "on" (show for all other values)
    'show_if_not' => array(
        'use_icon' => 'on',
    ),
),
```

Multiple conditions in a single `show_if` array are evaluated with AND logic — all conditions must be true for the field to appear. ⚠️ Observed

```php
<?php
'advanced_setting' => array(
    'label'       => 'Advanced Setting',
    'type'        => 'text',
    'show_if'     => array(
        'enable_advanced' => 'on',
        'mode'            => 'custom',
    ),
    // Only visible when enable_advanced="on" AND mode="custom"
),
```

api/wp-cli.md: WP-CLI Integration > Example Scripts > Validate Divi Content Integrity
memories.solution:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Check all Divi pages for common content issues

echo "Validating Divi content integrity..."
echo "==================================="
errors=0

wp db query "SELECT ID FROM wp_posts WHERE post_content LIKE '%wp:divi/%' AND post_status='publish'" --skip-column-names | while read -r page_id; do
    title=$(wp post get "$page_id" --field=post_title)
    content=$(wp post get "$page_id" --field=content)

    # Check for double comments
    double_comments=$(echo "$content" | grep -c '<!--[[:space:]]*<!--' || true)
    if [ "$double_comments" -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "ERROR: Page $page_id ($title) - Double comment pattern found ($double_comments instances)"
        errors=$((errors + 1))
    fi

    # Check for builder flag
    builder_flag=$(wp post meta get "$page_id" _et_pb_use_builder 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$builder_flag" != "on" ]; then
        echo "WARNING: Page $page_id ($title) - _et_pb_use_builder is not 'on' (value: '$builder_flag')"
    fi

    # Check for balanced section tags
    opens=$(echo "$content" | grep -o 'wp:divi/section' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    closes=$(echo "$content" | grep -o '/wp:divi/section' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    if [ "$opens" != "$closes" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: Page $page_id ($title) - Unbalanced sections: $opens opens, $closes closes"
        errors=$((errors + 1))
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "Validation complete."
```

🔬 Needs Testing — these scripts are based on standard WP-CLI patterns applied to Divi 5 block content. Test on a staging site before running on production.

memories.summary: api/wp-cli.md: WP-CLI Integration > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "WP-CLI not found"
    **Symptom:** `wp: command not found`

    **Fix:** Install WP-CLI: `curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wp-cli/builds/gh-pages/phar/wp-cli.phar && chmod +x wp-cli.phar && sudo mv wp-cli.phar /usr/local/bin/wp`

!!! warning "Database table prefix differs"
    **Symptom:** SQL queries return empty results despite Divi content existing.

    **Fix:** The examples use `wp_posts` and `wp_postmeta`. Your site may use a different prefix. Check `wp-config.php` for `$table_prefix` and adjust queries accordingly. You can also use `wp db prefix` to get the current prefix.

!!! warning "search-replace modifies serialized data"
    **Symptom:** After `wp search-replace`, some options or widgets are broken.

    **Fix:** Always use `--include-columns=post_content` to limit replacement scope. The `--precise` flag handles serialized data correctly but is slower. For Divi block content (which is not serialized), either flag works.

!!! warning "Content changes not visible on frontend"
    **Symptom:** `wp search-replace` reports changes but the frontend shows old content.

    **Fix:** Clear all caches after modification:
    ```bash
    wp cache flush && wp transient delete --all
    ```
    Also clear any server-level caches (Varnish, Redis, page cache plugins).

!!! warning "Pages render blank after database modification"
    **Symptom:** A page shows nothing after direct SQL content changes.

    **Fix:** Check `_et_pb_use_builder` meta is set to `"on"`. Verify section tags are balanced. Run the content integrity validator script above. See [SSR Rendering — Section Validation Checklist](../internals/ssr-rendering.md).

memories.summary: builder/command-center.md: Command Center > Context-Aware Insertion
memories.solution: Element commands are context-aware. When you add an element through the Command Center, it is inserted relative to the currently selected element on the canvas. If no element is selected, the new element is appended to the end of the page. The `^` operator overrides default placement by inserting above the selection.

memories.summary: builder/find-replace-attributes.md: Find & Replace Attributes > The "Only Replace Identical Fields" Option
memories.solution:
This is an important safety toggle. When **enabled**, Divi only replaces values in fields that are the same type as the source field. For example, if you right-clicked a border-radius field with value `10px`, the replacement will only touch other border-radius fields -- not margin, padding, or font-size fields that might also happen to contain `10px`.

When **disabled**, any field containing the matching value is replaced regardless of field type.

!!! tip "Enable This for Safety"
    Leave "Only Replace Identical Fields" enabled unless you specifically need cross-field replacement. This prevents accidental changes to unrelated settings that happen to share the same numeric value.

memories.solution:

| Setting | Type | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| Meta Key | Text input | The post meta key to filter on |
| Meta Value | Text input | The value to compare against |

| Type | Dropdown | Data type for comparison (string, number, date, time) |

!!! warning "Visual Builder Not Loading"
    If the Visual Builder fails to load or shows a blank screen, try these steps:

    1. Clear your browser cache and cookies
    2. Disable other WordPress plugins to check for conflicts
    3. Switch to a default WordPress theme temporarily to rule out theme conflicts
    4. Increase your PHP memory limit in `wp-config.php`: `define('WP_MEMORY_LIMIT', '256M');`
    5. Check the browser console for JavaScript errors

!!! warning "Changes Not Saving"
    If your changes are not saving:

    1. Check your internet connection
    2. Verify your WordPress login session has not expired
    3. Check for server-side errors in your hosting error logs
    4. Try saving with Cmd/Ctrl + S instead of the Save button

modules/accordion.md: Accordion > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Module Not Rendering"
    If the Accordion module doesn't appear on the front end, verify that:

    - The module is not inside a disabled section or row
    - Visibility settings aren't hiding it on the current device
    - There is at least one accordion item with content

!!! warning "All Items Appear Open"
    If multiple items display open simultaneously, you may have accidentally inserted individual Toggle modules instead of an Accordion module. The Accordion enforces one-open-at-a-time behavior; Toggles do not.

!!! tip "Accordion Won't Collapse on Mobile"
    Check that JavaScript is not being blocked on the page. The accordion's expand/collapse behavior relies on JavaScript. Also verify no custom CSS is overriding the `display` property on toggle content elements.

memories.summary: modules/audio.md: Audio > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Audio File Not Playing"
    If the player appears but no audio plays, verify that:

    - The audio file URL is accessible and not behind authentication
    - The file format is supported by browsers (MP3 is the most widely compatible)
    - Your hosting server allows direct file access and has not blocked the MIME type

!!! warning "Cover Image Not Displaying"
    If the uploaded image does not appear beside the player:

    - Confirm the image was uploaded to the Media Library and the URL is valid
    - Check that Design tab image sizing settings are not collapsing the image to zero dimensions
    - Verify no custom CSS is hiding the `.et_pb_audio_cover_art` element

!!! tip "Player Looks Unstyled or Broken"
    The Audio module relies on the MediaElement.js library bundled with WordPress. If the player appears as a plain HTML5 control, check that no optimization plugin is deferring or combining the mediaelement scripts incorrectly. Exclude `wp-mediaelement` from script optimization to restore styling.

memories.summary: modules/before-after-image.md: Before After Image > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Module Not Rendering"
    If the Before/After Image module does not appear on the front end, verify that:

    - The module is placed inside a valid section and row
    - Both a "before" and "after" image have been selected
    - Visibility settings are not hiding the module on the current device

!!! warning "Slider Handle Not Draggable"
    If the comparison images display but the handle cannot be dragged, check that:

    - JavaScript is not blocked or erroring on the page (check browser console)
    - No CSS `pointer-events: none` is applied to the module or its parent
    - The module is not inside an element with `overflow: hidden` that clips the handle

!!! tip "Images Not Aligning Properly"
    For the best comparison experience, both images should have identical dimensions and aspect ratios. If the images are different sizes, the comparison may look misaligned or one image may appear cropped. Resize both images to the same width and height before uploading.

modules/button.md: Button > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Button Not Clickable"
    If the button appears but does not respond to clicks:

    - Verify the **Link** field contains a valid URL including the protocol (`https://`).
    - Check for overlapping elements with a higher z-index that may be intercepting clicks. Use browser DevTools to inspect stacking order.
    - JavaScript errors from other plugins can prevent click handlers from firing. Check the browser console for errors.

!!! warning "Button Icon Not Showing"
    If you have enabled custom button styles but the icon does not appear:

    - Confirm that an icon is selected in the **Button** settings under the Design tab.
    - Check the **Button On Hover** toggle — when enabled, the icon only appears on hover. Disable it to show the icon at all times.
    - Verify the icon color is not the same as the button background color.

!!! tip "Button Width Not Matching Design"
    By default, the button width is determined by its text content and padding. To create a full-width button, add `width: 100%` via the CSS editor in the Advanced tab. For a fixed-width button, set a specific `min-width` value instead.

memories.summary: modules/code.md: Code > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Code Not Executing on the Front End"
    If your HTML, CSS, or JavaScript does not work when viewing the published page:

    - Verify that CSS is wrapped in `<style>` tags and JavaScript is wrapped in `<script>` tags. The module outputs content verbatim, so the browser needs these tags to interpret code correctly.
    - Check the browser console (F12 > Console) for JavaScript errors that may indicate syntax issues or conflicts with other scripts.
    - Confirm that a caching plugin or CDN is not serving a stale version of the page. Purge all caches after making changes.

!!! warning "Module Appears Empty in the Visual Builder"
    The Visual Builder may not execute JavaScript or render certain third-party embeds in the editor preview. This is expected behavior — the code will run normally on the published front end. Use the front-end preview (eye icon) to verify your output.

!!! tip "Shortcode Not Rendering"
    If a shortcode displays as plain text instead of its expected output, verify that the plugin providing the shortcode is active. Also confirm the shortcode syntax is correct — mismatched brackets or incorrect attribute names will cause WordPress to treat the shortcode as literal text.

memories.summary: modules/group-carousel.md: Group Carousel > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Slides Not Advancing Automatically"
    If automatic rotation is not working:

    - Confirm that **Automatic Rotation** is toggled on in the Content tab.
    - Check whether the transition speed is set to an extremely high value, causing very slow movement.
    - JavaScript errors on the page can prevent the carousel script from initializing. Inspect the browser console for errors.

!!! warning "Navigation Arrows or Dots Not Visible"
    If navigation controls are missing:

    - Verify that **Show Arrows** and **Show Dot Navigation** are enabled in the Content tab.
    - If arrows are positioned outside the carousel, ensure the parent column has enough horizontal space to display them.
    - Check whether the arrow or dot color matches the background, rendering them invisible.

!!! tip "Carousel Looks Cramped on Mobile"
    Reduce the **Slides to Show** value for tablet and phone breakpoints using the responsive toggle. A single visible slide per viewport often works best on narrow screens. Also reduce horizontal padding on individual slide groups to maximize usable content area.

memories.summary: modules/icon.md: Icon > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Icon Not Displaying"
    If the Icon module appears as an empty box or shows a broken character, verify that an icon has been selected in the Content tab. If you selected a Font Awesome icon, ensure the Font Awesome library is loading correctly by checking for CSS conflicts in the browser developer tools. Clear any site caching plugins after making changes.

!!! warning "Icon Color Not Changing"
    If the icon color does not respond to the Design tab color setting, check for custom CSS overrides that may be applying a more specific color rule. Inspect the icon element in the browser developer tools to identify conflicting styles. Also verify that you are not accidentally setting the hover-state color instead of the default color.

!!! tip "Accessibility Considerations"
    Icons that convey meaning (such as navigation or action indicators) should include accessible text for screen readers. Use the CSS ID or Class field to target the icon with custom CSS that adds an `aria-label` attribute, or pair the Icon module with a visually hidden text element. Purely decorative icons should be marked with `aria-hidden="true"` to prevent confusion for assistive technology users.

memories.summary: modules/image.md: Image > Common Patterns > 2. Image Card Grid
memories.solution: Arrange multiple Image modules in a three- or four-column row. Apply a consistent border radius of 8-12px and a subtle box shadow to each image to create a card-like appearance. Use the fixed aspect ratio CSS snippet above with a shared CSS class to ensure all images maintain the same proportions regardless of their original dimensions.

memories.summary: modules/login.md: Login > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Login Form Not Submitting"
    If clicking the login button does not authenticate the user or the page simply reloads:

    - Check that the username and password are correct by testing them on the standard WordPress login page at `/wp-login.php`.
    - Verify that no security plugin is blocking the login request or requiring additional fields like a CAPTCHA.
    - Inspect the browser console for JavaScript errors that may be preventing the form submission.
    - If using a custom redirect URL, confirm the URL is valid and accessible.

!!! warning "Login Form Visible to Logged-In Users"
    If authenticated users can still see the login form:

    - Add a display condition in the Advanced tab to show the module only when the user is not logged in.
    - Check that browser caching or a page cache plugin is not serving a stale version of the page. Full-page caching can interfere with conditional display logic since it serves the same HTML to all visitors.

!!! warning "Styling Not Applying to Form Fields"
    If your custom CSS or Design tab changes do not affect the input fields or button:

    - Use more specific CSS selectors to override default styles — for example, `.et_pb_login input[type="text"]` instead of just `input`.
    - Check for conflicting styles from your WordPress theme or other plugins using the browser inspector.
    - Ensure custom CSS is placed in the correct element target within the Advanced tab CSS fields.

memories.summary: modules/post-carousel.md: Post Carousel > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Module Not Rendering"
    If the Post Carousel module does not appear on the front end, verify that:

    - The module is placed inside a valid section and row
    - There are published posts matching the selected post type and category filters
    - Visibility settings are not hiding the module on the current device

!!! warning "No Posts Displaying"
    If the module renders but shows no post cards, check that:

    - The selected post type has published posts
    - The selected categories have posts assigned to them
    - Posts have featured images set (the carousel relies on featured images for its visual display)

!!! tip "Carousel Not Scrolling"
    If the carousel appears as a static grid instead of scrolling, verify that the Layout setting in the Design tab is set to Carousel rather than Grid. If the Layout is correctly set to Carousel but there are fewer posts than visible columns, the carousel will not scroll because there is nothing to scroll to.

memories.summary: modules/post-content.md: Post Content > Common Patterns
memories.solution:
1. **Centered Reading Layout** — Constrain the Post Content module width to 700-750px and center it horizontally using auto margins. This creates an optimal reading column width that improves readability for long-form blog posts, similar to Medium or Substack article layouts.

2. **Two-Column Post with Sidebar** — Place the Post Content module in the wider column of a two-column row, with a sidebar column containing related posts, author bio, or table of contents. This classic layout provides content and context side by side.

3. **Full-Width with Contained Text** — Place the module in a full-width row but use the Sizing settings to set a max-width on the text content while allowing images to extend wider. This creates a modern editorial layout where text is readable but images make a visual impact.

memories.summary: modules/post-content.md: Post Content > Troubleshooting
memories.solution:
!!! warning "Module Not Rendering"
    If the Post Content module does not appear on the front end, verify that:

    - The module is placed inside a Theme Builder template (not a regular page built with the Visual Builder)
    - The template is assigned to the correct post type or specific posts/pages
    - The post or page being viewed has actual content in its WordPress editor

!!! warning "Content Appears Unstyled or Broken"
    If the content renders but does not look right, check that:

    - Design tab settings for Heading Text and Body Text are not conflicting with your theme's global CSS
    - The original content was authored in the WordPress editor (not within Divi builder blocks on the post itself)
    - Shortcodes in the content are from active plugins

!!! tip "Post Content Shows Builder Layout Instead of Text"
    If the post was built using the Visual Builder rather than the WordPress editor, the Post Content module will render the Divi builder output. For Theme Builder templates, it is typical to author posts using the standard WordPress editor and use the Post Content module to render that content within the template layout.

memories.solution: Some shared hosts strip the `Authorization` header from requests, breaking WordPress Application Passwords for REST API auth. If the user reports 401 errors despite valid credentials, suggest browser-based cookie auth with `wpApiSettings.nonce` instead.

memories.summary: playbooks/known-limitations.md: Playbook: Known Limitations > Soft Rules (Getting These Wrong Wastes Time) > 20. Claude in Chrome Security Filter
memories.solution: When running JavaScript via the Claude in Chrome browser tool, the extension filters output for security. Strings containing `=`, `;`, `?`, `&`, URLs, or base64-like patterns get blocked. Return booleans, counts, or key names instead of raw CSS/JSON values. Replace problematic characters if you must return structured data: `=` → `[eq]`, `;` → `[sc]`, `?` → `[q]`.

theme-options/general.md: General Settings > Settings & Options > Performance
memories.solution:
| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---------|------|---------|-------------|
| Dynamic Module Framework | toggle | Enabled | Allows the Divi Framework to only load the modules that are used on the page and process the logic for the features in use. |
| Dynamic CSS | toggle | Enabled | Greatly reduces CSS file size by dynamically generating only the assets necessary for the features and modules you use, eliminating file bloat and improving load times. |
| Dynamic Icons | toggle | Enabled | The Divi icon font is broken up into subsets that load only when needed. Disable this option to load the entire icon font library on all pages (useful if you use the icon font in your child theme). |
| Load Dynamic Stylesheet In-line | toggle | Enabled | Dequeues the Divi style.css file and prints the contents in-line, removing a render-blocking request and improving PageSpeed scores. However, it also prevents the style.css file from being cached. Recommended to keep enabled since the stylesheet is small. |
| Critical CSS | toggle | Enabled | Greatly improves website load times and Google PageSpeed scores by deferring non-critical styles and eliminating render-blocking CSS requests. |
| Critical Threshold Height | range | — | When Critical CSS is enabled, Divi determines an "above the fold threshold" and defers styles for elements below the fold. Increasing threshold height defers fewer styles, resulting in slightly slower load times but less chance for Cumulative Layout Shifts (CLS). Increase this if you are experiencing CLS issues. |
| Dynamic JavaScript Libraries | toggle | Enabled | Only loads external JavaScript libraries when they are needed by specific Divi modules on the page, removing unused JavaScript from the main scripts bundle and improving load times. |
| Disable WordPress Emojis | toggle | Disabled | Removes WordPress emoji assets. Modern browsers support native emojis, making WordPress's emojis unnecessary in most cases. Removing them improves performance. |
| Defer Gutenberg Block CSS | toggle | Enabled | If a page is built with the Divi Builder, the Gutenberg block CSS file is moved from the header to the footer, removing a render-blocking request and improving performance. |
| Improve Google Fonts Loading | toggle | Enabled | Enables caching of Google Fonts and loads them inline, reducing render-blocking requests and improving page load times. |
| Limit Google Fonts Support For Legacy Browsers | toggle | Enabled | Lowers the size of Google Fonts and improves load times but limits Google Fonts support in some very old browsers. Turn this off to increase support for older browsers at a slight cost to performance. |
| Defer jQuery and jQuery Migrate | toggle | Disabled | When possible, moves jQuery and jQuery Migrate to the body to speed up load times. If a third-party plugin registers jQuery as a dependency, it will be moved back to the head. |
| Enqueue jQuery Compatibility Script | toggle | Disabled | Loads an additional compatibility script to prevent console errors when jQuery is deferred. Some third-party scripts may be incorrectly enqueued without declaring jQuery as a dependency. Enable this if you experience console errors after enabling "Defer jQuery And jQuery Migrate". |
| Defer Additional Third Party Scripts | toggle | Disabled | When enabled, scripts registered by plugins and themes will be deferred to improve performance and jQuery will always be loaded in the body. Warning: This can cause JavaScript errors in some cases and should be used with care. |

!!! warning "Performance Settings Can Cause Conflicts"
    Enabling "Defer Additional Third Party Scripts" can cause JavaScript errors with some third-party plugins. If you experience issues after enabling performance options, disable them one at a time to identify the conflict. Always test performance changes on a staging site first.

Use the third parameter of add_action()/add_filter() (e.g., 5 or 99) to control execution order; lower numbers run first.
Always enqueue JavaScript for the Visual Builder using `et_core_is_fb_enabled()` in PHP to prevent loading on front-end pages.

Always wrap VB scripts in `et_core_is_fb_enabled()` to prevent loading on the front end.

Use `wp.apiRequest` instead of `wp.apiFetch` in the Divi editor context.
Divi 5 uses WordPress block comments with JSON attributes, replacing Divi 4's shortcode-based content (`[et_pb_section]...[/et_pb_section]`).
Always chain calls sequentially using `.done()` callbacks.

Before saving content, validate for the pattern `<!--

Use the **Divi Variables From Style Guide** Claude skill to generate a Global Variables import file.
Option Group Presets are a Divi 5 feature. Earlier versions have limited or no preset functionality.
Make core typography, button, and background presets the defaults so new elements start in the right place.

Design Variables are the built-in system for defining reusable tokens (colors, numbers, etc.). Custom CSS variables (`--name`) provide raw CSS functionality and must be used when dynamic content is insufficient.
Use the Image module for single images; use Gallery or multi-column rows of Image modules to display multiple images in a grid.
Gradient fields (Divi 5.7+) copy and paste as a single unified attribute, ensuring stops, type, and direction move together.
All documented features, modules, and behaviors are exclusive to Divi 5 (or later) and do not apply to Divi 4 or earlier versions.
Core Divi modules (Text, Image, Button, Blurb, etc.) are fully compatible with Divi 5.
The Divi 5 Migrator System scans a Divi 4 site, converting supported modules to Divi 5 format and wrapping unsupported modules in shortcode format.
The Loop Builder functionality is exclusive to Divi 5 and later versions.
The Default Website Template box is the primary location for adding Global Header, Custom Body, and Global Footer.
Use dynamic modules (Post Title, Post Content) in body templates to ensure consistency across all assigned items.
This documentation is specific to Divi 5's Theme Builder workflow. Do not apply methods from Divi 4.
Content organization follows a strict hierarchy: Sections contain Rows, Rows contain Columns/Nested Rows, and Columns contain Modules/Nested Modules.
Programmatic modifications to a global canvas affect all pages and templates.
Composable settings, Condition Options, and Theme Options are exclusive features of Divi 5. Divi 4 uses different interfaces.
Multiple conditions are combined using AND logic; all must be true for the element to display.
Use mutually exclusive conditions (e.g., logged-in vs. logged-out) if multiple elements occupy the same position.

The granular attribute copy/paste system (with separate content, style, and preset paste options) is available in Divi 5. Divi 4 supports copying and pasting module styles but does not offer the same level of granularity.
Always check the page on tablet and mobile views before publishing. Test on Phone, Tablet, and real devices to adjust spacing or column counts.
Modules have three main tabs: Content (text, images), Design (fonts, colors, spacing), and Advanced (custom CSS, conditions).
For simple linear arrangements, Flexbox is the better choice. Use CSS Grid for complex asymmetrical layouts.
The Custom target offset accepts standard CSS `nth-child` syntax, including examples like '3n+1' (every 3rd item starting at the first) and '-n+3' (the first three items only).
Keep data-* attribute names lowercase and hyphenated to comply with the HTML5 spec and ensure correct JavaScript dataset access.
Always choose the narrowest appropriate scope (Same Group, Same Column, etc.) to prevent unintended style propagation across unrelated sections of the page.

The foundational layer is Desktop (1441px+), which does not use a media query. Smaller breakpoints should use `min-width` queries, and larger optional breakpoints (Widescreen/Ultra Wide) should use `max-width` queries.
All custom breakpoint widths must be set in strictly ascending order, and Divi enforces this constraint to prevent overlaps.
All documentation regarding responsive editing and breakpoints is exclusive to Divi 5. Divi 4 uses a different responsive approach.

Global variables define site-wide design tokens (colors, fonts, numbers, etc.) and are the primary mechanism for ensuring consistency across all pages, templates, and Theme Builder layouts. Local/Design Variables can be used on individual pages.
Use descriptive names that reflect the variable's purpose (e.g., 'Section Padding Large') rather than its raw value ('40px').
Store global variables in site-wide locations like `wp_options` or custom post types, not per-page post meta.
Design variables must be stored in a dedicated site-wide location (e.g., `wp_options` or custom database table), separate from post content.
All preset types (general, option group) are stored in a shared site-wide location (`wp_options` or custom post type).
The Custom CSS field syncs with Appearance → Customize → Additional CSS in WordPress.
Code can be injected into the <head>, at the start of <body>, or before closing </body> tag (footer).
The Google Maps API key must have both the Maps JavaScript API and Geocoding API enabled in the Google Cloud Console.

English only

Use Global Variables for all design values (spacing, colors, fonts) in the Design Tab to ensure consistency and allow site-wide updates via a central 'Manage' panel.

The design system follows a three-tier hierarchy: 1. Variables (raw values like brand colors/type scale) define raw data. 2. Option Group Presets compose variables into reusable patterns (e.g., spacing, typography). 3. Element Presets compose option group presets into complete element designs.
Element Presets are scoped to a single element type (e.g., Button preset only applies to Button modules).
Every element (Section, Row, Column, Module) can act as a container for nested content.
Sections contain Rows, Rows contain Columns, and Columns contain Modules.
JSON or SVG

Interactions is a new system in Divi 5, replacing and extending the limited hover and animation options of Divi 4.

Divi 5 behavior only. Divi 4 uses a different layout engine.

Map static (one-off) colors and values to global color variables for consistency.
Limit fonts and weights to a curated set of approved options.

Prefer using defined presets (e.g., buttons, typography) over custom overrides to maintain design system integrity and enable bulk updates.

Use Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + C/V for quick attribute replication across elements.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using raw `<`, `>`, or `"` characters directly in innerContent values.
antiPatterns.reason: These characters must be encoded using their literal 6-character unicode escape strings (`\u003c`, `\u003e`, `\u0022`) to prevent rendering errors. Always use the double-escaped format when writing JavaScript code that will produce JSON.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on generic hooks for extension loading
antiPatterns.reason: Always use the dedicated `divi_extensions_init` action hook to ensure the module loads correctly after Divi is initialized.

antiPatterns.pattern: Manually setting module properties like `$props`, `$content`, or `$module_id()`.
antiPatterns.reason: These properties are managed automatically by the Builder framework and must not be set manually.

antiPatterns.pattern: Module does not appear in the module picker.
antiPatterns.reason: Ensure the PHP class extends `ET_Builder_Module`, that the `$slug` property is set and non-empty, and that the appropriate hook (`et_builder_ready` or `divi_extensions_init`) fires correctly. Check `debug.log` for loading errors.

antiPatterns.pattern: Module renders on front end but is blank in Visual Builder.
antiPatterns.reason: Verify that the JavaScript component is registered using `API.Modules.register()` and that the `slug` defined in JavaScript matches the PHP `$slug` exactly (case-sensitive). Ensure the JS file is enqueued with the `jquery` dependency.

antiPatterns.pattern: `show_if` conditional fields not working.
antiPatterns.reason: The field key and comparison value in the `show_if` array must exactly match a defined field key in `get_fields()` and one of its possible values, respectively.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming module IDs are persistent across sessions.
antiPatterns.reason: Module IDs (UUIDs) are ephemeral and change every time the Visual Builder loads a page, or when navigating away and back. Always re-query `getAllModuleIds()` after any reload to get current IDs.

antiPatterns.pattern: Accessing `window.divi.data` directly from the parent window context.
antiPatterns.reason: The data registry lives inside the Visual Builder's iframe (`#et-vb-app-frame`). You must first switch the execution context to this iframe before calling any methods.

antiPatterns.pattern: Attempting to write state using `window.divi.data.dispatch()`.
antiPatterns.reason: `dispatch` is not a documented or confirmed public API for writing state. Calling it may corrupt the builder's internal state and cause data loss. Use UI interaction or REST APIs (via `wp.apiRequest`) instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming write access to module state.
antiPatterns.reason: The Divi Data Registry is strictly read-only; there is no documented public API for writing or dispatching state changes. Use UI interaction or the REST API approach (modifying block JSON in `post_content`) instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Caching or persisting module UUIDs/IDs.
antiPatterns.reason: Module IDs are ephemeral and change on every page reload. Always re-query the store after navigation or reload to get current identifiers.

antiPatterns.pattern: Confusing `window.divi.data` with standard WordPress data stores (`wp.data`).
antiPatterns.reason: `window.divi.data` is a separate, proprietary system and does not initialize or interact with the standard WordPress `wp.data` store.

antiPatterns.pattern: Forgetting to return a value from filter callbacks.
antiPatterns.reason: The filtered content will become `null`, which breaks rendering. Always ensure your filter callback returns the modified output.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Visual Builder-only hooks on the front-end (or vice versa).
antiPatterns.reason: Hooks like `et_builder_api_ready` only fire inside the VB, and other hooks are specific to certain contexts. Check the URL or use context detection functions.

antiPatterns.pattern: Adding action/filter callbacks that don't run when expected.
antiPatterns.reason: The hook might fire before your code loads, or you may be testing in the wrong environment (e.g., front-end vs VB). Move `add_action()` to an earlier WordPress hook like `init` or `plugins_loaded`, and verify the hook name is case-sensitive.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming all Divi 4 hooks are active in Divi 5.
antiPatterns.reason: While most are retained for backward compatibility, some shortcode-era hooks (e.g., et_pb_shortcode_*) may no longer fire because Divi 5 uses a block format.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on iframe globals for production extensions
antiPatterns.reason: Iframe objects are internal implementation details and may change without notice. Use the documented public API (`API` from `et_builder_api_ready`) instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Omitting `$in_footer = true` or setting it to `false`
antiPatterns.reason: Scripts loaded in the `<head>` execute before the builder initializes, causing the critical `et_builder_api_ready` event to never fire. Always set the fifth parameter of `wp_enqueue_script()` to `true`.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming JavaScript slug matches PHP `$slug` (case-insensitive)
antiPatterns.reason: The JavaScript `slug` must match the PHP `$slug` exactly, including case sensitivity. If they mismatch, the module will appear blank in the Visual Builder.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using field names that do not match between PHP and JS
antiPatterns.reason: If a value is `undefined`, it means the field name used in the JavaScript `props` property does not exactly match the field name returned by PHP's `get_fields()`. Log `props` to debug.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on REST API for new module creation
antiPatterns.reason: REST creation produces content that renders on the frontend but may not appear in the Visual Builder (VB) layer view. Use browser automation (e.g., Playwright) instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Running multiple `wp.apiRequest` calls in parallel
antiPatterns.reason: This can cause requests to hang indefinitely. Chain all API requests sequentially using `.done()` callbacks.

antiPatterns.pattern: Inserting blocks after the `<!-- /wp:post-content -->` boundary
antiPatterns.reason: Blocks inserted after this boundary will not render correctly on the frontend or appear in view source. Always insert them before the boundary.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring shared hosting limitations for REST API authentication
antiPatterns.reason: Some shared hosts strip the `Authorization` header, causing 401 errors despite valid credentials. Use browser cookie authentication with `wpApiSettings.nonce` instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Running multiple `wp.apiRequest` calls in parallel (e.g., assigning to variables like var p1 = ...;)
antiPatterns.reason: This causes WordPress to throttle or hang requests indefinitely because it serializes authenticated REST API requests per session. Instead, chain all calls sequentially using `.done(function() { return wp.apiRequest(...) })`.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using standard regex or searching for `-->` to extract JSON from block comments.
antiPatterns.reason: `-->` can appear inside JSON string values. This method fails because it cannot reliably determine the true end boundary of the JSON object, especially when nested braces are present. Use a brace-depth character-by-character parser instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Modifying raw block content or rearranging sections.
antiPatterns.reason: Be aware of how Divi SSR processes blocks. When it encounters `<!-- wp:divi/section {...} -->`, it consumes the closing `-->`. If a stray `<!--` precedes this, the browser interprets everything that follows as an unclosed HTML comment node (`<!--...`), hiding sections.

antiPatterns.reason: Use the following JavaScript check to detect if section content has been trapped inside a comment node:

antiPatterns.pattern: Using REST API to create new sections/blocks.
antiPatterns.reason: New sections created programmatically via REST API will be invisible in the Visual Builder (VB). Use browser automation or Playwright/Claude in Chrome for creating new structure elements. Always confirm if the content needs to be editable in the VB before choosing an API method.

antiPatterns.pattern: Inserting content after `<!-- /wp:post-content -->` boundary.
antiPatterns.reason: Any blocks or content inserted after this boundary will not render on the live page. All structural changes must occur before this marker.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using standard HTML tags for Unicode escapes (e.g., `<`).
antiPatterns.reason: When handling innerContent or migrating styles, always use proper Unicode escape sequences (e.g., `<`) in JSON strings to prevent rendering issues.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using regex for block JSON extraction of closing tags (`-->`).
antiPatterns.reason: Regex is unreliable for complex nested structures like block content. Use a brace-depth parser instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating 'Card Everything' presets (combining shadow, border, padding, etc.)
antiPatterns.reason: Keep Option Group Presets focused on a single job (e.g., only Shadow or only Border). This ensures maximum reusability across different contexts.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using stacked presets for basic styling foundations
antiPatterns.reason: Let defaults and nested presets handle the foundational styles. Reserve stacking for context-specific tweaks (e.g., 'hero version' or 'dark section').

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming all variable types support units.
antiPatterns.reason: Only the 'Numbers' variable type supports explicit CSS unit validation. Other types (Strings, Images, etc.) are for different data formats and do not require unit consideration.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using the Image module for multiple images in a grid layout.
antiPatterns.reason: For grids, use the dedicated Gallery module. For custom layouts, arrange several Image modules in a multi-column row instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Building a custom navigation menu from scratch using Divi modules.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated Menu module (if available) or standard WordPress widget/theme builder methods for navigation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Pasted attributes have no effect.
antiPatterns.reason: The source and target modules may not share compatible settings for the selected paste type. Try using 'Paste Design Attributes' or 'Paste Style Attributes' for a more targeted transfer.

antiPatterns.pattern: Keyboard shortcuts fail to work.
antiPatterns.reason: Check for browser extension or OS-level shortcut conflicts with Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + C/V/R.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming feature parity between Divi 4 and Divi 5.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi 5 is a complete architectural redesign. Features like the Command Center, Composable Settings, Flexbox/CSS Grid systems, and the unified Attributes panel are new or significantly changed compared to previous versions. Always check the Divi 5 documentation for current status.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring performance warnings after migration.
antiPatterns.reason: Pages containing unsupported Divi 4 modules load the Divi 4 framework, causing temporary slowdowns. To restore optimal speed and benefit from Divi 5's optimized code (smaller CSS/JS bundles), gradually replace legacy modules with Divi 5 equivalents.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming all third-party modules are compatible.
antiPatterns.reason: Third-party module compatibility must be checked individually on the [Divi Marketplace](https://www.elegantthemes.com/marketplace/). If a module lacks Divi 5 support, contact the author or consider rolling back to Divi 4 if the plugin has opted out of Divi 5.

antiPatterns.pattern: Manually duplicating content layouts.
antiPatterns.reason: This is inefficient and fails when content needs updating. Use the Loop Builder instead, which connects to live database queries.

antiPatterns.pattern: Setting Posts Per Page to 'All' or leaving it blank for pagination.
antiPatterns.reason: Pagination requires a finite number of results to split. The loop query must have a specific limit set (e.g., 6, 9).

antiPatterns.pattern: Using complex Meta Queries or filtering without necessity.
antiPatterns.reason: Large meta queries can significantly slow down database performance. Use filters judiciously and check for missing database indexes.

antiPatterns.pattern: Nesting loops (looping inside a loop).
antiPatterns.reason: This creates exponential query complexity, leading to severe performance degradation. Avoid it if possible.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating individual templates for every content type/category.
antiPatterns.reason: This leads to template bloat and performance issues. Instead, use a single global template with targeted assignments or combine similar designs into one flexible template.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using static text instead of Dynamic Content modules in body templates.
antiPatterns.reason: Static content will only display on the page where it was created, failing to show the actual post title or content for other assigned items.

antiPatterns.pattern: Forgetting the Post Content module in custom post templates.
antiPatterns.reason: If the **Post Content module** is missing or improperly configured, the actual content of the blog post or page will not display on the template.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring responsive breakpoints during design.
antiPatterns.reason: Designing only for desktop leads to poor mobile experiences. Always test and adjust layouts (e.g., changing multi-column to single-column) at tablet (768px) and mobile (480px) breakpoints.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming off-canvas content is visible by default.
antiPatterns.reason: Off-canvas content is hidden until an Interaction (e.g., Click, Viewport/Scroll, Hover, Load) explicitly triggers its display. Always verify the interaction setup.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using default canvas auto-appending behavior for precise placement.
antiPatterns.reason: If you need off-canvas content to appear at a specific spot rather than being appended or overlayed, use the **Canvas Portal Module** to render the source canvas exactly where desired.

antiPatterns.pattern: Overwriting a preset configuration.
antiPatterns.reason: Option group state (enabled/disabled) is not persisted when overwriting an existing preset. Always create a new preset with a unique name to save the current option group configuration state.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming all elements support composable settings.
antiPatterns.reason: Option groups are only available on modules that contain multiple styled sub-components. If 'Toggle Options' is missing, try a different element type or verify the module supports this feature.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring PHP memory limits when using Theme Options.
antiPatterns.reason: If Theme Option settings revert to defaults after saving, increase the PHP memory limit (minimum 128MB in `wp-config.php`) and check for conflicting plugins or disabled WordPress Customizer API by the host.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using complex condition stacks without documentation.
antiPatterns.reason: Complex rules are difficult to debug when an element fails to appear. Always document the logic in the element's label or CSS ID field.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on conditions for SEO content visibility.
antiPatterns.reason: Content hidden by conditions is typically not rendered server-side and may not be indexed by search engines.
