antiPatterns.pattern: Over-customizing a premade layout.
antiPatterns.reason: Changing everything ignores the professional design intent. Instead, keep the overall structure, update text/images, and adjust colors to match your brand.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring responsive testing.
antiPatterns.reason: The page may look cramped or broken on mobile devices. Always test on different screen sizes (Phone/Tablet) and adjust spacing or column counts accordingly.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming vertical alignment works without container height.
antiPatterns.reason: For properties like `align-items` to function, the grid container must have an explicit `height` or `min-height`. Otherwise, items naturally expand to fill available space, overriding alignment controls.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Grid Density set to Dense when source order matters.
antiPatterns.reason: Dense mode attempts to fill gaps by allowing items to break out of their original document flow (source order). If the visual sequence must match the HTML structure, change the density setting to `Auto` instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Gap for outer container spacing.
antiPatterns.reason: The CSS `gap` property only creates space *between* items. If you need space around the entire group of elements, apply padding directly to the parent container instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Duplicating native attributes (e.g., adding a 'class' attribute manually).
antiPatterns.reason: Adding class attributes will not merge with Divi's built-in classes and may override them entirely. Use the dedicated CSS Class attribute field for additions.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming an attribute is applied to the outer wrapper when it fails to appear in HTML.
antiPatterns.reason: Some modules render multiple DOM nodes (e.g., inner and outer wrappers). Always verify that the correct Target element was selected using the Target dropdown.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming all settings support the Responsive Editor.
antiPatterns.reason: Not every setting supports per-device overrides (e.g., color, font family). If an icon is missing, the setting either applies globally or must be adjusted using the device view selector at the top of the builder.

antiPatterns.pattern: Modifying element attributes directly to change brand styles.
antiPatterns.reason: Always modify the controlling variable (e.g., global color variable) instead. This ensures the change propagates sitewide and is the most efficient method for brand-level updates.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming variables are stored in post content or element attributes.
antiPatterns.reason: Variables are designed to be site-wide constants, requiring storage in `wp_options` or a custom database table. Use dedicated REST endpoints/functions for access.

antiPatterns.pattern: Disabling Google Maps Script when using the Maps module.
antiPatterns.reason: The Maps module will become unavailable if the site-wide script is disabled. Only disable it if no part of the site uses the maps module to avoid conflicts with other plugins and reduce initial load size.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming default post counts are sufficient for all archive types.
antiPatterns.reason: Post counts must be explicitly set in the Layout tab for Category, Archive (date/author), Search, and Tag pages to override WordPress Reading settings correctly.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming global sections are visible in the Builder.
antiPatterns.reason: If Header/Footer aren't showing, ensure 'Show Theme Builder Layouts' is enabled via the Builder Settings icon (gear).

antiPatterns.pattern: Not creating a template before expecting edit options on archive pages.
antiPatterns.reason: The 'Edit with Divi' option will not appear on archive pages until at least one Theme Builder Header or Footer template has been created first.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring cache clearing when making design changes.
antiPatterns.reason: Changes may be cached by the browser, WordPress plugin, or server. Always clear all caches and hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) to view updates.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming Divi AI is accessible via a public API endpoint.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi AI does not expose a public REST API or programmatic interface. All features must be accessed through the Visual Builder UI, as the underlying calls are made server-side by the Divi plugin.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using vague prompts for image generation.
antiPatterns.reason: Descriptive English prompts (including style, subject, lighting, and composition) produce significantly better results. Always review AI output as a draft before publishing.

antiPatterns.pattern: Editing Theme Builder templates in isolation.
antiPatterns.reason: This forces users to switch between pages and the dedicated Theme Builder, leading to disruption and loss of design context. Use editable theme builder areas on a page instead (Divi 5).

antiPatterns.pattern: Overusing global elements for minor components.
antiPatterns.reason: While globals ensure consistency, over-reliance makes it difficult to customize pages when necessary. Reserve globals for truly universal components (e.g., site-wide headers/footers).

antiPatterns.pattern: Hardcoding data or styles into modules.
antiPatterns.reason: Instead of hard-coding values (e.g., page title, author name, spacing), use dynamic content tokens and Global Variables. This ensures the template automatically adapts to different content and allows for site-wide design changes.

antiPatterns.pattern: Deleting a Global Variable without checking dependencies.
antiPatterns.reason: Global Design Tab values reference variables by ID. Deleting such a variable will break all dynamic references across the entire site, causing broken styling.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Element Presets for shared styles across different module types.
antiPatterns.reason: Element Presets are limited by their scope and cannot be applied cross-element. Use Option Group Presets instead, as they target a single option group (like Typography or Background) and can be applied to any element with that matching group.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring the preset hierarchy when building designs.
antiPatterns.reason: Always start by defining global design variables. Then, build Option Group Presets for recurring patterns (spacing, borders). Finally, compose these into Element Presets to maintain a modular and scalable system.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on block layout mode for nested content.
antiPatterns.reason: If a parent module's layout type is not set to Flex or Grid, the nested children may fail to render correctly on the front end. Always verify that the container uses Flex or Grid.

antiPatterns.pattern: Programmatically modifying nested structures without validation.
antiPatterns.reason: Malformed `innerBlocks` arrays can cause the Visual Builder to fail parsing the layout, leading to structural integrity issues. Always validate parent-child relationships when updating JSON.

antiPatterns.pattern: Uploading Lottie files directly to WordPress media library without permission.
antiPatterns.reason: WordPress blocks JSON and SVG uploads by default for security reasons. Install a plugin (e.g., 'Safe SVG') or add an upload filter in `functions.php` to allow these file types.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on CSS HSL functions or `var()` references for derived color relationships.
antiPatterns.reason: Relative color offsets exist only in Divi's data layer, not in the browser. The final output is static hex/RGBA values. Developers must use standard CSS specificity rules to override colors; they cannot rely on a dynamic relationship (e.g., `color-mix()` or `var(--base)`) that doesn't exist in the rendered CSS.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using media queries for responsive scaling.
antiPatterns.reason: Instead of setting different values at each breakpoint, use `clamp()` (e.g., `clamp(min, preferred, max)`) to achieve smooth, fluid scaling across all screen sizes automatically.

antiPatterns.pattern: Expecting extended attributes to apply universally.
antiPatterns.reason: Extended attributes only affect elements that support the specific attribute type being extended. For example, extending button styles to a Text module will have no effect on button-related fields the Text module does not possess.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming replacement will affect fields that just contain the value (e.g., replacing `20px` in font size and border width).
antiPatterns.reason: If you do not enable 'Only Replace Identical Fields,' the replacement may apply to any field containing the matching text, regardless of its intended type or function. Always use this filter when precise targeting is needed.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Find and Replace for data that needs to be persistent or undone easily.
antiPatterns.reason: The operation modifies block attributes in `post_content` at build time and is irreversible. Always ensure you have a backup of the original content before executing a global replacement.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming Align Items handles text alignment.
antiPatterns.reason: Align Items aligns the entire element/module within its space. To align text or content *within* a module, use the module's dedicated text alignment settings.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring that Align Items only works in flex containers.
antiPatterns.reason: The setting must be applied to a parent container (Row or Column) that has flexbox layout enabled. Ensure the parent container is configured as a flex container.

antiPatterns.pattern: Manually updating content across multiple pages.
antiPatterns.reason: This is inefficient and prone to errors. Use Global Elements instead, as they automatically synchronize changes site-wide from a single source (the Divi Library).

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming Presets share content like Global Elements.
antiPatterns.reason: Presets only share design settings (style); each element instance retains its own unique content. Use Global Elements when both content and design must be identical across all pages.

antiPatterns.pattern: Manually recreating gradient stops when moving between elements.
antiPatterns.reason: The unified **gradient field type** allows copying, pasting, and finding/replacing gradients as a single attribute value, eliminating the need to manually adjust stop positions or colors.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring compatibility warnings during rollback.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi 5 designs are not backward compatible with Divi 4. Custom CSS/code specific to Divi 5 (e.g., flexbox) will fail, and third-party plugins designed for Divi 5 may break in Divi 4. Always test thoroughly.

antiPatterns.pattern: Attempting migration without updating prerequisites.
antiPatterns.reason: Ensure WordPress, Divi, and all plugins are fully updated before starting the migration process.

antiPatterns.pattern: Opening individual modules to find style origins.
antiPatterns.reason: The Style Inspector centralizes all applied styles, content values, and presets, allowing for rapid auditing across the entire page or element without opening multiple settings panels.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring attribute audits (e.g., alt text).
antiPatterns.reason: Use the Content tab to audit attributes like missing alt text, incorrect titles, or stray IDs across all elements simultaneously, which is faster than checking each module individually.

antiPatterns.pattern: Installation Failed — Theme Could Not Be Installed
antiPatterns.reason: The `.zip` file may be corrupted or incomplete. Delete the attempted install, re-download the theme from your Elegant Themes account, and verify that the file size matches the original download.

antiPatterns.pattern: License Activation Not Appearing
antiPatterns.reason: Check for plugin dependencies or theme conflicts. Ensure all other Elegant Themes plugins (like Bloom or Monarch) are updated, temporarily deactivate other plugins to isolate conflicts, and clear your browser cache/log out then log back in.

antiPatterns.pattern: Cannot Access Divi Menu in Dashboard
antiPatterns.reason: Confirm the theme is fully installed and active. Verify that **Divi 5** shows as 'Active' under **Appearance** → **Themes**. If necessary, re-upload the theme via FTP and ensure your WordPress user has administrator privileges.

antiPatterns.pattern: Updates Not Downloading
antiPatterns.reason: Verify that the license key is correctly entered in **Divi** → **Theme Options** → **Updates**. If necessary, generate a fresh API key from your Elegant Themes account and re-enter it. Ensure your Elegant Themes subscription remains active.

antiPatterns.pattern: Interaction fails to fire
antiPatterns.reason: The trigger element must be accessible and clickable on the front end. Elements with zero dimensions, hidden overflow, or covered by other elements may prevent expected events.

antiPatterns.pattern: Effect targets wrong element (using CSS selectors)
antiPatterns.reason: If you intend to affect only one element, ensure the selector is unique. A class selector will apply the effect to all matching elements.

antiPatterns.pattern: Cookie effects not persisting
antiPatterns.reason: These interactions depend on browser cookie settings. They will fail if the visitor has cookies disabled or uses a privacy-focused browser.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying solely on canvas dragging for reordering/moving.
antiPatterns.reason: Dragging elements within the Layers tree is more precise than dragging directly on the canvas, especially when moving elements between containers or reordering complex sections.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming a single editing control location.
antiPatterns.reason: The interface is complex. Contextual tools live in the persistent left sidebar; global settings open in the right panel; and device-specific controls are on the top bar. Always check all three areas for functionality.

antiPatterns.pattern: Attempting to nest rows deeper than one level.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi 5 enforces a single level of row nesting. If the insert modal does not offer a Row option, check if the column is already inside a nested row.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring responsive settings for columns within nested rows.
antiPatterns.reason: If columns do not display at expected widths, ensure **Layout Wrapping** is set to **Wrap** on the nested row and that Column Class values are properly assigned under Design Tab > Sizing.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using old focus-specific design options.
antiPatterns.reason: Older focus-specific design options have been deprecated in Divi 5. Existing values are automatically migrated to the new **focus state** editing mode, which must be used instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Exiting the builder to manage pages.
antiPatterns.reason: This requires navigating to the WordPress Pages screen and relaunching the builder, creating an inefficient 'exit-navigate-relaunch' cycle. Use the Page Manager instead to stay within the design environment.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming settings are not responsive by default.
antiPatterns.reason: In Divi 5, every design setting is inherently responsive. You do not need to manually enable responsive toggles per setting or use a separate 'enable responsive' switch.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using fixed pixel values for all spacing and sizing.
antiPatterns.reason: Fixed pixels often require excessive device-specific overrides. Use relative units (percentages, `em`, `vw`) to allow the layout to scale more naturally across different devices.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using CSS media queries for all responsive styling.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi 5's built-in settings (device view icons and tabs) handle most breakpoint-specific styling. Reserve CSS media queries only for advanced patterns that the settings panel cannot express, such as reordering elements or defining custom breakpoints.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring global module edits for client roles.
antiPatterns.reason: Editing a global module updates every instance across the site, which can cause unintended layout changes. Always disable 'Edit Global Modules' for non-admin roles.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming disabled modules are removed from content.
antiPatterns.reason: Disabling a module only prevents adding or editing it; it does not remove existing instances. An Administrator must manually edit and delete the module instance from the page to fully remove it.

antiPatterns.pattern: Nesting landmarks improperly (e.g., `nav` inside another `nav`).
antiPatterns.reason: Plan your semantic structure carefully before applying tags; improper nesting can confuse accessibility tools and crawlers.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using HTML wrappers without matching pairs in Before/After fields.
antiPatterns.reason: Unclosed or mismatched tags will cause layout breaks and invalid DOM markup. Always ensure opening tags have corresponding closing tags.

antiPatterns.pattern: Setting styles manually on every page/module.
antiPatterns.reason: This is time-consuming and leads to brand inconsistency. Instead, define global defaults in the Theme Customizer's design system settings (Primary Color, Typography, etc.) and rely on those tokens.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using thin fonts (<400 weight) for body text.
antiPatterns.reason: Thin fonts reduce readability. Always use a font weight of 400 or 500 minimum for body text.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming filters are limited to one tab.
antiPatterns.reason: Filters span all three tabs (Content, Design, Advanced) simultaneously. This is expected behavior.

antiPatterns.pattern: Not using the Modified filter before saving changes.
antiPatterns.reason: The `Modified` filter serves as an audit tool, allowing users to confirm they have only changed what was intended.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming conflicts are global issues.
antiPatterns.reason: Safe Mode only affects the current user's session, ensuring that other site visitors remain unaffected while troubleshooting.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming items will automatically fill gaps or maintain source order.
antiPatterns.reason: Use `Dense` for auto-placement to fill gaps, but be aware this may reorder the visual flow. Use `Auto` if maintaining strict document (source) order is critical, accepting potential gaps.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using column padding for spacing in a Flex container.
antiPatterns.reason: Padding breaks proper Flex alignment; use the `column-gap` and `row-gap` properties on the flex container instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on custom CSS targeting old Block classes after conversion to Flex.
antiPatterns.reason: Block class selectors may become invalid or require updates (e.g., target Flex equivalents) after converting a layout from Block to Flex.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring the parent container's display setting.
antiPatterns.reason: The Direction property only works if the parent Section/Row has **Display: Flex** enabled (not Grid or Block). Always verify this setting in the Design tab.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming Space Between creates a gap with one item.
antiPatterns.reason: Space Between only works with two or more items. With a single item, it behaves like Start. Use margin/spacing controls on the item itself to create spacing around a single element.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying solely on Justify Content when wrapping is enabled.
antiPatterns.reason: When Flex Wrap is active and items wrap, Justify Content only manages alignment *within* each line. Use **Align Content** instead to control spacing between the wrapped lines themselves.

antiPatterns.pattern: Confusing visual order with DOM source order (Row Reverse/Column Reverse).
antiPatterns.reason: Reversing direction only changes the *visual* display order, not the underlying HTML structure. Screen readers and accessibility tools will still read items in their original source order. For critical structural changes, modify the HTML or use JavaScript.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming wrapping happens when items are simply too wide.
antiPatterns.reason: Wrapping only occurs if the combined width of elements exceeds the parent container's width. Ensure child modules have minimum widths set to guarantee wrapping behavior.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Align Content without enabling Flex Wrap or ensuring multiple lines.
antiPatterns.reason: Align Content controls multi-line distribution and only works when items wrap to multiple lines. If there is only one line, use Justify Content instead. Also ensure the parent container has sufficient height for spacing to be visible.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on visual order for accessibility.
antiPatterns.reason: Screen readers always follow the HTML source order, regardless of the visual arrangement set by Flex Order. Critical information flow must maintain semantic source order.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using global variables for text/border colors without checking scope.
antiPatterns.reason: Ensure that the chosen color variable is correctly scoped to apply sitewide changes automatically. Always verify the variable's availability and intended use case.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring form typography consistency.
antiPatterns.reason: Failure to match the Input Text font, weight, and size with other form fields makes radio buttons appear disconnected from the rest of the form group.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using hardcoded colors for form elements.
antiPatterns.reason: Assigning global color variables to Border Color and Fields Icon Color ensures that sitewide palette changes automatically update the radio button appearance.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming global changes apply everywhere.
antiPatterns.reason: Global elements can be overridden. To customize a specific page, use the Theme Builder to create a custom template and explicitly add/override the header or footer for that scope.

antiPatterns.pattern: Not publishing changes after building templates.
antiPatterns.reason: Changes require multiple steps: Click **Save** in the editor, then click **Exit**, and finally click **Save Changes** (top right) to publish the template globally or locally. Failure to save changes means the site won't reflect the design.

antiPatterns.pattern: Overwriting existing variables without confirmation.
antiPatterns.reason: The generator will prompt the user to confirm before replacing existing variables if a variable prefix already exists in the Variable Manager. Always check for conflicts first.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming the preview unit matches the generated CSS unit.
antiPatterns.reason: The live results table always displays sizes in `px` for readability, even if the chosen output unit is `rem`. The actual generated CSS uses the selected unit (`rem` or `px`).

antiPatterns.pattern: Exiting the Visual Builder without manual saving.
antiPatterns.reason: Although Divi auto-saves periodically, relying solely on this feature risks losing the latest changes. Always perform a manual save before exiting to ensure all work is preserved.

antiPatterns.pattern: Migrating a portion of the site while leaving the rest in Divi 4.
antiPatterns.reason: Migration is site-wide. The system handles compatibility page by page: fully compatible pages get full performance, and unsupported pages load the slower Divi 4 framework.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring pre-migration testing or backup.
antiPatterns.reason: Always back up the site and test migration in a staging environment before upgrading live. Use Divi 4 until critical third-party modules are confirmed compatible with Divi 5.

antiPatterns.pattern: Targeting builder-only classes in front-end CSS.
antiPatterns.reason: Classes starting with `.et-fb-*` only exist when the Visual Builder is active. Use `body:not(.et-fb-root-ancestor)` to scope styles that should *not* apply in the builder context, or use standard selectors for production code.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on positional classes (e.g., `.et_pb_text_2`)
antiPatterns.reason: These classes change when modules are reordered, added, or removed. Instead, use the module's CSS ID or assign a stable custom class in the Advanced tab.

antiPatterns.pattern: Custom CSS not taking effect
antiPatterns.reason: Divi's built-in styles may have higher specificity. Use a more specific selector, or add `!important` as a last resort. Alternatively, ensure your stylesheet is enqueued with Divi's stylesheet as a dependency.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring specificity conflicts when overriding Divi styles.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi's built-in CSS often has high specificity. To ensure overrides apply, prefix selectors with `body` or the page ID, or use `!important` sparingly.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming custom CSS will work on all devices without media queries.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi applies responsive styles using `@media` queries that can override desktop-only CSS at smaller breakpoints. Always wrap mobile/tablet specific overrides in the correct `@media` query (e.g., `max-width: 980px` for tablet).

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on raw CSS overrides for global changes.
antiPatterns.reason: Global changes should be handled by updating the relevant variable or preset at the highest level, not by finding and replacing custom CSS across multiple pages.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating variables for every shade of a color (e.g., Blue-light, Blue-dark).
antiPatterns.reason: Use relative colors (HSL) instead; only create variables for core brand values.

antiPatterns.pattern: Overriding variable values using CSS custom properties or standard CSS specificity (e.g., `!important`).
antiPatterns.reason: Variables resolve to static CSS values at render time, making them un-targetable by `var()` or standard CSS selectors. This creates a disconnect between the Variable Manager and the rendered output. Instead, change the variable itself via the Variable Manager or use element-level overrides in the builder.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming mathematical color harmony matches brand identity.
antiPatterns.reason: Mathematical color relationships (like complementary pairs) are useful starting points, but always verify that the derived colors meet specific brand guidelines and aesthetic requirements.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying solely on HSL lightness for contrast verification.
antiPatterns.reason: HSL lightness is not perceptually uniform. A given percentage change (e.g., 15% L) can produce different perceived contrasts depending on the hue (e.g., blue appears darker than yellow). Always verify contrast ratios using a dedicated tool like WebAIM Contrast Checker.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using relative colors for fixed-meaning status indicators or independent brand choices.
antiPatterns.reason: If the color's meaning (e.g., error, success) is fixed, or if two brand colors are chosen independently with no mathematical relationship, they should be managed using separate variables to prevent unintended divergence.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using `tinymce.setContent()` to programmatically update text content in the Visual Builder.
antiPatterns.reason: `tinymce.setContent()` only updates the visual display (DOM) but does not write to Divi's underlying React save state. Content set this way will be lost or revert when the user clicks Save. Instead, simulate manual keyboard input (e.g., click into editor -> Cmd+A/Ctrl+A -> type content).

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming Redux or wp.data access in the iframe.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi 5 does not expose a Redux store or `wp.data` stores for state management; it is handled internally.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new modules via REST API
antiPatterns.reason: REST creation may produce content that renders on the front end but might not appear in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation (e.g., Playwright) for reliable module creation instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Circle Counter when horizontal progress is needed
antiPatterns.reason: For horizontal progress bars, use the Bar Counter module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Circle Counter when a simple animated number is required
antiPatterns.reason: For an animated number without a circular visual, use the Number Counter module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Before/After for single or multiple images
antiPatterns.reason: Do not use this module to display a single image; use the Image module instead. For browsing multiple images, use the Gallery module. For content slideshows, use the Slider module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using the Blog module for project-type posts.
antiPatterns.reason: Use dedicated modules like Portfolio or Filterable Portfolio instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using the Blog module for image-only grids from the media library.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the Gallery module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Needing posts in a full-screen sliding format.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the Post Slider module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Post Carousel for a fullscreen post slideshow or traditional blog feed.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the **Post Slider** module for full-screen slideshows with text overlays. Use the **Blog** module for traditional blog feeds and excerpts.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on default Post Carousel behavior without checking constraints.
antiPatterns.reason: If posts are not displaying, verify that published content exists in selected categories, the Offset value is appropriate, and no custom code interferes with the query. Ensure Post Count > 0.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using custom CSS classes instead of Presets
antiPatterns.reason: Presets are preferred because they are managed visually, require no CSS knowledge, propagate changes instantly to all instances, and avoid the need for `!important` overrides. Use custom CSS only for edge cases (e.g., special interactions or third-party integrations).

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on `:hover` pseudo-class for mobile feedback
antiPatterns.reason: Hover states rely on the CSS `:hover` pseudo-class, which does not exist on touch devices. On mobile, use a separate mobile preset or implement button feedback using the `:active` pseudo-class (for tapping) or JavaScript.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using CTA when only a button is needed.
antiPatterns.reason: If you need only a standalone button without heading or description, use the dedicated [Button] module instead of the Call to Action (CTA) module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on REST API for new CTA creation.
antiPatterns.reason: While modifying existing modules via `wp.apiFetch` PATCH is possible, creating entirely new modules via REST API may result in content that renders but does not appear in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation (e.g., Playwright) for reliable module creation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Not filling both button text and link URL.
antiPatterns.reason: The CTA button will not render if either the Button Text or the Link URL is empty. Always ensure both fields are populated to display a functional button.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new modules via REST API (e.g., using `wp.apiFetch` POST)
antiPatterns.reason: The resulting content may render on the front end but might not appear in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation (Playwright) for reliable module creation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using the Contact Form module for CF7-dependent flows.
antiPatterns.reason: The native module cannot replicate complex behavior (like mail tags, specific add-ons) or maintain existing form definitions built in Contact Form 7. Use the dedicated CF7 module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming Divi controls all form submission logic.
antiPatterns.reason: For forms using Contact Form 7, submission behavior (validation, email delivery, messages) is entirely handled by CF7 and the WordPress environment, not Divi. Check CF7's Mail tab and SMTP configuration.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring pseudo-class styling for form fields.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi’s harmonized design system requires using `:focus` and `:checked` editing modes alongside hover states to ensure consistent, modern styling across all field types (Input, Checkbox, Radio).

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming form fields are limited to basic types.
antiPatterns.reason: The module supports unlimited field types including text inputs, email fields, textareas, checkboxes, radio buttons, and dropdown selects. Furthermore, advanced features like conditional visibility logic allow for complex, multi-step forms.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying solely on default server mail configuration (`wp_mail()`/`sendmail`).
antiPatterns.reason: Default PHP mailing functions often fail due to poor server setup or spam filtering. Always install an SMTP plugin (e.g., WP Mail SMTP, FluentSMTP) to route emails through a dedicated, reliable mail service.

antiPatterns.pattern: Timer shows all zeros
antiPatterns.reason: The target date has passed. Update the module settings with a future date and verify WordPress General Settings timezone to ensure correct calculation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Numbers not updating in real time
antiPatterns.reason: JavaScript may be blocked, or caching might serve a static page version. Check the browser console for JS errors and exclude the page from full-page caching if necessary.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Dropdown for Primary Navigation
antiPatterns.reason: The Dropdown module is designed for interactive content panels, not the site's main navigation. Use the dedicated Menu module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Dropdown for Always-Visible Content
antiPatterns.reason: Dropdown modules are for hover/click reveals. For sections that must always be visible and collapsible, use Accordion or Toggle modules.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Email Optin for general contact forms or data collection.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated Contact Form module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Email Optin for user authentication.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the Login module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Email Optin to display comments or discussions.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the Comments module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using standard posts or pages for projects.
antiPatterns.reason: The module only pulls content from the dedicated **Projects** custom post type. Standard posts and pages will not appear in the portfolio display.

antiPatterns.pattern: Not assigning featured images or categories to projects.
antiPatterns.reason: If projects lack a featured image or are not assigned to at least one project category, they may fail to display correctly.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on the Portfolio module for client-side filtering.
antiPatterns.reason: The standard Portfolio module does not support dynamic, client-side category filter buttons; use the Filterable Portfolio module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring parent container constraints when setting grid columns.
antiPatterns.reason: The Portfolio module's column count must work within the established constraints of its parent row (Flexbox or CSS Grid). If columns do not align, check the parent container settings and spacing values.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Fullwidth Menu for widget sidebar navigation
antiPatterns.reason: Use the [Sidebar] module instead. The Fullwidth Menu is designed for full-width sections, not widget areas.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Fullwidth Menu for single row links without dropdowns
antiPatterns.reason: Consider using the [Social Media Follow] or manual link methods instead of this module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Fullwidth Portfolio for non-project image collections.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated [Gallery](gallery.md) module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Placing Fullwidth Portfolio inside a standard content column section.
antiPatterns.reason: The module requires a fullwidth container; it will not be visible or function correctly otherwise.

antiPatterns.pattern: Expecting the carousel to scroll without enough items.
antiPatterns.reason: Carousel navigation arrows only appear if the number of projects exceeds what can fit in the visible area. Ensure Posts Number is high enough for scrolling.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Fullwidth Slider for a single static hero section.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated [Fullwidth Header](fullwidth-header.md) module instead, as the slider is designed for rotating content.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Fullwidth Slider for standard content-width sliders.
antiPatterns.reason: If you need a standard section slider, use the dedicated [Slider](slider.md) module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming automatic slide advancement.
antiPatterns.reason: If slides are static, ensure the auto-advance setting is enabled and a timing interval is configured. Also, confirm the slider contains more than one slide, as single-slide sliders will not animate.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Gallery for filtered projects
antiPatterns.reason: If you need to display project posts with client-side category filtering, do not use the Gallery module; instead, use Filterable Portfolio.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Image/Gallery for full-screen text sliders
antiPatterns.reason: For a full-screen content slider that includes text overlays, use the dedicated Slider module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring JavaScript errors during troubleshooting.
antiPatterns.reason: Check the browser console (F12) for JS conflicts, especially when dealing with unresponsive sliders or lightboxes. Temporarily deactivating other plugins can isolate the issue.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on default padding for slider height.
antiPatterns.reason: Varying content lengths and default vertical padding will cause the slider to jump or be inconsistent in height. Set a fixed **Min Height** value in the Design tab's Sizing group and remove vertical padding instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using generic filters like `et_module_shortcode_output` without checking `$render_slug`.
antiPatterns.reason: The filter must check if the current module slug matches the target module (`if ('et_pb_module' !== $render_slug) { return $output; }`) to prevent unintended modifications across all modules.

antiPatterns.pattern: Child Modules Not Aligning Properly
antiPatterns.reason: If child modules stack when side-by-side is desired, verify the Group's Layout is set to **Flex** (Block stacks vertically). Also check if child widths exceed available space or if the parent column constrains the container.

antiPatterns.pattern: Group Background Not Visible
antiPatterns.reason: Ensure the background is applied directly in the Group's Content tab, not just on the parent row/section. The Group must also have sufficient height (via content or min-height), and child modules should not have opaque backgrounds covering it.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using the Heading module when combined with body text.
antiPatterns.reason: The Heading module is for stand-alone titles. Use the Text module instead if you need a heading followed by paragraphs or rich content.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using static headings in templates that require dynamic data.
antiPatterns.reason: If the title needs to automatically display the current post's name, use the Post Title module or enable dynamic content within the Heading module. Static entries will fail to update.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring semantic HTML tags when using headings.
antiPatterns.reason: Always verify that the selected HTML tag (H1-H6) matches your intended document outline, even if the visual size settings are different. This is crucial for accessibility and SEO.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new modules via REST API (e.g., `wp.apiFetch` POST)
antiPatterns.reason: REST creation may produce content that renders on the front end but fails to appear or be correctly represented in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation for reliable module creation instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Icon module when text is required
antiPatterns.reason: The Icon module is designed for standalone icons. If you need an icon paired with descriptive text, use the Blurb module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new modules via REST API
antiPatterns.reason: While it produces content that renders on the front end, it may not appear in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation (Playwright) instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Link module for prominent CTAs or full site menus
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated Button module for primary calls-to-action, and use the Menu module for full site navigation structures. The Link module is best suited for structured link lists or card components.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Login for other purposes
antiPatterns.reason: Do not use this module for collecting visitor inquiries or email signups; use dedicated modules like Contact Form or Email Optin instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Search for Navigation
antiPatterns.reason: Do not use the Search module for navigation menus. Use the dedicated Menu module (`divi/menu`) or Fullwidth Menu module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Building Site Header with Standard Module
antiPatterns.reason: Do not build a full-width, site-wide header using the standard Menu module. Use the dedicated Fullwidth Menu module or Theme Builder for global templates.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Post Navigation for archive listings or loop-driven content
antiPatterns.reason: Post Navigation is designed only for single post/project transitions. For paginating collections (archives, loops), use the dedicated Pagination module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on Main Query pagination on static homepages
antiPatterns.reason: Main Query pagination only generates links on single post or page views. It will not generate links on static homepage layouts or non-singular contexts.

antiPatterns.pattern: Placing on static pages or archive templates
antiPatterns.reason: The module requires adjacent post data and will render empty if placed on static pages or general archive templates. Use it only in single post/project templates.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring category restriction
antiPatterns.reason: If links point to unrelated topics, enable the 'In Same Category' toggle to restrict navigation contextually.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on default theme title output
antiPatterns.reason: The Post Title module must be used within Theme Builder templates to gain precise, customizable control over every element (title, author, date, featured image) and its styling.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring the master 'Show Meta' toggle
antiPatterns.reason: Individual meta toggles (Author, Date, Comments Count) will not display if the main `Show Meta` toggle is disabled in the Content tab. Always enable `Show Meta` first.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Pricing Table for single CTAs or standalone buttons.
antiPatterns.reason: The module is designed for comparison layouts. For a simple call-to-action block, use the dedicated Call To Action module. For a standalone action button, use the Button module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new modules via REST API (e.g., `wp.apiFetch` POST)
antiPatterns.reason: While the content may render on the front end, it might not appear correctly in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation (Playwright) for reliable module creation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using the Shop module on a single product page template.
antiPatterns.reason: This is incorrect. For displaying products on an individual product page, use the specialized Woo Product modules instead of the general Shop module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming the module works for non-WooCommerce content grids.
antiPatterns.reason: The Shop module is strictly for WooCommerce data. Use dedicated modules like Blog or Portfolio for non-e-commerce content grids.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Product Upsell for related products based on category or tag similarity.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated [Woo Related Products] module instead. This upsell module is specifically for recommending higher-value alternatives linked to the product.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Product Upsell for cross-sell suggestions on the cart page.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated [Woo Cross Sells] module for cart-page recommendations. This upsell module is designed for single product pages.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Cart Products on non-cart pages.
antiPatterns.reason: This module requires the active WooCommerce cart context. Use the Shop module for product grids or catalog views, and the Woo Checkout Details module for order summaries.

antiPatterns.pattern: Sidebar showing no content on the front end.
antiPatterns.reason: Verify that widgets are assigned to the selected widget area (Appearance > Widgets), confirm the widget area name matches a registered sidebar, and ensure individual widgets are not set to display conditionally.

antiPatterns.pattern: Widget content looking out of place in Divi layout.
antiPatterns.reason: Use Title Text/Body Text settings or add custom CSS (Advanced tab) to override default widget styles and match the global design.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Social Media Follow for team member profiles
antiPatterns.reason: This module is designed for general brand/author linking. For displaying individual team member profiles with social links, use the dedicated **Person** module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Social Media Follow for single decorative icons
antiPatterns.reason: If you only need to display a single icon that is purely decorative or functional (without linking), use the dedicated **Icon** module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using inline `<script>` for Fix 1 without checking jQuery availability.
antiPatterns.reason: If Divi defers or loads jQuery asynchronously (e.g., via 'Defer jQuery' in Theme Options > Performance), an inline script calling `jQuery` or `$` will throw a `ReferenceError: jQuery is not defined`, potentially breaking other scripts like sliders or carousels. Use the polling snippet (Option A) or, preferably, hook into `wp_footer` (Option B).

antiPatterns.pattern: Editing child 'Social Network' items to change link target.
antiPatterns.reason: The child panel only shows **Profile URL** and lacks a target field. To set the link target for all icons in an instance, navigate up using the breadcrumb until you reach the parent **Social Media Follow** module settings (Content > Icon) and set the **Link Target** there.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using generic filters for all modules.
antiPatterns.reason: Always check if a specific filter (e.g., `et_module_shortcode_output`) is necessary, or if dedicated hooks/filters exist for the module type (e.g., `woocommerce_cart_item_name`, `woocommerce_billing_fields`).

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Testimonial module for team member profiles with social links.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated Person module instead. The Testimonial module is strictly for customer quotes/reviews.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Testimonial module for a rotating quote slideshow.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the Slider module instead. This module is designed for static, structured endorsements.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Testimonial module for general icon-and-text feature cards.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the Blurb module instead. The Testimonial module requires specific attribution fields (Author/Company).

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming all modules have identical advanced options and CSS targets.
antiPatterns.reason: While many core options are shared, specific modules (like Testimonial or Toggle) define unique CSS targets within the Advanced tab's CSS option group. Always verify the available elements to target per module type.

antiPatterns.pattern: Setting section height using 'height'
antiPatterns.reason: For predictable behavior, use `min-height` instead of `height`, as parent layout styles (Flex/Grid) or padding/margin may override explicit height rules.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming background image visibility
antiPatterns.reason: Ensure the image URL is correct and publicly accessible. Also, verify that opacity/overlay settings are not hiding the image, and check the background size setting (cover, contain, or custom).

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring divider requirements
antiPatterns.reason: Dividers require both top or bottom margin/padding AND a defined height to display. Also, ensure the color contrasts with the background and that the SVG/shape asset is loaded (check for CORS issues).

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming columns are equal width when using custom CSS.
antiPatterns.reason: Always verify that the row's column structure setting (e.g., '2 Equal') matches the desired layout, as custom CSS can override structural widths and cause conflicts.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring device-specific settings for spacing or visibility.
antiPatterns.reason: Responsive layouts require checking padding/margin adjustments and column visibility toggles (mobile, tablet, desktop) individually to prevent layout breakage on smaller screens.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Toggle for mutually exclusive content groups.
antiPatterns.reason: If the goal is to group items where only one can be viewed at a time, use the Accordion module instead of multiple independent Toggles.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Toggle for horizontal switchable panels.
antiPatterns.reason: For organizing content into tabs or horizontal switchable panels, use the Tabs module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring JavaScript conflicts when toggles fail to open/close.
antiPatterns.reason: If interaction fails, check browser console for JS errors, verify no other plugins conflict (especially caching plugins), and ensure the toggle is not wrapped inside a link element.

antiPatterns.pattern: Allowing content overflow when expanded.
antiPatterns.reason: Check Advanced settings and set Overflow to `visible`. Also, remove fixed height values from Sizing settings and ensure embedded media has responsive widths (`max-width: 100%`).

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Video for multiple videos
antiPatterns.reason: The Video module is designed for a single embed. For navigable carousels, always use the Video Slider module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Video Slider for single video
antiPatterns.reason: If you only need to display one video, it is simpler and more appropriate to use the dedicated Video module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring performance limits with many videos
antiPatterns.reason: Video sliders with 10+ items can impact page load. Limit the slider to 6-8 videos and use optimized thumbnails.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using the Video module for multiple navigable videos.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the [Video Slider](video-slider.md) module instead when presenting multiple videos in a carousel format.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Add to Cart for general product grids.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated [Shop] module instead, as it handles built-in add-to-cart functionality for grid views.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Add to Cart only for price display.
antiPatterns.reason: If you only need to show the price without a purchase button, use the [Woo Product Price] module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Add to Cart only for stock status.
antiPatterns.reason: If you only need to show stock availability without the purchase button, use the [Woo Product Stock] module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Breadcrumbs on non-WooCommerce pages or for general site navigation.
antiPatterns.reason: The module requires WooCommerce context and is designed specifically for product/category hierarchy. For general site breadcrumbs, use a dedicated breadcrumb plugin instead. For page-level navigation, use [Post Navigation].

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring JavaScript errors when totals fail to update.
antiPatterns.reason: If cart totals do not recalculate after changing quantities, check the browser console for JavaScript errors. This is often due to plugin conflicts interfering with WooCommerce's AJAX updates; temporarily disabling other plugins can help identify the conflict.

antiPatterns.pattern: Missing shipping costs in the totals table.
antiPatterns.reason: Verify that shipping zones and methods are correctly configured (WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping). The module only displays shipping costs if at least one method is available for the customer's location, and the 'Enable the shipping calculator on the cart page' option must be enabled under WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Shipping Options.

antiPatterns.pattern: Placing payment options in a non-sticky or non-visible area.
antiPatterns.reason: For long checkout forms, use Position settings to make the payment module sticky in a sidebar column. This keeps the payment options and Place Order button accessible as customers scroll.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using the Billing Module on non-checkout pages.
antiPatterns.reason: This module requires the WooCommerce checkout context to function. Use a general Contact Form module instead for unrelated pages.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using this module for shipping address collection.
antiPatterns.reason: It is designed only for billing details. Use the dedicated Woo Checkout Shipping module for that purpose.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Checkout Details on non-checkout pages or for cart listings.
antiPatterns.reason: The module requires the WooCommerce checkout context and pulls data from the active cart session. For product catalog displays, use the Shop module; for general cart review/editing, use the Woo Cart Products module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming order totals are static between cart and checkout pages.
antiPatterns.reason: WooCommerce recalculates totals on the checkout page based on entered billing/shipping addresses. Always verify that shipping costs, taxes, or coupons may apply differently at checkout compared to the cart page.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on REST API for new module creation
antiPatterns.reason: Creating new modules via REST API may produce front-end content that does not appear in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation (Playwright) for reliable module creation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Notice on non-WooCommerce pages
antiPatterns.reason: Notices require WooCommerce page data to render; they will appear empty until a notice-triggering event occurs.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using this module on non-WooCommerce pages.
antiPatterns.reason: The module requires a product context to function. Use general rich text modules instead if not on a WooCommerce page.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Product Description for tabbed content (description, reviews, attributes).
antiPatterns.reason: This is the wrong module for structured, multi-section product data. Use the dedicated [Woo Product Tabs] module instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new modules via REST API using `wp.apiFetch` PATCH.
antiPatterns.reason: While modifying existing content attributes works, creating entirely new modules via REST API may result in front-end rendering without appearing correctly in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation (e.g., Playwright) for reliable module creation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Product Gallery for non-WooCommerce galleries or single images.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the general [Gallery] module for multi-product/non-WooCommerce collections, and use the dedicated [Image] module for a single standalone image.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Product Reviews for average star rating display only.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated Woo Product Rating module instead, as the Review List module is designed to show full reviews and the submission form.

antiPatterns.pattern: Placing either module on a non-WooCommerce page or without product context.
antiPatterns.reason: Both modules require an active WooCommerce environment and must be placed within a valid product template to function correctly.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring CSS conflicts when stars appear as plain text characters.
antiPatterns.reason: The star icons rely on WooCommerce's font icon system. Ensure the main WooCommerce stylesheet is loaded to prevent styling issues.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming reviews will display without proper setup.
antiPatterns.reason: WooCommerce must be installed, activated, and reviews must be explicitly enabled under `WooCommerce > Settings > Products`. Additionally, at least one product must have received a review for the module to function.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Product Tabs for standalone content display.
antiPatterns.reason: Do not use this module for single descriptions or reviews. Use dedicated modules: `Woo Product Description` for long descriptions, and `Woo Product Reviews` for customer feedback.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming all products show stock status.
antiPatterns.reason: WooCommerce allows enabling stock management per-product. If a product is set to 'Do not manage stock', the module will not provide stock data for it.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring caching when troubleshooting display issues.
antiPatterns.reason: Both WooCommerce and related modules can serve stale content due to page caching plugins. Always clear all caches (including WooCommerce settings) when troubleshooting unexpected or missing product data.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new modules via REST API (PATCH)
antiPatterns.reason: While modifying existing module content works, creating entirely new modules this way may result in front-end rendering but fail to appear in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation (Playwright) for reliable module creation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Product Title on non-WooCommerce pages or for static text
antiPatterns.reason: This module requires a product context and dynamically pulls the title from WooCommerce. For post/page titles, use [Post Title](post-title.md); for static headings, use a Text or Heading module.

antiPatterns.pattern: Missing tab content (empty panels)
antiPatterns.reason: Verify that the product has corresponding data filled in. The Description tab needs the long description; Additional Information requires configured attributes; Reviews need approved reviews.

antiPatterns.pattern: Custom tabs not appearing
antiPatterns.reason: Check two things: 1) The `woocommerce_product_tabs` filter priority must allow your tab to register before the module renders. 2) Ensure the Included Tabs setting in the module is not restricting display.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new modules via REST API (PATCH)
antiPatterns.reason: While modifying existing module content works, creating entirely new modules this way may result in front-end rendering without appearing correctly in the Visual Builder layer view. Use browser automation for reliable creation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using multiple h1 tags on a page
antiPatterns.reason: This violates proper SEO heading hierarchy. Only one module should be set to `h1` (the primary product title) while others should use `h2` or lower.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Related Products on non-product pages.
antiPatterns.reason: Related products require a product context (shared categories/tags) to determine relationships. Use dedicated modules like Shop or manually curated grids instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using Woo Related Products for cross-sell suggestions on the cart page.
antiPatterns.reason: The module is designed for product pages, not checkout flows. Use the specialized Woo Cross Sells module for cart-related suggestions.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new modules via REST API
antiPatterns.reason: While content renders on the front end, it may not appear in the Visual Builder (VB) layer view. Use browser automation (Playwright) for reliable module creation.

antiPatterns.pattern: Applying shadows without considering background color.
antiPatterns.reason: Overly dark or large shadows can feel heavy. Use subtle shadow values with colors that complement the element's background to create a natural sense of depth.

antiPatterns.pattern: Applying filters without considering blend mode.
antiPatterns.reason: If you are layering elements, always check the Blend Mode setting. Failing to adjust it can result in unexpected visual interactions between the filtered element and background content.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming front-end impact from Meta settings.
antiPatterns.reason: The Meta options group only affects the Visual Builder's editing environment and has no effect on the site's front-end output. Use it solely for organizational purposes (Element Label, Force Visible).

antiPatterns.pattern: Using legacy 'Fields' settings for focus styling.
antiPatterns.reason: Settings like 'Fields Focus Background Color', 'Fields Focus Text Color', and 'Use Focus Borders' are superseded by the harmonized **:focus** mode in the current UI. Use the dedicated pseudo-class controls instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on deprecated focus styling shortcuts.
antiPatterns.reason: Older 'focus-only' color pickers and similar shortcuts have been migrated into the standard **:focus** editing mode to keep all state treatments consistent.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming general text controls apply everywhere.
antiPatterns.reason: Typography options are module-specific. For instance, menu items use `Menu Text Options`, pagination uses `Pagination Text Options`, and body content uses `Text Options`. Always check the specific group for the element you are styling.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using visibility toggles for minor adjustments (e.g., font size or spacing).
antiPatterns.reason: Reserve visibility toggles only for structural changes; use responsive styling options instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating too many device-specific layout versions.
antiPatterns.reason: Limit layout versions to one desktop and one mobile version to maintain manageable maintenance.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring Global Design System Setup
antiPatterns.reason: Divi defaults (14px body text, 30px headings) will make every module look wrong. Always run the Design System Setup playbook first.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using HTML/CSS patterns when native Divi modules suffice.
antiPatterns.reason: Always prefer using Divi's built-in modules and visual controls. These are easier for the user to maintain in the Visual Builder, and workarounds should only be used when native settings fail or programmatic content is involved.

antiPatterns.pattern: Creating new editable content via REST API or backend methods (using `wp:divi/placeholder`).
antiPatterns.reason: The content will render on the frontend but be completely invisible and uneditable in the Visual Builder's Layers panel because API-injected blocks do not register in Divi's internal React state. Use browser automation instead.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using `tinymce.setContent()` to update text content.
antiPatterns.reason: This method does not persist changes. To ensure persistence, the user must type the content via keyboard events to trigger Divi's React event chain.

antiPatterns.pattern: Running multiple REST API calls in parallel (e.g., using Promise.all).
antiPatterns.reason: Parallel calls will hang indefinitely within the Divi editor context. Requests must be chained sequentially using `.done()` callbacks.

antiPatterns.pattern: Hardcoding a module UUID or relying on it after page reload.
antiPatterns.reason: Module IDs (UUIDs) change every time the page reloads in the Visual Builder. Instead, locate blocks by searching for a unique string within its content and then walking backward to find the containing block comment start (`raw.lastIndexOf('<!-- wp:divi/text', idx)`).

antiPatterns.pattern: Using `wp.apiFetch` in the Divi editor context.
antiPatterns.reason: `wp.apiFetch` is not available and throws a TypeError. Always use `wp.apiRequest` instead, as it is always available when logged into wp-admin.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using generic CSS selectors for Divi customizations.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi's deep selector structure (e.g., `.et_pb_section .et_pb_row .et_pb_module .et_pb_text_inner p`) requires highly specific selectors or the use of `!important` to ensure styles are applied correctly.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using this recipe to filter blog posts or custom-post-type entries.
antiPatterns.reason: Use the dedicated [Filterable Portfolio] module instead, as this plugin only filters images within the Media Library.

antiPatterns.pattern: Placing two Divi galleries on one page and expecting independent filtering.
antiPatterns.reason: The plugin filters all gallery items in the DOM; therefore, multiple galleries will be filtered together. Use separate pages or a different approach if isolation is required.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on pagination for image visibility when filtering.
antiPatterns.reason: Filtering only operates on items currently loaded in the DOM. If the gallery uses Divi's pagination (`Images Per Page` set), paginated images will not appear when their category is selected.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on default pagination when filtering is active
antiPatterns.reason: The frontend JavaScript only filters items currently loaded in the DOM. If 'Images Per Page' is set lower than the total count, items on subsequent pages are missed by the filter mechanism.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring theme CSS conflicts for list styling
antiPatterns.reason: Some themes apply high-specificity `list-style: disc` and `padding-left` to all `<ul>` elements, overriding the plugin's default styles. If custom CSS is cleared or the seed fails, use this block:

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming category counts update automatically after taxonomy changes
antiPatterns.reason: Cached term counts can become stale if the taxonomy was registered without the `_update_generic_term_count` callback before a plugin upgrade. Re-deactivating and reactivating the plugin forces re-registration and a fresh count.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming filters work when they fail silently
antiPatterns.reason: If clicking a filter button does nothing, the cause is likely a JavaScript error elsewhere on the page that halts script execution. Check the browser console (F12 → Console) for red errors at page load.

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on post-render DOM mutations after the plugin runs.
antiPatterns.reason: The plugin operates at server render time. If another plugin wraps or replaces the gallery DOM after the `render_block` callback executes, the data attributes will be lost and filtering will fail.

antiPatterns.pattern: Importing layouts before variables/presets.
antiPatterns.reason: If you import layouts before setting up global variables and presets, the imported styles may be incomplete or incorrect. Always establish the design system foundation first.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming font availability after importing variable names.
antiPatterns.reason: Divi variables only store font family *names*. The actual font files must also be loaded and available on the site (e.g., uploaded or served by Google Fonts) for them to render correctly.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming the banner ad works without filling all fields.
antiPatterns.reason: If you enable the single post banner but fail to fill both the banner image URL and destination URL, the ad will not display. Ensure both are provided.

antiPatterns.pattern: Code not appearing on site
antiPatterns.reason: Always check that the corresponding 'Enable' toggle is turned on and clear all caches (including plugin caches) after adding code.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring Featured Images for thumbnails.
antiPatterns.reason: If thumbnails are enabled but not appearing, ensure posts have a Featured Image set. If you intend to use the first image in the post content instead of a Featured Image, enable 'Grab the first post image' in General Settings.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming navigation settings apply everywhere.
antiPatterns.reason: If using the Theme Builder with a custom header template, navigation settings may be overridden by your Theme Builder configuration. Clear caching plugins and browser cache if changes don't appear on the front end.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming custom titles appear when enabled.
antiPatterns.reason: If custom titles are enabled but not appearing, ensure you have created the correct custom field on your post. The custom field Name must exactly match the value specified in the 'Custom field Name to be used for title' setting.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring authentication requirements
antiPatterns.reason: To receive product updates and access features like version rollback, you must authenticate your Elegant Themes subscription by correctly entering both the Username and API Key. Failure to do so will prevent updates.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming ACF fields are visible without enabling looping.
antiPatterns.reason: ACF data must be explicitly pulled into the loop using the Dynamic Content settings and selecting 'Loop Post Custom Field' (or setting the Query Type for repeaters).

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming all Divi 4 features work in Divi 5.
antiPatterns.reason: Features like **Quick Action** and **Split Testing** have been deprecated. Check documentation for compatibility details.

antiPatterns.pattern: Ignoring the orange warning indicator during migration.
antiPatterns.reason: The indicator signals that a page is running in backward compatibility mode due to unconverted Divi 4 modules, which may cause reduced performance.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming custom CSS will work without checking scope.
antiPatterns.reason: CSS must be placed in the correct location to affect the desired element (e.g., using `selector.` for single elements, or global settings for site-wide rules).

antiPatterns.pattern: Relying on cached versions of the page.
antiPatterns.reason: CSS changes will not appear if any layer (Divi cache, plugin cache, browser cache, server CDN) is active. Always clear all caches when debugging CSS.

antiPatterns.pattern: Disabling global on an element used across multiple pages.
antiPatterns.reason: Other instances will no longer receive updates. Ensure you understand the impact before converting.

antiPatterns.pattern: Assuming automatic reconnection after disabling global.
antiPatterns.reason: The element is disconnected from the library version. To reconnect, manually 'Save to Library' and check 'Save as Global', which creates a new library entry.

antiPatterns.pattern: Search results show default WordPress style.
antiPatterns.reason: Ensure the Search Results template is created in Theme Builder and verify **Divi** → **Theme Options** → **Builder** → **Post Type Integration**. Also, clear browser cache and confirm Visual Builder is enabled for the post type.

antiPatterns.pattern: Blog module shows all posts instead of search results.
antiPatterns.reason: Open the Blog module settings, go to the **Content** tab, and explicitly enable the **Posts For Current Page** option.

antiPatterns.pattern: Dynamic Content icon is missing for Post/Archive Title.
antiPatterns.reason: Ensure you are using Divi 5.0 or later, and try using the Heading module instead of a Text module. Clear cache if issues persist.

antiPatterns.pattern: Pagination does not work on search results.
antiPatterns.reason: Open the Blog module settings and ensure **Show Pagination** is enabled in the Content tab. Set the desired pagination type (standard, load more, infinite scroll).

antiPatterns.pattern: Template fails to trigger for certain searches.
antiPatterns.reason: WordPress may not trigger search templates for empty or very broad queries; test with a clear, specific search term.

antiPatterns.pattern: Setting the Section or Row background to a color.
antiPatterns.reason: The Ken Burns effect only applies when the section or row uses a background image. Always ensure a background image is set for the effect to work.

antiPatterns.pattern: Posts not showing on archive pages
antiPatterns.reason: Verify that you selected 'All Archive Pages' as the template type, ensure the Blog module has 'Posts For Current Page' enabled in the Content Tab, and confirm posts exist in relevant archives.

antiPatterns.pattern: Broken grid layout
antiPatterns.reason: Check column counts; very high numbers on narrow screens can cause issues. Also verify theme container width settings using Theme Customizer and test responsiveness (mobile/tablet).

antiPatterns.pattern: Pagination not working
antiPatterns.reason: Confirm pagination is enabled in the Blog module's Content Tab, set a reasonable post count per page, and ensure enough posts exist to create multiple pages.

antiPatterns.pattern: Dynamic content title shows placeholder text
antiPatterns.reason: Ensure you used the Dynamic Content icon (lightning bolt) and selected 'Post/Archive Title'. Verify the template type is set correctly and that viewing occurs on the front end, not in the builder.

antiPatterns.pattern: Reporting known issues
antiPatterns.reason: Before submitting a bug report, ensure you have updated to the latest Divi version, tested in Safe Mode (Divi > Support Center > Safe Mode) to rule out plugin conflicts, checked the Elegant Themes help center for known fixes, and cleared all caches while testing in an incognito window.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using code snippets to enable SVG/JSON uploads without sanitization.
antiPatterns.reason: The `upload_mimes` filter method does not sanitize uploaded files, creating a security risk. Only upload these file types from completely trusted sources.
